| <a id="h002"></a>H002 | Run one scripted agent turn from a pipe and get a machine-readable cost report | copy | Echivalent | Reevaluat | H002 whole-contract review: \`nerva chat -z\` preserves final-answer-only stdout, bounded piped/file/argument input, nonzero refusal/failure/usage/auth/unreachable/interrupt exits, confirmed versus requested session attribution, and an atomic nerva.chat.usage.v1 receipt on ordinary success and failure paths. It never approves a queued action; pending IDs remain queued and force an incomplete result. Interactive output/exit compatibility remains while its optional receipt can report incomplete. The hub supplies request-owned bounded generation usage on JSON chat replies and SSE end events. Accepted owned generation dispatch attempts are observed after quota, physical data-handling and host/protocol checks. Task8 admitted native requests now account once at the signed leased physical transport after those checks, with post-entry failure/cancellation recorded as possibly sent (agents/core/llm/providers/native_transport.py:210-257). Retries, specialists, synchronous response-driving auxiliary generation, streaming and synthesis are included; control probes, embeddings/audio and explicitly detached title/review/cache jobs are excluded. Task-owned pending attempts prevent cross-task usage attribution; nested scopes preserve provenance, inactive inherited scopes cannot authenticate a model, unknown POSTs during generation make totals unknown, and closed/bounded collectors reject late or overflowing observations. Tokens require complete valid provider counters for every attempt; failed/partial retries cannot hide behind later success. Local zero needs positive provider/route/host proof and complete counters. Exact requested models confirmed against the wire can use dated repository estimates; unsupported cache-write premiums, Gemini Pro long-context tiers, unknown models and uncertain provenance stay unpriced. Mixed identities receive a bounded breakdown. The provider field denotes the backend adapter, not an attestation of remote weights or an invoice. Source-assigned runtime stops survive synthesis independently of prose: settled tool-loop exits, exact thinking exhaustion, terminal agent failures/timeouts, policy/continuation refusal and terminal synthesis errors make one-shot execution incomplete. Stop metadata is finite and bounded; malformed present metadata fails closed. Legacy hubs retain text-fallback limits. Successful deterministic synthesis fallback may still return complete specialist answers; a failed observed attempt keeps its usage unknown. Authorization and early owner/session preflight errors retain their HTTP failure codes and can yield unavailable telemetry while still producing a failure receipt. CLI validators reject malformed, missing, negative, boolean, nonfinite, oversized or inconsistent telemetry without crashing or changing the answer verdict; error objects carry only bounded projected telemetry. Verification includes real owned HTTP MockTransport calls through actual backend adapters, actual ASGI JSON/SSE, concurrent/nested/late task behavior, runtime-stop to synthesis to HTTP to CLI, malformed receipts, pending approvals, transport failures, real isolated FastAPI lifespan/CLI smoke and the frozen backend milestone with its explicitly recorded outcome. No live-provider, native Windows/device or invoice claim is made. Unrelated Hermes flags, invocation IDs and writing through a symlink are outside the frozen acceptance; the atomic replace behavior is retained. Interrupt review and regressions verify exit 130 before POST and after decoded response/output, preserving observed session, usage, stops and pending IDs; already emitted terminal text cannot be retracted. The full frozen run was not green (32 failed cases); all 32 original nodes pass after fixture/status repairs, and the isolated interrupt fix passes integrated CLI coverage. | <a id="h006"></a>H006 | Read and change configuration without an editor, and validate/migrate it | update | Echivalent | Reevaluat | \`nerva config\` now has nine actions: list, get, set, unset, check, edit, path, env-path and migrate (agents/cli/nerva.py:268-280 declares the four new ones, the dispatch is agents/cli/nerva.py:1329-1336, and tests/test_nerva_cli.py:105 pins the tree). The first five behave as before: list/get/set/unset take dotted or escaped names that reach into a JSON value, and \`check\` validates every stored value against its declared schema (agents/cli/nerva.py:1337-1349). Every verb is offline, on the same data root and settings store the hub uses. \`config edit\` opens every editable setting in $VISUAL, then $EDITOR, then vi (notepad on Windows) as one \`category.key = JSON\` file in the \`config list\` format (agents/cli/nerva.py:1448-1463, agents/cli/nerva.py:1473-1494). The file is created owner-only and deleted afterwards. A secret, a route-only row and an undeclared row are named in a comment and their value is never written to it. After the editor exits 0, only lines whose value differs from the stored one are written. Each goes through the same schema validation and the same guarded write as \`config set\`: the retention approval, the model-selection guards and the busy-store message (agents/cli/nerva.py:1361-1422, agents/cli/nerva.py:1525-1601). A bad line (not JSON, duplicated, unknown, secret, route-only, schema-refused) is named and the rest is still written, with exit 1. A missing editor, a non-executable editor or a nonzero editor exit writes nothing. Tests: tests/test_nerva_cli.py:569-592 (only changed lines written, temp file removed), tests/test_nerva_cli.py:595-612 (no change, failed editor, $VISUAL over $EDITOR), tests/test_nerva_cli.py:615-630 (partial acceptance with every rejection named), tests/test_nerva_cli.py:633-651 (secrets never shown or written), tests/test_nerva_cli.py:654-659 (route-only), tests/test_nerva_cli.py:662-667 (non-executable editor), tests/test_nerva_cli.py:670-676 (Windows argv). \`config path\` prints the profile, its data root and the settings database, with a row count read read-only without creating or seeding anything, and \`--json\` (agents/cli/nerva.py:1604-1641; tests/test_nerva_cli.py:713-729, including a \`-p\` profile). \`config env-path\` lists the repo, data-home and profile \`.env\` files in the order the hub reads them, whether each is present and read, the \`.env.example\` and the secret store, and whether dotenv is disabled. It prints names and presence only, never a value (agents/cli/nerva.py:1644-1697; tests/test_nerva_cli.py:732-762). \`config migrate \[--dry-run\] \[--json\]\` is the "missing or outdated keys" report plus the write. agents/core/settings_migrate.py reads the raw store read-only and plans three kinds of change: a \`seed\` for each declared setting the store lacks, a \`default\` for a shipped default a later build changed (applied only while the stored value is still the old default and the change has not already been applied), and a \`retired\` rewrite of a model id that a vendor retired, on every model setting rather than only the row that shipped it. Skill-switch rows are listed as \`kept\`, never reseeded (agents/core/settings_migrate.py:134-170). \`apply\` writes exactly that plan in one transaction, each statement guarded so a value the owner changed since the plan is left alone, records the default markers, and notifies a running hub (agents/core/settings_migrate.py:173-225). The \`migrate\` verb prints one line per change, writes nothing under \`--dry-run\`, and with no store says it would create one with all declared settings or creates it (agents/core/settings_migrate.py:228-234; agents/cli/nerva.py:1712-1767). A locked store gives a named retry message, and a file that is not a settings store gives a named failure. Tests: tests/test_settings_db_migrate.py:95-123 (plan names a seed, a changed default and retired ids and writes nothing), tests/test_settings_db_migrate.py:126-133 (owner values left alone), tests/test_settings_db_migrate.py:136-146 (kept switch rows), tests/test_settings_db_migrate.py:152-196 (apply writes exactly the plan, records the marker, works on a store with no migrations table), and tests/test_nerva_cli.py:679-693, tests/test_nerva_cli.py:696-710, tests/test_nerva_cli.py:765-806 and tests/test_nerva_cli.py:809-820 (busy store, rewrite, dry-run then apply then idempotent, create-only-when-applied). The retired-model table is data and is Anthropic-only. It has four rows, each naming the repo file that records the retirement, and a test checks that file holds the retired id and date (agents/core/settings_migrate.py:58-67; tests/test_settings_db_migrate.py:51-73, tests/test_settings_db_migrate.py:218-220). The model settings it scans are claude_model, default_model, gemini_model, compatible_model and the sub-agent model (agents/core/settings_migrate.py:71-77). Nothing in the repo records a retired xAI, OpenAI, Google or OpenRouter id, so none is listed and none is taken from memory. The mechanism is the same one \`hermes migrate xai\` is: tests/test_settings_db_migrate.py:199-215 shows that a row supplied for an xAI id rewrites llm.compatible_model and leaves an unlisted id alone. Hermes's own vendor-specific retired-model list is data that Nerva does not carry. \`config check\` validates stored values against their schema, and the report of missing keys, changed defaults and retired ids is \`config migrate --dry-run\`. A boot still applies seeds and changed defaults silently, but the retired-model rewrite across every model setting runs only when the owner runs \`nerva config migrate\`. Nothing here was run against a live provider. | <a id="h009"></a>H009 | Produce a pasteable, non-sensitive diagnostic report for a support thread | keep | Echivalent | Reevaluat | Implemented 2026-10-20 on PR #1249, revised after an adversarial review. Hermes' \`debug dump\`/\`debug share --local\` report: version and commit, active model/provider, which API keys and platform tokens are set, non-default config, and redacted log tails. build_bundle (agents/core/support_bundle.py:293) now carries all of it, still allow-listed. \`meta\` adds the checked-out commit, read from .git without running git (agents/core/support_bundle.py:92). \`model\` (agents/core/support_bundle.py:196) names the selected backend, the default/Gemini/Claude/compatible model ids, compatible provider, cloud fallback and reasoning effort (agents/core/support_bundle.py:44). It leaves out base URLs. The product posture is read from the hub's runtime settings, or the stored rows offline (agents/core/support_bundle.py:120). Every shown value passes _shown_value (agents/core/support_bundle.py:69), which does not trust a row's declared kind, because a write does not check it. A select value must be one of its declared options. A number or toggle must be one. A model id (the free-text rows at agents/core/support_bundle.py:48) must have a model id's shape (no \`@\`, so neither \`user:pw@host\` nor an e-mail passes), no scheme, no JWT prefix and nothing the settings credential scanner flags. Anything else reads \`(withheld)\`. \`credentials\` (agents/core/support_bundle.py:210) reports, by variable name only, which provider keys are set: each profile's auth_env, plus the \*_API_KEYS pool only for providers that actually pool (provider_probe.POOLED). It also covers tool, platform and hub credentials Nerva reads (agents/core/support_bundle.py:55). \`overrides\` (agents/core/support_bundle.py:230) lists stored settings whose source is not \`default\` (set, undeclared, unreadable), through the same filter. \`logs\` (agents/core/support_bundle.py:254) adds the newest WARNING+ hub log records, up to 500. They go through the HUD log reader and its secret redactor, and e-mail addresses are masked as Hermes masks them. Logs are opt-in (\`--logs N\`, route \`?log_lines=N\` at agents/core/routers/support.py:23) rather than default-on. They are the only section that can carry message text, so a default bundle stays aggregates-only; the text report says how to add them. render_text (agents/core/support_bundle.py:316) prints the pasteable report. \`nerva support bundle\` (agents/cli/nerva.py:206, agents/cli/nerva.py:823) reads the hub's admin GET /api/support/bundle (agents/core/routers/support.py:21; agents/cli/nerva.py:840). It offers \`--offline\` (build from the data root when the hub is down), \`--json\`, \`--logs N\` (agents/cli/nerva.py:214) and \`--out FILE\`, written owner-only 0600 even over an existing wider file (agents/cli/nerva.py:850). | <a id="h010"></a>H010 | Back up and restore the whole install | keep | Echivalent | Reevaluat | Final review at HEAD 6d341cd on codex/hermes-progress-20261010. The row's code is commits 8e6af8c through 846d8f4, plus the regenerated sweep and schema in dd922d1 and the integration follow-up 6d341cd. The integration follow-up moved the binding-inventory lines and made sd_notify read the restart marker with env_flag (agents/core/sd_notify.py:270-273). The earlier assessment listed three gaps against Hermes \`backup\` / \`backup --quick\` / \`import\`. All three are closed on this branch: 1. Quick state-only snapshot. create_backup(quick=True) keeps only the state databases (agents/core/backup.py:573-574). The \`nerva backup create --quick\` verb is defined at agents/cli/nerva.py:329-331, and the module CLI has the same flag (agents/core/backup.py:1753). 2. Restore is no longer limited to the module CLI. - The \`nerva backup\` tree has create, list, verify, restore and cancel (agents/cli/nerva.py:327-349; dispatch in cmd_backup at agents/cli/nerva.py:2254). - The admin route POST /api/admin/backup/restore queues a backup.restore card at the irreversible tier and answers 202. It never restores on the request alone (agents/core/routers/backup.py:98-137). DELETE withdraws a staged restore (agents/core/routers/backup.py:160-175). - With a hub running, \`nerva backup restore\` posts to that route (agents/cli/nerva.py:2348). With no hub running, the owner must type RESTORE; the restore is then staged and applied in place (agents/cli/nerva.py:2375-2392). - An accepted card is routed to backup.apply_approved (agents/core/autonomy/irreversible.py:45). Only a process that can restart the hub may take it (agents/core/autonomy/irreversible.py:51, agents/core/backup.py:1624-1643). 3. The server no longer has to be stopped by hand. - apply_approved stages the restore and asks the hub to restart (agents/core/backup.py:1673-1713). - serve.py applies the staged restore at boot, before agents.web opens any store (serve.py:113-131). - run_server installs a stopper and then re-execs (POSIX), exits 75 for NSSM, or spawns a successor (interactive Windows) (serve.py:416-426, serve.py:482-509). - When the hub has no restart path, it says "manual" everywhere instead of promising a restart (agents/core/routers/backup.py:140-144, agents/core/backup.py:1702-1712). - Each restore first takes a rollback snapshot of the matching kind (agents/core/backup.py:1562-1566). What review round 7 added: - GET /api/admin/backup now also reports restart, stage_within_seconds and refused_restore (agents/core/routers/backup.py:47-52). The tick comes from a single helper that the coordinator loop also sleeps on (agents/core/autonomy_coordinator.py:154-158, agents/core/autonomy_coordinator.py:573). - \`nerva approvals accept\` says at once whether the restore is "NOT applied yet" or will be applied by a self-restart (agents/cli/nerva.py:2059-2074). It then follows for 8 s and reports a stage, an outcome or a refusal (agents/cli/nerva.py:2077-2121). - A refused apply is now recorded and listed (agents/core/backup.py:1646-1671; agents/cli/nerva.py:2302-2306). Review history: the row passed seven fix rounds (r1–r7) and two adversarial skeptics, and was then cherry-picked onto this branch. Honest limits: - The Windows restart paths (NSSM exit 75, spawned successor) are tested only through simulation. - The environment a frozen PyInstaller build hands to its successor is not exercised. - The HUD Backup panel still offers only back-up, restore-drill and export; it has no quick or restore button (frontend/src/gap.tsx:3642). POST /api/admin/backup takes no quick flag (agents/core/routers/backup.py:65). Hermes has no HUD, so this does not affect parity. - The frontend vitest suite was not run in this review. | <a id="h014"></a>H014 | Uninstall cleanly, with a dry run | keep | Echivalent | Reevaluat | At HEAD d2ec765, all three gaps in the 2026-10-14 assessment are closed in code. (1) Dry run. --dry-run is a real CLI path. With it, _main prints plan_uninstall as JSON and removes nothing (agents/core/uninstall.py:719-728). The plan lists every target and whether it exists. It also shows the data root and purge feasibility when --purge-data is given, and the desktop paths when --gui or --gui-only is given (agents/core/uninstall.py:370-402). The dry run is reachable from all three entry points: uninstall.sh --dry-run (uninstall.sh:69-70, 87-91), UNINSTALL.bat /DRYRUN (UNINSTALL.bat:108-113) and \`nerva uninstall --dry-run\` (agents/cli/nerva.py:699-700, 3762-3774). Without --confirm, the CLI still refuses with exit 2 (agents/core/uninstall.py:730-732). (2) Typed confirmation. --purge-data is no longer a bare flag. _confirm_purge (agents/core/uninstall.py:581-617) works in two ways. Interactively, the user must type back the data root's folder name; a mismatch cancels and removes nothing. Without a terminal, --yes-purge must give the data root's exact absolute path. A relative path or the bare folder name is refused, because it would match on every machine (agents/core/uninstall.py:568-579). --yes-purge without --purge-data is refused (agents/core/uninstall.py:715-717). Purge feasibility is checked before the prompt (agents/core/uninstall.py:739-762). The purge runs before any software is removed, so a failed purge leaves the install intact. (3) Desktop app removal. --gui also removes the Tauri desktop shell, and --gui-only removes only the shell. desktop_app_targets covers macOS, Windows and Linux, plus the cargo output of a source build (agents/core/uninstall.py:119-202). _remove_desktop (agents/core/uninstall.py:429-475) handles each kind of install: - NSIS installs run their own uninstall.exe in place. - Copies owned by a package manager are reported with the command that removes them, not deleted. - A path is reported removed only once it is gone. --gui-summary is a read-only JSON probe (agents/core/uninstall.py:227-249). The flags are wired in uninstall.sh:28-30, 75-76, in UNINSTALL.bat:44-46, 58 and in agents/cli/nerva.py:707-711. Latest change (the regression both skeptics found): with no system Python on Windows, UNINSTALL.bat runs from .venv. That fallback, and only that one, now passes --allow-locked-venv (UNINSTALL.bat:87-96, 111, 117). The module then removes every other target and leaves .venv in place. It lists .venv under not_removed with venv_left_behind and exits 1 (agents/core/uninstall.py:529-539, 662-665, 745-749). Before, it refused and pointed the user back at the same script. \`nerva uninstall\` does not expose the flag (agents/cli/nerva.py:4848-4851). The implementer reports that the new tests failed before the fix (6 failed) and passed after. Both skeptic reviews passed. Limits that still apply: - On Windows, \`nerva uninstall\` (which runs inside .venv) still refuses to remove the software and points to UNINSTALL.bat (agents/core/uninstall.py:303-307, 746-748). Only the dry run and --gui-only work there. - In the bat's no-system-Python fallback, .venv must be deleted by hand. - --purge-data erases only the data root. The user-home entries it leaves are listed by kept_after_purge. - Hermes' --yes maps to --confirm here, and its --full maps to --purge-data. Tests: tests/test_uninstall.py passed 83/83 on two separate runs (not flaky). Together, tests/test_uninstall.py and tests/test_nerva_cli.py gave 189 passed. | <a id="h015"></a>H015 | Create and manage scheduled jobs, and see why past runs failed | update | Echivalent | Reevaluat | Whole frozen H015 contract reviewed, batch 06 (2026-10-10). CLI/API support list/create/edit/pause/resume/run/remove/status/tick, durable runs, incidents, independent KV notes and read-only doctor. List provides global scheduler status; status provides job/request outcomes. A completed one-shot rearms through edit to a distinct future time and may then run immediately under the same gate/reservation. Direct actions reserve one pending run before execution and finish that row atomically with counters/output and any failure incident. Cancellation/orphan recovery yields unknown without replay, only while the execution gate proves no cooperating executor is live. Scripts reserve one one-shot/repeat slot in their own CAS transaction, freeze input notes and reconcile once. Deleted configuration cannot deliver a later model result; history and acknowledged incidents survive reopening. Terminal history is bounded at 200 rows/job and 10,000 globally with active references protected. Incidents group normalized redacted failures by job/signature, expose numeric IDs and detected/closed state, acknowledge idempotently, preserve the three-failure pause and never invent an alerted transition. Closed matching signatures remain closed. Diagnostic redaction covers known environment/settings/catalogue secrets before cuts and fails closed. Notes are separate from previous model output: 128 printable characters/key, 16 KiB/value, 64 KiB/job and 256 keys, enforced transactionally. Continuity defaults on; disabling omits previous output but keeps KV and saves the latest bounded output. Both enter shared direct/script asks as JSON-escaped fenced untrusted data. Additive continuity edits merge atomically without replacing other options. Detailed model failures become failed attempts before delivery; legitimate queued-approval answers and silent suppression retain their meanings. Existing script/URL monitors skip the model when unchanged. Native no_agent executes a bounded approved Python command rather than introducing a shell. Scripts need fresh risk-3 ASK per attempt; URL hops remain plugin.egress. Task jobs preserve kind, payload, risk floor and host-bound inbound:job identity through the live governed worker as ASK, with no raw-queue fallback or standing grant. Existing action gates remain on direct ask/delivery paths. All five new routes are admin guarded. Core 476/476, surface 137 passed/3 unavailable-Fish skips, 43 route/doctor guards and actual disposable lifespan CLI smoke passed. Full backend milestone is separately required before assessment update. H451 watchdog/recovery, H452 classifier/alerting/preflight, H454 cross-job context and new dedicated HUD/mobile controls remain separate. No live-provider/native-host claim. | <a id="h039"></a>H039 | Subscribe an external system's events to the agent via a webhook | keep | Echivalent | Reevaluat | Inbound webhook subscriptions are real and owner-managed. The admin-only routes list, create, patch and delete hooks, and a delivery posts to POST /api/webhooks/{id} with a token or an HMAC-signed body, a deliver-only mode that skips the agent, an event allow-list, a prompt template and a receiver switch that refuses everything when off (agents/core/routers/webhooks.py:674-748, agents/core/routers/webhooks.py:111-133). The three items the row still listed are now built. (1) A signed test action. The store builds a sample delivery for a hook (its first subscribed event or the one given, a small payload that says it is a test or the owner's own object) and signs it the way a sender must, as the HMAC of the raw body or the token header (agents/core/webhooks.py:936-965). POST /api/webhooks/{hook_id}/test is admin-only; it verifies that sample with the receiver's own signature or token check, reads the receiver switch and the hook's switch, runs the same event, filter and prompt-template classification as a real delivery, and answers a report with the outcome (run, deliver_only, skipped, filtered or refused), the HTTP status a sender would see, the reason, the text the target would get and the sample with its credential masked (agents/core/routers/webhooks.py:308-359, agents/core/routers/webhooks.py:640-671, agents/core/routers/webhooks.py:167-184). It is dry: no turn runs, nothing is pushed, no call, skip or filter is counted, and only a last_test note and an audit row are written. (2) A declarative payload filter instead of the refused --script hook. A hook carries up to 16 rules {path, op, value}, all of which must hold; the ops are eq, ne, contains, startswith, endswith, glob (at most one \*), in, exists and missing, each linear in what it reads, with no regex and no owner code run over the attacker-controlled payload (agents/core/webhooks.py:264, agents/core/webhooks.py:277-326, agents/core/webhooks.py:364-420). It is set on create and by PATCH, checked after the event list and before the template, and a delivery a rule turns away is answered 202, never run, and counted as filtered with the rule and the echoed value kept on the hook for the admin (agents/core/routers/webhooks.py:102-108, agents/core/routers/webhooks.py:124, agents/core/routers/webhooks.py:146, agents/core/routers/webhooks.py:627-633, agents/core/routers/webhooks.py:792-796, agents/core/webhooks.py:916-924). A stored filter that is not valid, including a rule from the first build with the removed regex op matches, reads as unreadable and filters every delivery (fail closed) until it is rewritten (agents/core/webhooks.py:821-828). (3) The CLI verbs. nerva webhook subscribe\|list\|remove\|test ride the same admin routes: subscribe takes the target, type, name, --signed, --events, --prompt, --deliver, --deliver-only, --description and a JSON --filter and prints the hook URL and the token or signing secret once; list shows credential kind, switch, destination, events, filter rule count (or unreadable) and calls; remove deletes; test sends the signed dry sample with --event and --payload and prints the outcome (agents/cli/nerva.py:448-480, agents/cli/nerva.py:2990-3011, agents/cli/nerva.py:3014-3112). The HUD Webhooks panel has a test button that shows the report, a filter editor in each hook's detail pane, a filter box in the create form, a rule-count tag, the filtered count with the last rule that turned a delivery away, and an unreadable-filter warning that never clears the stored filter unless the owner edits it (frontend/src/panels/webhooks.tsx:96-112, frontend/src/panels/webhooks.tsx:127-145, frontend/src/panels/webhooks.tsx:194-205, frontend/src/panels/webhooks.tsx:331-339, frontend/src/panels/webhooks.tsx:424-445, frontend/src/panels/webhooks.tsx:542-547, frontend/src/panels/webhooks.tsx:579-583, frontend/src/panels/webhooks.tsx:590-595). Pinned by tests: every filter op and the verdict text, rule validation, the removed regex op and fail-closed stored rules, an adversarial-subject timing check, filtered deliveries not retried under an Idempotency-Key, the sample being verified by the receiver, the dry admin-only test route with filtered, skipped and refused outcomes, the CLI verbs round-tripped through the real route handlers, the command tree, and the HUD test button, filter editor and unreadable-filter behaviour (tests/test_h153_webhook_subscriptions.py:443-485, tests/test_h153_webhook_subscriptions.py:499-528, tests/test_h153_webhook_subscriptions.py:554-569, tests/test_h153_webhook_subscriptions.py:581-588, tests/test_h153_webhook_subscriptions.py:607-621, tests/test_h153_webhook_subscriptions.py:654-664, tests/test_h153_webhook_subscriptions.py:686-701, tests/test_h153_webhook_subscriptions.py:704-724, tests/test_h153_webhook_subscriptions.py:727-738, tests/test_h153_webhook_subscriptions.py:741-755, tests/test_h153_webhook_subscriptions.py:758-765, tests/test_h153_webhook_subscriptions.py:843-845, tests/test_h153_webhook_subscriptions.py:848-941, tests/test_nerva_cli.py:88-94, frontend/src/test/webhooks-panel.test.tsx:808-924, frontend/src/test/webhooks-panel.test.tsx:928-1019). Honest limits: the filter only accepts or turns away a delivery, it cannot rewrite the payload (the Hermes --script transform is deliberately not copied, because it would run owner code over untrusted input); the test is dry and in-process, unlike a Hermes test POST that really runs the agent, so it proves the sender's signing recipe and the hook's routing, not network reachability, a proxy or a real third-party sender; the CLI tests drive the route handlers through a stand-in client rather than real HTTP, and no live external sender or hardware is claimed. Re-read 2026-10-24 (batch 4): added the signed dry test route, the linear-time declarative payload filter with its fail-closed storage, the nerva webhook subscribe\|list\|remove\|test verbs and the HUD test button and filter editors. Re-read 2026-10-25 after the Codex review fixes (embedded globstar, skills verify --json exit). | <a id="h042"></a>H042 | Start, check and stop the web UI / headless backend | update | Parțial | Reevaluat | Hermes's row is start, check \*\*and stop\*\*, and the stop half is entirely absent: no \`stop\` verb, no pidfile, no ready file. The row cites \`hermes dashboard --status/--stop\` plus backend ready sentinels and a ready file (06-cli-f.md, 16 entries); Nerva has \`nerva status\`, which reads the HTTP surface and so cannot report a hub that is starting or wedged before the port opens, and Ctrl-C. Hermes also signals the conflict as a machine-readable \`BACKEND_PORT_IN_USE\`, where this slice signals it as an exit code and an English sentence — enough for a supervisor, not enough for a caller parsing a status stream. Not delivered either: \`--isolated\`, \`--skip-build\`, \`--no-open\`, the SSH session-token file and owner-nonce, or the interactive auth-setup prompt. \*\*One known limit, in the safe direction:\*\* the probe picks a single address family from the host string while uvicorn binds every address \`getaddrinfo\` returns, so a dual-stack name like \`localhost\` is probed on v4 only and can miss a conflict held on the v6 address — it misses silently, and uvicorn then reports it exactly as it does today. The Windows half of the \`SO_REUSEADDR\` choice is read off asyncio's \`reuse_address = os.name == "posix"\` line and has never been executed here; that test skips off POSIX and the docstring says so. The bind guard (\`assert_safe_bind\`) stays fail-closed and no flag may widen it. [d1](../serve.py) [d2](../tests/test_h2311_operability.py) [d3](../docs/test-manual/01-environment-and-boot.md) |

(1) Memory and user-profile cost are not components; the report lists personas, identity, host-detected, environment-hint, tools, skills index, skills loaded and scaffold only. (5) Not verified against a real service: no request was sent, so the figures are estimates comparable with the internal budget, not a provider's count. H154 added the bulk clear-pending: the store method is at agents/core/channels/pairing.py:669, and the admin-guarded POST /api/channels/pairing/clear-pending is at agents/core/routers/pairing.py:115-131. The store writes ALLOWED = "allowed" (agents/core/channels/pairing.py:95). Reject removes only a pending record (agents/core/channels/pairing.py:642-650). The SENDER PAIRING card now uses senderApproved, which accepts 'allowed' and the older 'paired' (frontend/src/gap.tsx:668). The only compare-and-set is the checkpoint-clock commit of a compaction (agents/core/orchestrator.py:5228), and it guards a summary, not turn ownership; the H063 route generations in channels/session_lifecycle.py fence which session a channel route resolves to after a reset, not whether a running turn still owns its session. There is no active-session slot claimed before the first await and no \`max_concurrent_sessions\` cap: turns on different sessions run concurrently without bound (tests/test_turn_lease.py:88). No watchdog evicts a session whose turn is wedged: its lease stays held until the turn ends, and later messages only get the busy reply. There is no eviction of an in-memory slot whose durable routing row ended, and no single per-session \`SessionState\` object with explicit lifetimes. There is no per-session warm agent cache and no memory-pressure eviction. Agents are process-wide: every session shares \`orchestrator.agents\`, which the compaction-boundary persona refresh walks as a whole (agents/core/orchestrator.py:492). Slack and Discord replies are not streamed: both descriptors declare \`supports_edit\`, but \`_begin_channel_draft\` refuses them because the row's governance clause requires one edit stream to be a single \`channel.reply\` approval decision and no such contract exists yet; until it does, their replies arrive whole after approval. The Matrix adapter (\`MatrixChannel\`, a webhook channel), another edit-capable platform the rationale names, posts whole \`m.room.message\` events: its descriptor does not declare \`supports_edit\` and it has no edit (\`m.replace\`) or draft path. | <a id="h117"></a>H117 | Message batching and debounce (treat a burst as one turn) | copy | Echivalent | Reevaluat | Message batching remains per (chat, sender), in arrival order, with the existing 0.35-second rolling window, 1-second cap and 32-part bound (agents/core/channels/batching.py:45-47). Telegram keys the batch by (chat, sender) and, inside a forum topic, also by the topic id (agents/core/channels/telegram.py:1308-1310); Discord keys by (channel, author) (agents/core/channels/discord.py:156) and Slack by (channel, member, thread) (agents/core/channels/slack.py:649-650). Ordinary Telegram callbacks flush held batches and enter the chat lane; ordinary messages, attachment descriptions, command and reason ordering and merged-text injection scanning retain their existing paths: a command flushes what was held and is delivered alone (agents/core/channels/telegram.py:1311-1316), and the Gateway scans the merged turn normalised (agents/core/channels/gateway.py:281-284). Reserved autc reusable-consent callbacks are an explicit exception: they intercept before the normal batch flush. A registered current callback uses a separate bounded 32-task lane to release its waiting owner/model turn; stale, malformed, replayed, unregistered or overflowing reserved callbacks refuse promptly without entering the occupied ordinary lane. The existing live aut1 owner-once callback retains its separate post-flush lane. This is deliberate collateral behavior review with existing batching/reason/owner-once regressions, not a new batching feature or renewed mutation receipt. Batch collateral review (2026-10-04, base 9bfa085c): Native reusable-consent \`/deny\` is now a reserved direct reply to the delivered card. It dispatches outside the occupied chat lane and consumes stale or malformed \`/deny\` without forwarding it as a model turn. Ordinary batching, callback, command and reason paths retain their existing ordering. This is a scoped lane exception, not new batching equivalence or live Telegram proof. Owner-once denial collateral review (2026-10-04, base 22005244): an original current \`/deny \[reason\]\` reply to the delivered owner-once card is now another reserved pre-flush exception. Telegram selects exactly one current owner-once or reusable-consent registry, dispatches the selected reply outside the occupied ordinary chat lane, and consumes stale, ambiguous and malformed \`/deny\` without forwarding text to the model. The (chat, sender) batching window, cap, part bound and ordinary callback/command/reason paths are unchanged. The new native owner-once test exercises the occupied-lane reply and refusal paths; this preserves the prior batching verdict without a live Bot API or new mutation claim. Pending-input drift re-read (2026-10-11, PR #1249 head): the h067 pending-input work added two more reserved pre-batch exceptions and does not change the batching contract. (1) A \`h067:\` callback is dispatched on its own bounded 32-task lane before the consent/owner-once callback handling and before any batch flush (agents/core/channels/telegram.py:883-890); with no hook, a bad id or a full lane it is answered "Not applied." without entering the ordinary lane. (2) A fresh, directly authored, group-admitted text with no attachment that is not a claimed decision reason is first offered to the Gateway's pending handler (agents/core/channels/telegram.py:1046-1048; agents/core/channels/gateway.py:77-78 runs it ahead of the rate limit, pairing and the merged-text scan), and only a consumed clarification answer skips batching; anything not consumed continues down the unchanged reason/batch path. Discord offers original human messages the same way before the batch submit (agents/core/channels/discord.py:156). The held Telegram batch now carries session metadata, and coalescing keeps a pending_input_eligible=False mark sticky across the merged pieces (agents/core/channels/telegram.py:1317-1320). The topic-scoped key and the sticky mark are not exercised by the pinned regressions; the 0.35 s / 1.0 s / 32-part contract, the command and reason ordering, the Discord and Slack bursts and the shutdown discard are, and all 301 pinned tests pass at this head. Slack's wake coalescing moved into _enqueue_event_locked with the same effect, and the H677 test drift is warm-up fixtures plus the ephemeral-delete handle in the Telegram stop test, not batching. | <a id="h133"></a>H133 | Live status chrome (gateway state, sessions, model, data provenance) | keep | Echivalent | Reevaluat | Final review at HEAD 57ed6db. The three gaps from the 2026-10-14 assessment were that the chrome did not show the messaging gateway, had no active-sessions count and had no version badge. All three are now closed on this branch. Backend. /status (agents/core/routers/status.py:111) now returns three more things: - "version" (agents/core/routers/status.py:125). - A "gateway" summary (agents/core/routers/status.py:141). It is built by _gateway_state (agents/core/routers/status.py:65-70): "running" with the sorted list of running channels, "stopped" when channels are registered but none runs, and "none" when no channel is registered. - A "sessions" block (agents/core/routers/status.py:142). It is built by _session_counts (agents/core/routers/status.py:73-85), which counts sessions active in the last 900 s (agents/core/routers/status.py:32). The count comes from CheckpointStore.active_session_count (agents/core/checkpoint.py:418-432), which returns None when the store is missing or fails. In that case the API reports state "unknown" instead of a guessed 0. Frontend. - The loader reads /status with readStatusChrome (frontend/src/api/loaders.ts:119). Malformed or missing fields become unknown (frontend/src/api/status-chrome.ts:24-36). - app.tsx stores this on the existing poll (frontend/src/app.tsx:614). The poll runs every 30 s (frontend/src/app.tsx:630) and passes the data to TopBar and Rail (frontend/src/app.tsx:676, frontend/src/app.tsx:682). - The top bar has a GATEWAY badge (frontend/src/shell.tsx:177). Its readout comes from gatewayView (frontend/src/shell.tsx:14-20). - The active-session count sits inside the GATEWAY badge (frontend/src/shell.tsx:149-151, frontend/src/shell.tsx:177). The badge title gives the count and the time window, and the count shows a dash when unknown. - The hub version is shown on the brand line (frontend/src/shell.tsx:169). - The collapsed rail has a gateway dot (frontend/src/shell.tsx:240-242). The badge strip now drops whole badges in a fixed priority order when space runs short (frontend/src/shell.tsx:32-49). GATEWAY carries data-keep 6 and is never dropped before LLM and DATA, so the session count stays on screen as long as GATEWAY does. The count is styled so it does not wrap (frontend/src/styles.css:126). The existing honesty chrome (DATA DEMO/OFFLINE/EMPTY/LIVE, EGRESS, MIC, LiveSourceChip) is still in place. Review history, briefly. Round 3 fixed the last skeptic finding: a separate SESSIONS badge had the lowest priority and was dropped at every laptop width from 1600 down. The count was merged into GATEWAY. The +N overflow-chip alternative was rejected as redundant, because GATEWAY is never dropped. A later unit test pins this: at the 3-badge width the visible badges are LLM, DATA and GATEWAY, and the count is still visible (frontend/src/test/status-chrome.test.tsx:161-175). The row passed two adversarial skeptics. Honest limits: - The poll runs every 30 s, where Hermes polls every 10 s. This is a cadence difference, not a missing capability. - The Playwright layout spec (frontend/e2e/status-chrome-layout.spec.ts:54-108) checks that the count is drawn and is the top element at its own centre, across viewport widths. It was not run here because no Playwright browsers are installed. The implementer reports it passing, and that it fails on the previous commit. - The pixel measurements in the implementer's summary come from a temporary probe that has been deleted. I did not re-check them. Test runs, done twice: - tests/test_status_router.py: 8 passed in both runs. - vitest on frontend/src/test/status-chrome.test.tsx plus frontend/src/test/live-source-chip.test.tsx: 20 passed (2 files) in both runs. | <a id="h154"></a>H154 | Approve or revoke who may talk to the agent (pairing) | keep | Echivalent | Reevaluat | This branch closes the missing bulk "clear pending" action, so the row is equivalent. Pairing works end to end. A stranger's request arrives through /api/channels/pairing/request (agents/core/routers/pairing.py:57). The owner lists senders (agents/core/routers/pairing.py:73) and approves, rejects, blocks or unpairs them (agents/core/routers/pairing.py:79), backed by SenderPairing.decide (agents/core/channels/pairing.py:694). The PairingPanel has per-row approve and block buttons, plus reject for a pending sender or unpair for an approved or blocked one (frontend/src/gap.tsx:701-707). Each sender is stored by channel and sender_id, kept as separate fields and joined by _key (agents/core/channels/pairing.py:351). Gap closed. SenderPairing.clear_pending (agents/core/channels/pairing.py:669-692) drops every pending request. It works from a snapshot and deletes each key safely, and it saves only when something was removed. Approved and blocked senders stay as they are, and a cleared sender can ask again. The flood counters are kept, so clearing does not reset rate limits. The admin-guarded POST /api/channels/pairing/clear-pending (agents/core/routers/pairing.py:115-131) calls it directly on the event loop (:128) and returns {ok, cleared, audited}. _audit_pairing (agents/core/routers/pairing.py:89-112) writes one SETTINGS_CHANGE audit row, action pairing_clear_pending, with the count only. It returns False when there is no audit log or the write fails. _serialize gives the JSON encoder shallow copies (agents/core/channels/pairing.py:387-396). On this branch the HUD button is a two-step ConfirmAction (frontend/src/gap.tsx:710-713). The panel shows "not audited" when the server could not write the audit row (frontend/src/gap.tsx:688-693). Tests. The store tests are tests/test_h12_19_pairing.py:229 and :247. The route tests are :266 (admin only), :277 (clears and audits with no sender ids), :296 (broken audit log still returns 200), :389 (no orchestrator gives audited False) and :400 (flood window kept). :355 checks that inserts from another thread do not break the clear. In vitest, frontend/src/test/pairing-deeplink.test.tsx:142 checks the two-step confirm and the X-Admin-Token header, :161 the "not audited" text and :170 that cancel sends nothing. Red first: before the review fixes, the thread, race and audited-key tests failed. The review fixes moved the clear onto the event loop, made the audit result honest, and added the copy-on-save. A test flake was found and fixed during integration: tests/test_h12_19_pairing.py:313 compared raw thread ids across two TestClient requests, which may use different portal threads. It now asserts that both writes ran with a running event loop, which a to_thread worker never has. Routing clear_pending through asyncio.to_thread makes it fail; it passed 6 of 6 runs alone. Results at HEAD: test_h12_19_pairing, test_channel_pairing, test_route_auth_matrix, test_route_parity_guard, test_openapi_parity_guard, test_route_tools_auth_parity, test_default_deny_front_door, test_pairing_secrets_at_rest, test_telegram_deeplink_pairing and test_telegram_pairing_shared_store: 146 passed. Vitest pairing-deeplink: 9 passed. Re-read 2026-10-21 (batch 2): H051 fixed how the PairingPanel reads statuses. The store writes ALLOWED = "allowed" (agents/core/channels/pairing.py:95), but the panel only treated 'paired' as approved, so an approved sender showed amber with an approve button and a reject button that does nothing for a non-pending record (SenderPairing.reject only drops a pending one, agents/core/channels/pairing.py:642-650). The panel now treats 'allowed' or 'paired' as approved (frontend/src/gap.tsx:668), colours it green, hides approve, and offers unpair instead of reject for any non-pending sender (frontend/src/gap.tsx:701-707); frontend/src/test/gap-panels.test.tsx:99 pins this. H051 also added \`nerva pairing list\|approve\|revoke\|clear-pending\` (agents/cli/nerva.py:428-447, handler at agents/cli/nerva.py:2906), which calls the same admin routes; clear-pending previews unless --confirm is given (agents/cli/nerva.py:2943-2950), tested in tests/test_nerva_cli_pairing.py:94 and tests/test_nerva_cli_pairing.py:171. | <a id="h156"></a>H156 | Edit an agent's persona and description from the UI | update | Echivalent | Reevaluat | An agent's persona can now be edited in the UI and is live on its next turn. That is Hermes' persona editor, over the version history Nerva already kept. Until now the history was a side record: a commit or rollback in the Prompts panel changed a JSON file while the agent kept its old persona. agents/core/soul_edit.py holds the one path an edit takes, apply_soul (:152). (1) Refusals. An agent the hub has not loaded is refused (404; agent_folder, :100, returns an enumerated folder name in the id alphabet, so no request value reaches a path). So is text over MAX_SOUL_BYTES (256 KiB of UTF-8, :40; 413), safe mode (:171; 409, because overlays are not read there, H275) and a persona the H387 guard would drop (:174; 422 with the verdict). guard_verdict (:60) runs the same scan and cap as Agent._load_soul, and GET /api/agents/{id}/soul now reports it through the same function. A line the guard only quarantines is applied, and the verdict names it. (2) Nothing live is lost. The first edit keeps the file on disk as v1 ("on disk before the first edit"). A file changed on disk since the last version, such as a hand edit, is kept as its own version ("on disk, changed outside the editor") before it is replaced (:185). An agent with no persona file has nothing to keep. (3) Written where the model reads it. The text goes to the owner's overlay (overlay_path, :115): souls/\<id\>/SOUL.local.md in the data home, else the repo-local SOUL.local.md, never the shipped SOUL.md. The write is atomic (_write_atomically, :126: temporary file, fsync, replace; a failure leaves no temporary file and records no new version). (4) Versioned, then live. The text is committed (:195; the same text twice is one version). The agent re-reads its persona (_load_soul, :197), and the result says whether the running agent now reads the written file. (5) Audited without the text. A SETTINGS_CHANGE row names the agent, the version and its hash. A plain commit and a history-only rollback are audited the same way (record_version, :224; agents/core/routers/admin.py:887, :860). Surfaces. PUT /api/admin/agents/{id}/soul {content, message} (agents/core/routers/agents_api.py:132, admin). POST /api/admin/prompts/{id}/rollback applies the version through the same path for a loaded agent (agents/core/routers/admin.py:928); the shared contract _identity (served from IDENTITY.local.md) and keys that are no loaded agent keep the history-only rollback. Description. A description: field in the SOUL front-matter is the agent's one-line description (description_of, :84, and description_in, :89: one line, at most 400 characters). It is listed on GET /agents and the SOUL read (agents/core/routers/agents_api.py:179, :124) and is never part of the prompt. POST /api/admin/agents/{id}/description/draft (agents/core/routers/agents_api.py:150; draft_description, :238) asks the strict-local model for one paragraph from the live persona and saves nothing. With no local model it is a 503, never a cloud call (:255-258). HUD. The Dossier has an Edit persona button that opens the live SOUL in frontend/src/soul-edit.tsx (SoulEditor, :49, mounted at frontend/src/modes.tsx:118). It offers Preview against the live text, Apply, Draft description with Use it (withDescription, :15, writes the front-matter line), and the hub's refusal in words (refusalText, :32). The Dossier also shows the description. The Prompts panel (PromptsPanel in frontend/src/gap.tsx, not pinned: high-churn) gets apply beside commit, through the same PUT, and says when a rollback is live. Two survivors of the first-edit-only seed led to keeping hand edits as versions; that code's own five mutants are caught. The fsync is a crash-only property. | <a id="h157"></a>H157 | Edit every configuration key from the UI | update | Echivalent | Reevaluat | Every configuration key is reachable and searchable from the UI, and every one but a secret or a route-only row (settings_db.ROUTE_ONLY: the skill switches, the voice command providers, the security data-handling acknowledgments) is portable and resettable. The backend it builds on: \`GET /api/admin/settings\` (agents/core/routers/admin.py:74) returns every category, and the per-category PUT (agents/core/routers/admin.py:242) validates with \`validate_category\` and answers 422 before any write, auditing the changed key names and the new value of a choice only (\`_audited_values\`, agents/core/routers/admin.py:125). New in H157: \`GET /api/admin/settings/export\` (agents/core/routers/admin.py:79, registered before the \`/{category}\` read so it is never taken for one) returns the declared settings as a \`nerva-settings/1\` document with an attachment disposition, leaving out every secret (encrypted at rest, or named like a token, secret, password, client id or API key), \`mcp.servers\` (it holds credentials by design) any URL that carries a password (\`http://user:pw@host\`, in a list too), and any free-form value the H495 secret scanner would mask (or every free-form value, when the scanner cannot run), and naming each left-out setting with its reason (export_settings, agents/core/settings_db.py:1430; is_secret_setting, agents/core/settings_db.py:1376; _looks_like_credential, agents/core/settings_db.py:1409; _url_password, agents/core/settings_db.py:1393). \`POST /api/admin/settings/import\` (agents/core/routers/admin.py:384) takes such a document (at most 1 MB and 1,000 keys, the body counted as it streams in, so a chunked upload is bounded too: _bounded_body, agents/core/routers/admin.py:371). The import and the reset take only an \`application/json\` request (415 otherwise, a type a browser must pre-check before sending) and refuse one the browser marks cross-site (403), since the admin guard trusts loopback on a default install (_refuse_cross_site_write, agents/core/routers/admin.py:357); every reply is no-store, and only a JSON \`true\` makes a dry run. A NaN, an Infinity or nesting too deep to store is refused (422), never stored, an \`mcp.servers\` entry needs a name (validate_category, agents/core/settings_db.py:1171, via _mcp_servers_problem, agents/core/settings_db.py:1243; the loader skips a nameless entry too, MCPManager.load_from_config, agents/core/mcp/client.py:925), and 2000 and 2000.0 are the same number, so no change (_same_value, agents/core/settings_db.py:1518). In the document every key must be declared and passes the same \`validate_category\` a single write does, so a posture flag or an out-of-range value is refused like any other; one refusal and nothing is written (422 with every reason) (plan_import, agents/core/settings_db.py:1462). Only the keys whose value differs are written, in one sqlite transaction, all or nothing, secrets encrypted as a single write encrypts them (apply_import, agents/core/settings_db.py:1552), with one audit row naming the settings (and the new value of a choice); \`"dry_run": true\` answers what would change, a secret's values shown as \`(secret)\` and a credential-shaped free value as \`(hidden)\`, so the preview never echoes one (describe_changes, agents/core/settings_db.py:1526). \`POST /api/admin/settings/{category}/reset\` (agents/core/routers/admin.py:460) puts one category back to its declared values and names the keys that moved, with an audit row; it keeps the category's secrets and its route-only rows (the skill switches, the voice command providers, the security data-handling acknowledgments) and names them (kept, reset_kept, agents/core/settings_db.py:1578; the HUD counts every kept row as a secret) and names the settings the product posture still forces (overridden, posture_overridden, agents/core/settings_db.py:1587), where the global reseed (agents/core/routers/admin.py:502) was the only reset (reset_category, agents/core/settings_db.py:1693). The v2 console SettingsPanel (frontend/src/gap.tsx:2894; widgets typed by settingsField, frontend/src/gap.tsx:2871) now has a search across every category matching a setting's category.key or label, with a match count and an honest no-match line (settingMatches, frontend/src/panels/settings-tools.tsx:37); a reset per category heading (only one with declared rows) that asks first, by a second click that names how many settings go back and moves the focus to itself, drops the category's unsaved edits once it runs and names what was kept and what the posture still forces (ResetCategory, frontend/src/panels/settings-tools.tsx:92); edits hidden by the search are counted beside the save; and a MOVE A CONFIGURATION section (SettingsTransfer, frontend/src/panels/settings-tools.tsx:187) that downloads the export and names what the hub left out, and imports a pasted or chosen file by showing the hub's dry run (each change old → new) and applying it only on a second step, listing every reason on a refusal; a pasted \`dry_run\` is dropped so the apply step is never a dry run, the text is held while the hub answers, and the file picker is reachable from the keyboard. The standalone /admin app's GlobalConfigPage (agents/web/static/admin.js:447) is unchanged, and \`nerva config list\|get\|set\|check\` (cmd_config in agents/cli/nerva.py; the file is high-churn and no longer pinned by this row) still edits single keys offline. tests/test_settings_transfer.py (28 cases) covers the export (every declared key either exported or named as left out, secrets, client ids, mcp.servers, a token-shaped value, a scanner that cannot run, the stored value), the import (an export imports back as no change, valid changes, every refusal a single write makes, nothing written on one refusal, one transaction, the posture flag, a secret encrypted and never echoed, the bound), the per-category reset, and the routes (admin only, the export not read as a category, preview then apply with one audit row, every reason on a refusal, no row when nothing changes, reset and 404); tests/test_h157b_settings_review.py (30, the first review) covers the JSON-only and cross-site refusals, URL passwords, a credential in a list, the hidden preview, NaN, Infinity and deep nesting, nameless MCP servers, number equality, secrets kept on a reset, the posture's settings named, the change listeners, the 1 MB bound for a sized and a chunked body and the JSON-only dry run; frontend/src/test/settings-tools.test.tsx (12) covers the search, the two-step reset, the export note, the dry-run preview and the second-step apply with the admin credential, a refusal's reasons, text that is not JSON, an import that changes nothing, a reset that drops unsaved edits and names kept secrets, edits hidden by the search, a pasted dry run never applied and the keyboard-reachable file button. 25 backend mutants, all caught (one after its case was added: a scanner that cannot run). The first adversarial review (review-H157: 2 major, 7 minor, 12 nit) found that a page the owner visited could post a plain-text import to a loopback hub, and that a URL password was exported; all are fixed, and its 18 mutants were all caught but one equivalent (two after their cases were pinned). | <a id="h164"></a>H164 | Share a diagnostic report for support | keep | Echivalent | Reevaluat | GET /api/support/bundle (admin) builds an allow-listed diagnostic bundle (agents/core/routers/support.py:21-39). It holds meta/version and build, posture, capabilities, egress and audit counts, model ids, the names of credential variables that are set, non-default settings, and an opt-in, redacted, e-mail-masked WARNING+ log tail. The route caps that tail at 500 lines with log_lines. With download=true it serves the same no-cache JSON as an attachment named nerva-support-bundle-\<UTC stamp\>.json (agents/core/routers/support.py:36-38). The bundle now has a component-health section. _health reads the orchestrator's ComponentRegistry, the same source as GET /api/health/components, and returns total, ok, the failed names, failed_unnamed and a state of ok, degraded or empty (agents/core/support_bundle.py:271-290). Only names that look like plain identifiers are printed (agents/core/support_bundle.py:66); any other key is only counted. With no registry, or when reading it fails, the section is {"error": "unavailable"} and never an invented all-ok. build_bundle includes the section (agents/core/support_bundle.py:312), and render_text prints a "components: N/M ok · failed: ..." line (agents/core/support_bundle.py:342-350). \`nerva support bundle --logs N\` serves the same report from the terminal (agents/cli/nerva.py:823). The HUD SupportBundleCard now offers the log tail through a 0/50/200/500 menu (frontend/src/panels/support-voice.tsx:97, frontend/src/panels/support-voice.tsx:203-211). The menu changes the admin read to ?log_lines=N (frontend/src/panels/support-voice.tsx:108). The card shows a logs row with the record count, the truncated flag, any note or the error (frontend/src/panels/support-voice.tsx:339-353). It also shows a component-health row with ok/total and failed names in red; an empty registry is shown grey, never green (frontend/src/panels/support-voice.tsx:319-337). A "download .json" button sits beside the copy button (frontend/src/panels/support-voice.tsx:355-360). It saves the admin-fetched JSON as a Blob named from the bundle's own generated_at (frontend/src/panels/support-voice.tsx:100-104, frontend/src/panels/support-voice.tsx:156-178). It says only that the download started, and it reports an unavailable or failed download as such. The card is mounted through the panel sections (frontend/src/gap.tsx:5528), and the ConsoleOverlay gives live inspection (frontend/src/gap.tsx:5567). Tests: tests/test_support_bundle.py:358-431 cover the health roll-up, an unavailable registry with odd names, the render_text line, and the route's attachment download with log_lines; the file passes 30 tests. frontend/src/panels/support-voice.test.tsx:178-266 cover the log opt-in path, unavailable logs, the health rendering including the empty registry, health counted as a failed section, the download file name, and an honest failure when the browser cannot download. Minor, not part of the row's gap: after a failed reload the copy and download buttons could still save the previous bundle. A slug is only ever a key into it, never joined into a path, so an unknown slug, '../' or encoded traversal is 404. - A file must be a regular file under the install root; a symlink is refused (agents/core/routers/help_docs.py:85). A file missing from an install reads as "not available", not an error. - Responses are no-store. (2) The page. DocsPanel (frontend/src/panels/docs.tsx:37) is registered in the console's Start group (frontend/src/console-routes.ts:6), in PANEL_COMPONENTS (frontend/src/gap.tsx:5420) and in the desktop app's route allowlist (desktop/src-tauri/hud-routes.json:49). - It lists the documents, disabling one not shipped, and renders the chosen one through the new shared Markdown component (frontend/src/markdown.tsx:101). - That component emits React elements only (no innerHTML path): headings with anchors, code fences, pipe tables, lists, quotes and rules, plus bold, italic, inline code and links. A link renders only for http(s) or a same-origin path, in a new tab with rel=noopener noreferrer (safeHref, frontend/src/markdown.tsx:25). Raw HTML in a document stays literal text. There is no regex lookbehind, so older Safari can parse the bundle. (3) Open in a new tab. | <a id="h200"></a>H200 | Webhook subscription management surface | update | Echivalent | Reevaluat | Built in #1207 together with H153 (critic note 7: one spec, one panel), then fixed after an adversarial review. The v2 console has a Webhooks panel, WebhooksPanel (frontend/src/panels/webhooks.tsx:269), registered in the Interop group (frontend/src/console-routes.ts:50; the entry is asserted at frontend/src/test/webhooks-panel.test.tsx:71). Interop mode's WEBHOOKS list links to it by an accessible name (frontend/src/modes2.tsx:343). Every panel call sends the admin credential. The backend stays admin-only CRUD: list, create, switch and delete all carry Depends(admin_guard) (agents/core/routers/webhooks.py:237, agents/core/routers/webhooks.py:243, agents/core/routers/webhooks.py:257, agents/core/routers/webhooks.py:284). Interop mode is built from its four sources alone (hydrateInterop, frontend/src/api/live.ts:126). All four (A2A peers, MCP servers, widgets, webhooks) are admin-only routes and are fetched with the admin credential, and so is the webhooks settings category: while the receiver switch is off every webhook row reads "receiver off", and a switch it could not read is said under WEBHOOKS (frontend/src/api/live.ts:119, frontend/src/modes2.tsx:344). A section whose source failed is empty and says "not connected", and an empty real list says "none" (Section, frontend/src/modes2.tsx:304); the demo seed's rows are never shown under the LIVE chip. When no source answers nothing is overwritten, so the mode stays "Not connected" and DEMO keeps its seed. The review found that fetching only the webhooks list with the credential had marked the whole mode LIVE over seeded peers, MCP servers and widgets. The five accepted parts: (1) Create dialog: name, agent or workflow target, target id and an HMAC-signed toggle, and, since H153, a description, an event list, a prompt template, where the result goes and deliver only, posted to POST /api/webhooks. A refusal shows the hub's own reason, and an empty target is refused before any request. The create button is held while the call is pending and while a new hook's credentials are on screen, so a second hook cannot replace a secret before it was saved. (2) Created result, shown once (Reveal, frontend/src/panels/webhooks.tsx:227): the absolute trigger URL (triggerUrl, frontend/src/panels/webhooks.tsx:63: the page origin, the base path and the encoded id), and the token, or the signing secret for a signed hook, each with a copy button that says "copied" in a polite live region, plus the header the sender must send. Only the warning sentence is an alert, so a screen reader does not read the secret aloud. On a loopback origin it says a sender elsewhere needs an address it can reach. The secret lives only in the panel's state and is dropped on "I have saved it" (focus returns to the create form) or unmount. The list never carries it: WebhookStore masks the token to a 4-character hint (agents/core/webhooks.py:842). (3) Detail pane: clicking a hook expands its trigger URL, auth header (with the token hint), calls, last call and creation time, the deliveries its event list skipped and the last event skipped, and an editor for its event list and prompt template (H153). The row shows target_type:target, an HMAC or token badge, an on/off badge and an event-count badge. (4) Delete with confirmation: "delete…" arms an inline confirmation that explains the sender's credential dies with the hook and moves focus to "delete for good", which sends DELETE; "keep it" returns focus to "delete…". Each row button's accessible name includes the hook's name. A row's buttons are held while its call is pending, and every switch or delete reloads the list whatever the hub answered: a hook already deleted elsewhere is reported as gone ("ci was already deleted", "ci no longer exists") and its row disappears, with focus moved to the create form; a refused delete keeps the confirmation and says why. A per-hook on/off switch (PATCH, H153) is offered as the reversible alternative. (5) Governance: creating, switching and deleting a hook each write a SecurityEvent (_audit_webhook, agents/core/routers/webhooks.py:203, called at agents/core/routers/webhooks.py:253, agents/core/routers/webhooks.py:278 and agents/core/routers/webhooks.py:290). It names the hook id, the target as a JSON string (agents/core/routers/webhooks.py:197), so a target cannot pass its own text off as the row's id or flags, and the signed and enabled flags as the store reads them, never the token or signing secret. A delete of an unknown id writes no webhook audit row (agents/core/routers/webhooks.py:289) and answers 404 "webhook not found" (agents/core/routers/webhooks.py:292). Since #1247 the admin guard's own auth telemetry (AUTH_SUCCESS and AUTH_FAILURE rows) lands in the same audit log, so the backend tests set those rows aside before counting webhook rows (_action_events, tests/test_h10_8_webhooks.py:266); an unknown switch adds none (tests/test_h10_8_webhooks.py:322) and a repeated delete adds none (tests/test_h10_8_webhooks.py:331). The receiver-disabled banner: when the receiver switch (H153, the setting webhooks.receiver_enabled) is off, the panel's receiver row says every delivery is refused until it is switched back on (frontend/src/panels/webhooks.tsx:478). The restart-gateway banner is not needed: a delivery sees the switch at most a second old (at once after a write in this process), and hook CRUD is served live; the receiver row says so. Not built, and not part of this row: a \`nerva webhooks\` CLI verb (critic note 7 places it with H409, as \`nerva webhooks inbound\|outbound\`) and a mobile screen. Tests: frontend/src/test/webhooks-panel.test.tsx has 56 cases. By describe block, 23 are this row's (the panel, the trigger URL and the review round; one of them, an open delete confirmation held while the same row switches, was added by H168), and 13 of those failed on the pre-review panel: the pending hold, the reload and the ghost row after a switch or delete, the one-POST create and the create held while a secret shows, the hook-named buttons, focus, the alert without the secret, the "copied" live region, the loopback hint and an unencodable id. The other 33 are H153's: the subscriptions, the receiver row and banner, the event list, the template, Deliver to, focus after a hook is gone, the push note and a proxy's 404. frontend/src/test/interop-live-honesty.test.tsx (14 cases, 5 of them H153's receiver read) drives the real useLiveModes against admin-guarded mock routes and renders InteropMode. The backend audit and DELETE guards are pinned in tests/test_h10_8_webhooks.py (tests/test_h10_8_webhooks.py:367, tests/test_h10_8_webhooks.py:377, tests/test_h10_8_webhooks.py:386); the file has 35 cases. Mutation: 60 mutants of the review round's guards (11 backend, 27 panel, 15 Interop, 7 v1) and 16 of the H153 panel additions were each run against their own suite, and all were caught; before the review round, 12 of the reviewer's 42 mutants had survived. Re-read 2026-10-12 (b339672c): the only change to agents/core/routers/webhooks.py is the quiet-hours hour now read in the app zone (H450 fix); no claim or cited line of this row moved. Re-read 2026-10-14 after main (#1255) changed the pinned file(s). The whole change is a Map index for the console panels: frontend/src/console-routes.ts gained CONSOLE_PANEL_MAP, a Map built from CONSOLE_PANELS (additive; the array and its entries are untouched). The 121 panel ids are unique, so Map.get and find return the same panel; a miss now yields null where find yielded undefined, and both call sites only test truthiness. Every citation of this review resolves unchanged. tsc is clean and the frontend suite (236 files, 2,198 tests) passes on this head. Verdict unchanged. | <a id="h209"></a>H209 | Keyboard shortcut customisation with a recorder and conflict detection | copy | Echivalent | Reevaluat | The HUD's keyboard shortcuts live in one registry, as in Hermes. frontend/src/shortcuts.ts defines every action once (ACTIONS: id, category, label, default chord, scope): the ten mode keys, World (w), the Console (\`), Ambient (a), Cinema (m) and its three stages (o, n, b, scope cinema), focus the message box (/), the command palette (mod+k) and the Keyboard Shortcuts panel (mod+/). app.tsx (World's key included: WorldAwareApp passes onWorld and shares the live overrides through useShortcutOverrides) and the cinema overlay in shell.tsx dispatch through matchAction over bindings(overrides) instead of literal key maps, and every key hint (palette, top bar, World, Console, cinema stages) is read from the registry (chordOf, displayChord). A matched action takes the key from the browser (preventDefault); Shift+letter falls back to the bare letter unless it is bound itself. frontend/src/shortcuts-panel.tsx is the panel mod+/ opens: categories Navigation, View, Composer and Session with search (searchBindings); click a chord to record a new one ("Press a key…", Esc cancels, a lone modifier keeps listening; chordFromEvent, rebind); the palette and the panel take only a chord held with Ctrl/⌘ or Alt (acceptsChord), fire in an input only then (firesInInputs), and the palette always has a Keyboard shortcuts entry, so no rebinding can lock the panel out; Space is spelled "space", and a chord with no key is refused on record and on read; Esc closes the panel without closing what lies beneath; per-binding reset and Reset all (resetBinding); an "Also bound to X" note when two actions share a chord (conflictsFor). Overrides persist per viewer in localStorage under hud.shortcuts, validated on read (readOverrides, loadOverrides, saveOverrides), and survive storage that is off. Governance: defineActions refuses any action whose id, category or label names an approval, a decision, an accept, reject, deny or consent (FORBIDDEN_TARGET), so no chord can reach a Decision Inbox action. Tests: frontend/src/test/shortcuts.test.tsx (25), app-routing.test.tsx (+14: panel, rebinding, persistence, World, composer focus, the Space and Ctrl+Space lockout, the palette entry, the typing guard, preventDefault, World behind the panel, storage off, live hints, Esc beneath, Cinema), cinema.test.tsx (+1: rebound stage keys); voice-orb and briefing-wall expect the registry's stage titles; 38 mutants, 36 killed, 2 equivalent; the review round's 19 mutants, all killed (4 by tests added after a first pass). Re-review on 2026-10-02: The current app diff only passes the active agent into the image composer; keyboard shortcut behavior remains unchanged. Existing no-media memory, text turns, previous composer route, and unrelated orchestrator/HUD behavior retain their prior branches; focused H277/H513/composer/session tests, 1,872 frontend tests, TypeScript and HUD build pass. Existing verdict preserved; this note does not claim live-provider acceptance or a new Hermes capability. It adds ACTIONS_MAP, a Map built from ACTIONS, and uses it for the four id lookups (acceptsChord, readOverrides, chordOf, rebind) in place of ACTIONS.find / a rebuilt Set. defineActions throws on a duplicate id, so first-match and last-wins coincide; the registry, the default chords, the governance filter and every cited line are unchanged (cite reports each citation unchanged). | <a id="h221"></a>H221 | Language switcher | keep | Echivalent | Reevaluat | The HUD's language control is now a list, not a two-way toggle. frontend/src/data.ts:283-286 defines LANGUAGES, the languages the HUD has full I18N tables for (English and Romanian, each with its own-language label and a text direction). The TopBar globe button is a menu button (LangMenu, frontend/src/shell.tsx:91-142) that opens a radio list over LANGUAGES with the active language checked and each row tagged with its own lang. It supports the keyboard pattern: ArrowDown/ArrowUp on the globe open it, arrows wrap, Home/End jump, Enter/Space or a click choose, Escape returns focus to the globe, and a press elsewhere or Tab closes it. The command palette carries one 'Language · \<name\>' row per language with the active one ticked, in place of the old 'Toggle language EN / RO' row (frontend/src/shell.tsx:413-414). There is no separate Appearance settings panel in the HUD frontend (the only 'Appearance' mention outside tests and the workspace app is the comment at frontend/src/shell.tsx:382 saying the palette is the control surface); font, accent, look, density, motion, scanline and dot grid are all chosen from the palette, so the Language rows there are this HUD's Appearance language row. The language is now a real appearance preference: 'lang' is a member of the client option table (frontend/src/appearance.ts:11-12), of the server option table whose codes mirror LANGUAGES (agents/core/appearance.py:17-18) and of the PUT body model of the preferences endpoint (agents/core/routers/preferences.py:24). It is cached locally, queued offline as an ordinary edit, and synced with the same revisioned document as the other display choices, so a second browser of the same owner picks it up; an untranslated code is coerced to 'en' by the server. App reads and sets it through that preference (frontend/src/app.tsx:105-108), sets the document lang and dir and keeps writing hud.lang for the still-served v1 shell once the first hydration has finished (frontend/src/app.tsx:233-239), and adopts a language change made by the v1 shell (jarvis:locale_changed or a hud.lang storage event) when the code is a known one (frontend/src/app.tsx:242-251). A legacy hud.lang that holds a translated, non-default code is journalled once as an explicit edit so a configured server document answering 'en' cannot revert the owner's old choice, and a plain 'en' is never uploaded (frontend/src/appearance.ts:62-77 and frontend/src/appearance.ts:85-88). Tests pin all of this: frontend/src/test/language-menu.test.tsx:25-34 ties LANGUAGES to the I18N tables, frontend/src/test/language-menu.test.tsx:44-57 and frontend/src/test/language-menu.test.tsx:59-74 pin the menu roles, checked state and keyboard flow, frontend/src/test/language-menu.test.tsx:111-123 pins switching strings and document lang with a single saved PUT, frontend/src/test/language-menu.test.tsx:160-175 and frontend/src/test/language-menu.test.tsx:177-187 pin the legacy adoption and no double upload, frontend/src/test/language-menu.test.tsx:189-200 pins following the v1 shell, and frontend/src/test/language-menu.test.tsx:202-210 pins the palette rows end to end; frontend/src/test/palette-tweaks.test.tsx:59-66 pins the palette rows and their choose-by-code action; tests/test_appearance_preferences.py:138-145 pins the server round trip and the coercion of an unknown code (its defaults document at tests/test_appearance_preferences.py:33 carries lang). Honest limits: only English and Romanian are offered, because those are the only translated tables (adding a language is a data change in LANGUAGES, the I18N tables and the server option tuple, which is kept in step by hand); the list is not searchable and there is no native-script flag or locale detection; Hermes's literal Settings page does not exist here and this is verified only by the component tests under jsdom, not in a real browser or with a screen reader. Re-read 2026-10-24 (batch 4): the globe toggle became a language list menu, the palette gained per-language rows, and the language joined the synced appearance preferences with legacy hud.lang adoption and test coverage. A reply cut off mid-body or a garbled status line on any hub read is HubUnavailable, so \`nerva status\` reports an unreachable hub instead of a traceback (agents/cli/client.py:187, tests/test_nerva_cli.py:200).
