| <a id="h247"></a>H247 | Wake word arming per surface, push-to-talk capture, TTS, and liveness/config primitives | update | Echivalent | Reevaluat | Nerva now knows which surface holds each microphone. A surface arms only if the owner allowed its kind; one device's microphone has one holder at a time; and arming, pausing, resuming and stopping carry the surface's identity and are audited. This is the adaptation's missing concept, on top of the voice primitives that already existed (wake word, push-to-talk and hands-free capture, TTS, STT, capabilities, and H222's listening indicator). The lease table is agents/core/voice/mic.py (MicArbiter, agents/core/voice/mic.py:93; one process-wide ARBITER, agents/core/voice/mic.py:232). (1) Surfaces and devices. A surface is kind:client: host:hub (the hub's own wake-word pipeline), hud:\<tab\> or mobile:\<device\> (ARMABLE, agents/core/voice/mic.py:39). A Wyoming satellite has its own microphone and is not armed here. A lease is for one device. host is the machine the hub runs on, and a browser that the route sees on loopback shares it. The route decides that from the address a trusted proxy vouches for (_mic_device, agents/core/routers/voice.py:528), so a LAN client cannot claim to be local. Otherwise a browser gets remote:hud:\<tab\>, and every phone gets mobile:\<device\>. (2) One holder per device. A second surface arming a held device is refused, naming the holder (MicRefused mic_busy, agents/core/voice/mic.py:49; HTTP 409). With take_over, it pauses the holder and tells it (on_change, agents/core/voice/mic.py:144). A pause frees the device (agents/core/voice/mic.py:199). A resume asks again, both for consent and for the device's holder (agents/core/voice/mic.py:212). A stop releases the lease (agents/core/voice/mic.py:221). (3) Consent. A kind arms only if the setting voice.mic_surfaces allows it (allowed_kinds, agents/core/voice/mic.py:59). The setting is a declared tags setting whose values are validated against host, hud and mobile (agents/core/settings_db.py:286, agents/core/settings_db.py:1212). The default is hud and mobile (DEFAULT_ALLOWED, agents/core/voice/mic.py:40): surfaces someone uses on purpose. The hub's always-on listener needs host added. So VoiceChannel.start (agents/core/channels/voice.py:29) opens the host microphone only with a lease. Before this, it started at boot with no check. It stops the pipeline when taken over and starts it again when given back (_on_lease, agents/core/channels/voice.py:48). Withdrawn consent ends a lease at its next renewal. (4) Leases lapse. A browser or phone lease lapses LEASE_SECONDS (45, agents/core/voice/mic.py:42) after its last renewal (_expire_locked, agents/core/voice/mic.py:108). The host pipeline's lease does not lapse. The table holds at most 32 leases. (5) Audit. Every arm, take-over, pause, stop and refusal is one audit row naming the surface and the device. A renewal is not. (6) Routes, all user-guarded. GET /api/voice/mic answers who holds each device, the paused leases and the allowed kinds (agents/core/routers/voice.py:549). POST /api/voice/mic/arm (agents/core/routers/voice.py:558) takes hud or mobile and answers 403 or 409. /pause, /resume and /stop act on a lease by name (agents/core/routers/voice.py:577, agents/core/routers/voice.py:588, agents/core/routers/voice.py:602). (7) The HUD. The voice loop arms its lease before getUserMedia (frontend/src/voice.ts:414; armMic, frontend/src/mic-lease.ts:47) and renews it every 20 s (frontend/src/voice.ts:434). It releases the lease on every end of the loop (frontend/src/voice.ts:135). If a renewal is refused, it stops and says who took the microphone. Only a hub refusal blocks: a hub that cannot answer does not. The loop offers take over (takeOver, frontend/src/voice.ts:454; the voice pill, frontend/src/cockpit.tsx:256). The voice settings list the holders, with pause, resume and stop (MicLeases, frontend/src/mic-leases.tsx:17). Tests: tests/test_h247_mic_lease.py has 27. They cover consent, kinds, client and device names, withdrawn consent, a conflict and a take-over, renewal, lapse, pause and resume, stop, the bound, status, the numbers, the setting and its reading, the voice channel's lease, loopback against LAN against a phone, the routes and their guard. frontend/src/test/mic-lease.test.tsx has 10: arm before the mic, a named holder and take-over, no consent, an unreachable hub, renewal and loss, a cancelled start, an unmount, a click handler, the pill and the settings list. 61 mutants: 60 caught, eleven of them after survivors got cases. One of those survivors exposed a device name that was too long for a 64-character client id; it is fixed. The last was a redundant check, removed. Not in this row: no install path installs a voice engine. The named STT/TTS command-provider change touched only the voice router's provider catalog, intake and selector fields; the mic lease routes and the consent check are unchanged, and both test files above pass. | <a id="h259"></a>H259 | Reset to defaults, scoped and previewed, plus export/import of the whole configuration | update | Echivalent | Reevaluat | A settings reset now shows what it will change, never touches a secret and can be undone, and the HUD marks every setting that differs from its default. Hermes' config-reset and defaults surface is covered, on top of H157's search, secret-free export, dry-run import and per-category reset. (1) Defaults. Every declared row that is not a secret carries its declared default (agents/core/settings_db.py:788, in _mark_overlay :731, used by GET /api/admin/settings and each category read). A secret carries none. The Settings panel marks a row whose value, or staged edit, differs from its default ("changed", with the default in its tooltip); a ↺ button stages the default and the usual save writes it through the validated PUT (frontend/src/gap.tsx:2996). (2) A preview before any reset. plan_reset (agents/core/settings_db.py:1614) computes what a reset of one category, or of every category, would write: each declared setting that is neither a secret nor a route-only row (settings_db.ROUTE_ONLY: the skill switches, the voice command providers, the security data-handling acknowledgments) and whose stored value is not its default. POST /api/admin/settings/{category}/reset and POST /api/admin/settings/reseed take {"dry_run": true} and answer the changes as current → default without writing anything (agents/core/routers/admin.py:460, :430; _dry_run_asked, :379; only a JSON true, in a body of at most 4 KB). The changes use describe_changes, so a credential-shaped value shows as (hidden). Arming the reset in the HUD asks for that preview and lists it, and counts the settings kept (secrets and route-only rows, all labelled secrets) and names the settings the posture still forces (ResetPreview, frontend/src/panels/settings-tools.tsx:64; ResetCategory, :92). (3) The reseed no longer deletes the store. It used to run DELETE FROM settings, wiping every setting, secrets included, with no preview and no way back. It is now the per-category reset over every category: secrets and route-only rows are kept (and named), rows nothing declares are left, it takes a JSON request from this origin only (415/403 otherwise, as H157's writes), and it is audited with the settings that moved (agents/core/routers/admin.py:502). The v1 admin page sends it as JSON (agents/web/static/admin.js:1520). The HUD gets "reset every category…" with the same preview (ResetAll, frontend/src/panels/settings-tools.tsx:115). (4) Undo. reset_settings (agents/core/settings_db.py:1654) writes the defaults and records what it replaced in settings_resets (:120) in the same transaction, keeping the last 20 (RESETS_KEPT, :1516). POST /api/admin/settings/undo (agents/core/routers/admin.py:536; undo_last_reset, agents/core/settings_db.py:1719-1726) puts back the latest reset not yet undone. A setting changed since that reset, one its declaration no longer accepts, or one no longer declared is left as it is and named in skipped. The undo is audited, and the listeners hear every value a reset or an undo writes, so the webhook receiver switch follows it. GET /api/admin/settings/resets (agents/core/routers/admin.py:92; list_resets, agents/core/settings_db.py:1706) lists the resets, newest first, naming settings but never their values. The HUD shows "last reset: \<scope\> · N settings · \<time\>" with "undo…" (UndoReset, frontend/src/panels/settings-tools.tsx:135). Every reset and undo in the HUD is a two-step ConfirmAction at the REVERSIBLE tier (H168). Adapted from the row's ask: the reseed does not go through the approval queue's irreversible tier, because it is no longer irreversible. It keeps secrets, previews, and can be undone. Routing it through the queue would need a new kernel action kind for it, and none is declared (agents/core/kernel/registry.py's one settings kind is H613's settings.voice_command). | <a id="h270"></a>H270 | Writer allowlist for names that hijack execution or soften posture | copy | Parțial | Reevaluat | Nerva has no write-side policy for environment-variable names — the row's deliverable (a declared-names allowlist, depends_on "the key registry") does not exist, and the row defers it rather than excluding it. #1179 changed nothing on this row's subject: its client.py change is an outbound disclosure (cwd_secret_files :215-242 and the "withholding is undercut" WARNING in _merged_env :561-572), not a name policy or a writer. Neither did the fail-closed tool-filter bounds change (56903ac1: tool_patterns_over_bounds, a deny-bounds block in MCPServer.__init__ and a tools_allow/tools_deny bounds refusal in admin_mcp_add) — it touches no env name, writer or override path and only moved line numbers. H502 (#1174) did change item 3 and half of item 2, and that is folded in here. Three items owed, two shippable today against real surfaces: 1. THE REGISTRY (the row's core item, blocked on its stated dependency). No general env-name registry exists and no \`config.write\` capability kind exists in agents/core/capability_actions.py. The one writer that persists env-var names today, H595's llm.execute_code_env_passthrough setting and skill declarations, is gated by code_env._passable_name (agents/core/code_env.py:84-92, enforced at agents/core/settings_db.py:1046-1052), a denylist that still passes NODE_PATH, EDITOR, VISUAL, PAGER, BROWSER and GIT_SSH_COMMAND; owed there: refuse those names too, or replace the denylist with the declared-names registry. Of Hermes' hijack names, PATH, SHELL (agents/core/mcp/client.py:166), NODE_PATH (:171) and PATH, SHELL, PYTHONPATH (agents/core/environments/__init__.py:18, :27, :30) are named as members of the two OUTBOUND allowlists, and EDITOR is exercised at tests/test_nerva_import.py:165 (pinned dropped at tests/test_nerva_import.py:825). Design consequence: the outbound lists cannot double as the write-side registry — they deliberately admit the plumbing names Hermes forbids on write — so the registry is a separate, inbound-only list. When any env/config writer lands, that allowlist must land in the SAME PR, refusing an undeclared name before authorization — the shape of agents/core/capability_actions.py:147-151 refusing missing_inputs before the authorizer at :159-160. 2. THE MCP \`env\` BOUNDARY IS UNREFUSED (shippable now; the "untested" half closed with #1174). MCPServerConfig (agents/core/routers/mcp.py:145-156) sets no \`model_config\`, so pydantic's default extra="ignore" makes \`POST /api/admin/mcp {"env": {"LD_PRELOAD": "/tmp/evil.so"}}\` return 200 and silently drop the key instead of refusing it — reproduced end to end at HEAD through TestClient (200 {"ok": true}; stored MCPServer.env == {}; to_config() has no env key). The field it would populate is live — MCPServer.env (agents/core/mcp/client.py:439) → _merged_env (:531-577) → create_subprocess_exec(env=…) (:453-460). Already pinned by tests/test_mcp_transports.py:507-522: \`env\` is not a MCPServerConfig field, to_config (:798-812) does not export it and load_from_config (:814-849) does not read it. Reachability: the HUD only GETs /api/admin/mcp (frontend/src/api/live.ts:449) and no CLI adds servers, so the raw admin API is the only path today. Still owed: \`extra="forbid"\` (or an explicit named refusal) on MCPServerConfig, plus a test asserting the route refuses an \`env\` body rather than swallowing it — and the same refusal must cover the hijack names above on the day \`env\` becomes operator-settable. 3. PER-SERVER \`env\` BYPASSES THE ALLOWLIST IN BOTH BRANCHES. stdio_env_baseline applies overrides unfiltered after the allowlist loop (agents/core/mcp/client.py:282-283; docstring :253 "Explicit per-server overrides always win"), and the legacy branch does \`merged = os.environ.copy(); merged.update(self.env)\` with no filter (:575-576). The "decide whether the baseline should become the default" half of this item is DONE: since H502 the baseline is on unless JARVIS_MCP_STDIO_ENV_BASELINE=0 (:179-190; docs/FLAGS.md "on by default since H502") and tests/test_mcp_transports.py:386-421 pins both directions, so the legacy branch is now the explicit escape hatch rather than the shipped path. Owed: gate per-server overrides on the item-1 write-side registry (NOT merely on STDIO_ENV_ALLOWLIST + _SECRET_LIKE — that policy passes PATH, SHELL, NODE_PATH and would pass an operator-supplied PATH/NODE_PATH override untouched), or make the bypass an explicitly reviewed, audited exception. Severity, checked directly rather than inferred: LATENT. \`MCPServerConfig\` has no \`env\` field, the admin route constructs MCPServer without one (agents/core/routers/mcp.py:226-238), and the dedicated WorldView override caller has been retired; the generic in-process override API remains. No untrusted input reaches the override loop, so this is a boundary to close before \`env\` becomes operator-settable, not a live hole. The outbound allowlist's one intentional exception — a name the owner lists in JARVIS_MCP_STDIO_ALLOWED_ENV passes even when credential-shaped (:256-260, :272-274; tests :449-503) — is owner-declared and host-wide, and is not this row's write boundary. | <a id="h273"></a>H273 | Tell the owner where an effective value actually came from | update | Echivalent | Reevaluat | Built in #1207, then fixed after eight adversarial reviews. The first found the stdlib parser was python-dotenv's pre-1.2.3 grammar, while the lock pins 1.2.3: the doctor could print value material as key names, a named-pipe .env was no longer loaded, and a data home named in the repo .env was no longer followed. The second found that the doctor sent the admin credential to whatever answered at the hub address, that more keys than serve.py's four were read before any .env was loaded, and that a one-case line of value material could still be printed as a name. The third found that the start itself read 31 more names before the load (so ten .env knobs, the audit key and the public-profile gate among them, were shown as in effect and were not), that two read-again entries were false, and that the MCP transport ignored a user token kept in .env. The fourth found that the MCP transport and the HTTP user guard asked different questions, so a lapsed or revoked user credential locked every route but left MCP open to a local caller; that the coordinator built its Orchestrator before the load, so its audit rows went unkeyed beside the hub's keyed ones; that an IPv6 bind (JARVIS_HOST=::1) escaped both loopback checks; and that the CLI sent the admin token to any hub. The fifth found that the admin tier still trusted a loopback caller once no admin credential was active, so after the owner revoked every credential a local process with no token could mint a fresh user token over HTTP and reopen the user routes and MCP (older than H273, but it falsified this row's credential sentence); that a managed user token that had expired counted as never configured; that the CLI asked the owner to set an admin token it had withheld; and that the supervisor wrote its respawns apart from a run-log named in .env. The sixth found that the sentence about minting did not hold where no admin credential was ever configured, that the offline recovery wrote a tokens.db the hub never read when the data home was named only in a .env (and a packaged build had none to run), that the CLI's withheld message fired on refusals https would not fix, and that a named-pipe .env still split the run-log. The seventh found that the supervisor now told its child a default the hub never read (a named-pipe .env hid the runtime from the brief), that the packaged recovery revived env tokens that had been rotated away or revoked, and that the CLI still asked for a token that was set. The eighth found that the packaged recovery still missed a token in the start environment or a moved data home, and left a LAN-bound app unable to start, and that the new hint called a valid user token refused on an admin verb and proposed a rotate that revoked the owner's working admin token. Every effective configuration key now carries the layer that supplied it, the note says when a .env value is not in effect, and every surface the row names reports names and layers only. The table. load_layered_env (agents/core/env_provenance.py:365) loads the files. Precedence: the process environment (the shell, a systemd EnvironmentFile, docker -e), then the repo .env, then the data-home .env, and the first layer to set a key wins (override=False). It keeps python-dotenv's behaviour: - Each file is read once, whether a regular file or a named pipe, the way python-dotenv reads it. 1Password mounts a .env as a FIFO. - The load is python-dotenv's public load_dotenv on the text that was read. The names come from python-dotenv's own parser (dotenv.parser.parse_stream), which logs nothing, so a bad line is warned about once. No private python-dotenv API is used. - PYTHON_DOTENV_DISABLED is checked before each layer, as python-dotenv checks it on every call, so a repo .env that sets it stops the data-home layer. Its spellings are python-dotenv's own, kept in env_config.py, the repo's one home for env-flag parsing (agents/core/env_config.py:112); a parity test pins them against python-dotenv's own switch. - The data home is a callable resolved after the repo layer is loaded, so a JARVIS_USER_HOME set in the repo .env names it, as before. A first-run home is scaffolded before its .env is read. - A second load in one process keeps a file's attribution only while the environment still holds the value that load set (a private digest, never the value), and works out afresh what the files shadow. The same file as both layers is read once. - It records which layer supplied each key, by diffing the environment around each file, and the lower layers that also define it (shadowed: their value is ignored). That answers "why is my .env change not applied?". - files() records what the load did with each file: its kind (file, fifo, absent, the same file as the repo .env, or disabled), whether it is present, and whether it was read. provenance() (agents/core/env_provenance.py:541) is the queryable in-process table; a key that appeared after the load reads as set while running. The hub loads first. load_hub_env (agents/core/env_provenance.py:463) is the hub's own load, once per process, so a named pipe is read once: - serve.py calls it before it builds the server and runs its guards (serve.py:345). The server's host, port, log level and shutdown timeout, the posture guards and the bind guard see a .env value, so a token in .env satisfies the bind guard. - The lifespan calls it before its boot guards (agents/web.py:476). The data home, logging, the orchestrator with its audit log, memory and budget ledger, and the router's detect() all read after it: the audit key, the public-profile seed gate, turn embeddings, the budget, the router's URLs and cloud keys in a .env are in effect. The boot guards, the front door among them, judge the loaded environment, so the late re-check was removed. - The coordinator (the systemd jarvis-runtime unit, compose runtime-coordinator) calls it first in run(), before its run-log path and cycle (scripts/coordinator.py:173), and again, idempotently, before it builds its Orchestrator (scripts/coordinator.py:84): it shares the hub's data root, so it keys the audit chain the hub keys. The supervisor that spawns it (scripts/runtime_supervisor.py) does not load, since its child would then read every file key as the process environment's; it reads the run-log path through hub_value (agents/core/env_provenance.py:490), the value the files give without loading them, and it hands its child only a path it found (the process, or a regular .env), which the child's load does not override, so both write that one run-log (scripts/runtime_supervisor.py:84; review-H273g m4). A path in a named-pipe .env, which the supervisor never reads, is not handed down: the child reads the pipe as the hub does, so the cycles land where the brief reads them, and only the supervisor's own events stay in the default file (_child_env, scripts/runtime_supervisor.py:122; review-H273h m1). An empty value is unset on both ends. The reality-evidence harness does too (agents/core/observability/reality_evidence.py:183). - agents/run.py, the REPL, loads before its logging and its imports (agents/run.py:21), so a log file or scanner pattern in .env is in effect. - PluginManager.build asks for it too (agents/core/plugin_manager.py:254), for any other entry. scripts/install_smoke.py does not load before it builds its isolated hub (a temp data root, from the process environment); its PluginManager.build loads afterwards, as for any entry. - Log redaction is imported first, so its switch stays the boot environment's alone: a .env cannot turn it off. Keys read before the load. note_for (agents/core/env_provenance.py:526) flags what is still read before any file can be. That is what importing agents.web freezes or resolves: the ASGI root path, the rate limit, CORS, CSP, the router's auto-deep switch, the analytics cap, the graph's Neo4j defaults, the app and data roots, and the log-redaction switch (agents/core/env_provenance.py:60). A .env value for them is recorded but not in effect, and the note says to set it in the process environment. - What locates the hub's own files (JARVIS_APP_ROOT, JARVIS_HOME, JARVIS_MEMORY_DIR) is never taken from a file (agents/core/env_provenance.py:69). A .env value would have split the stores between two roots. It is recorded and kept out of the environment, and its own note says so (agents/core/env_provenance.py:100). - JARVIS_USER_HOME from the repo .env names the data home and its .env. When JARVIS_HOME is not set, the stores opened while the hub was imported stay under the default root, and its note says so (agents/core/env_provenance.py:72). - Read again after the load, so a .env value is in effect (agents/core/env_provenance.py:93): DEV_MODE; the admin and user tokens (every guard reads them per request, the MCP transport included); the OAuth client ids; the trusted proxies. The lists are measured, not declared: - A test spies on the environment in a subprocess across the import and the whole start up to the load, with the data root set either way. Every Nerva name read there must be listed, and every listed name must be read there. - A second spy runs the start and a few requests. Every read-again name must be read after the load, and no name listed as read before the load may be (tests/test_h273d_provenance_review.py:667). The two false read-again entries are fixed: - The MCP transport, the HTTP user guard and the MCP identity check ask one predicate, _user_credential_required (agents/web.py:293; agents/core/routers/mcp.py:419). A token from .env guards MCP on this machine and lets a remote client in. The question is whether a credential was ever configured (_ever_configured, agents/web.py:109): an env token, active or superseded; a rotation or a revoke with --revoke-env, which leave the store's persistent flag; an issued token, live or expired. Such a credential that has lapsed, been rotated away or been revoked locks MCP exactly as it locks HTTP. The admin guard asks the same question for its tier (_admin_configured, agents/web.py:137), and so does the owner flag on /chat, so where an admin credential was ever configured and every credential is revoked or has expired, no local process mints its way back in over HTTP. Recovery is scripts/token_recover.py rotate admin on the box, which loads the hub's .env files first so it writes the tokens.db the hub reads, and says which (review-H273g m2); a packaged build first removes every JARVIS_ADMIN_TOKEN and JARVIS_USER_TOKEN from both places the app reads them, the data home's .env (wherever the home is) and the environment the app starts from, unsets JARVIS_HOST for the restart (the boot guard refuses a LAN bind with no token), then removes security/tokens.db under its data root (JARVIS_HOME and JARVIS_MEMORY_DIR named), because that file is also what records the rotations and revokes that superseded env tokens (docs/PACKAGING.md; review-H273h m2, review-H273i m1). The check lists the token table once per store: once a tier shows configured it stays so for that store (review-H273g n1). Only a hub that never had a credential of the tier trusts a localhost caller without one (for the exception, see Known limits). - The OAuth routes use the plugin manager's copy of the OAuth module (agents/core/routers/oauth.py:34), which re-reads the client ids after the load. Key names come from python-dotenv itself whenever it can be imported (text_keys, agents/core/env_provenance.py:202): every binding in file order, a rebound key each time. The stdlib port (_port_keys, agents/core/env_provenance.py:143) is 1.2.3's grammar and is the fallback for a broken install. A parity test pins it on 25 edge cases, including the BOM, escaped backslashes and a key rebound without "=". A seeded differential fuzz of 4,000 random files pins it too. derive (agents/core/env_provenance.py:327) builds the same table offline. It follows a data home named in the repo .env, or built from ${VAR}, resolving every binding in file order as load_dotenv does: the environment wins over the file's earlier values, a rebound key takes its last value, and a last binding without "=" sets nothing (agents/core/env_provenance.py:294). It parses each file once, keyed on its size, times and inode, and never opens a named pipe. Surfaces: - GET /api/admin/env/sources (agents/core/routers/admin.py:643) is admin-guarded and no-store, at the same boundary as GET /api/admin/env. Each key comes with its layer, a label, the layers it overrides, whether /api/admin/env masks its value, and its note. It also names what the load did with each file (path, kind, present, read); values are never included. - \`nerva doctor\`'s advisory config_sources check (scripts/doctor.py:891): - Reading the hub. It reads the running hub's own table when /readyz is ok, asking without a credential first. Every request to the hub goes over http or https, has a timeout, refuses a redirect, and never goes through a proxy to a hub on this machine (scripts/doctor.py:568). The hub address brackets an IPv6 bind (JARVIS_HOST=::1 gives http://\[::1\]:8080; scripts/doctor.py:352), and an unbracketed IPv6 address, whatever its first group (0:0:0:0:0:0:0:1 too), is read the way http.client dials it (scripts/doctor.py:526). The admin credential goes only to a hub on this machine, decided by its address rather than its spelling (127.0.0.2, 127.1, localhost., ::1 and ::ffff:127.0.0.1 count; scripts/doctor.py:542). config_sources sends it only after a refusal, and runtime_resolves only when no user token is set (scripts/doctor.py:584). Otherwise the doctor predicts the table from its own shell and says which of the two it did and why. - Which keys. It shows every key a .env file sets, and the shell's keys that the hub's code reads or that carry Nerva's prefixes. The hub's reads are found by reading agents/ and serve.py: helper calls, a bound mapping, \*_ENV constants (private ones too), a pool's from_env names and a descriptor's \*_env keyword (scripts/doctor.py:759). - Which names are printed. A .env name is printed when the hub reads it, .env.example declares it, it is an identifier with Nerva's prefix, or it is a plain one-case name with a value, an empty placeholder included (scripts/doctor.py:1005). Any other name is counted, never printed (withheld_env_names). That includes a name shaped like a digest, a seed or an access key id, whatever follows its "=" (scripts/doctor.py:777); a value that is only = padding; a PEM line; a mixed-case name; and a name with control characters. - Hub mode. On this machine it reads the files the hub names to tell names from value material. For a hub on another machine it shows only the names Nerva knows, and says why. - Other reports. It names a .env that is not UTF-8, which the hub's load fails on (env_not_utf8), and a named pipe it does not open. For each key it prints the .env values a higher layer overrides and the note. Any failure inside the check becomes a named reason, never a crash. - The \`nerva\` CLI's client (agents/cli/client.py:116) follows the same transport rules: no redirect (urllib carried both tokens to wherever one pointed), no proxy to a hub on this machine, and http or https only. Its loopback rule is the doctor's, pinned equal over one table of spellings. It sends the admin token only to a hub on this machine or over https (agents/cli/client.py:156), never in clear text to another host, whether or not a user token is set; the user token goes to the hub it names. When it withheld the admin token and the hub refuses, it names that as one possible cause beside the user token, never as the only one (review-H273g m3). The hint reads the hub's own reason for the tier it wanted: a verb that needs the admin tier asks for JARVIS_ADMIN_TOKEN when only the user token is set, only a token of the wanted tier that was sent is named as refused, a hub with no token of the tier configured is named as such, and the recovery offered is the additive token_recover.py issue (rotate only for a leaked token, since it revokes every token of the tier; review-H273i m2); nerva status reads the same reason on its runnable and e-stop lines (_auth_hint, agents/cli/nerva.py:1038; review-H273h m3, review-H273i m2, n4). - The settings plane: every row says default, set, undeclared, or unreadable (an encrypted secret whose key is lost) (value_source, agents/core/settings_db.py:748). A value a selected product posture puts in effect is named beside the stored one (in_effect, overlay). An unknown stored posture is off, and the posture is read in the listing's own connection; a stored row that is not JSON (the posture included) no longer reads as off: the whole store is validated when it is first opened and before every full listing (_require_readable_store, agents/core/settings_db.py:595), and the listing raises SettingsUnreadable instead (tests/test_h273d_provenance_review.py:739). \`nerva config list\` prints both (agents/cli/nerva.py:1237). - The HUD's Admin "API keys & secrets" list shows each key's layer, the layers it overrides and its note (hydrateAdminKeys, frontend/src/api/live.ts:205; frontend/src/modes3.tsx:261). Hermes records provenance only for vault-supplied names, and its own notes ask for this per-key table; Nerva has it. Nerva has no managed or secret-source layer in the environment: vault secrets are injected at action time, not loaded into the environment. Known limits: - On Windows, key names are compared case-sensitively although the environment is not; that case is theoretical and not handled. - A raw uvicorn start binds where uvicorn's own flags say. JARVIS_HOST there, from a file or from the shell alike, reaches the Host-header guard and the boot guard's bind check, which judges that value rather than the address uvicorn bound. - In a process that loads more than once (tests), a value equal to one an earlier load set keeps that load's attribution. The hub loads once. - JARVIS_USER_HOME set only in a .env, with no JARVIS_HOME, still splits the stores: what the hub opens while it is imported stays under the default root, and the rest follows the home (autonomy.db opens under both). Its note says so on the route, in the doctor and in the HUD. Moving either half would move an existing install's history, so it is left, and set in the process environment it does not split. - The CLI sends the admin token to a hub on another machine when that hub is reached over https: the owner named that hub, and its admin verbs need it. The doctor, which only reads, never sends the admin token off this machine. Over plain http to another machine the admin verbs (the e-stop, approvals, tools, jobs) are refused, and the CLI says why. - A box that never had an admin credential trusts a direct localhost caller as admin, whatever happened to its user tokens: after revoke user --revoke-env, or once a user token has lapsed, a local process still mints a user token. The user-token lock binds callers from other machines; revoke all --revoke-env closes it for this one too (pinned, review-H273g m1). - A run-log path set only in a named-pipe .env reaches the coordinator and the hub, not the supervisor, which cannot read the pipe: its own spawned, child_exited and respawned events go to the default logs/runtime.jsonl, apart from the cycles. Setting the path in the process environment keeps them together. - A token issued with token_store issue and deleted by a revoke without --revoke-env leaves no trace in the store, and so does anything that empties it (purge_expired, which nothing in the hub calls, a deleted tokens.db, a new data root), so that hub reads as never configured for its tier at its next start and trusts a localhost caller again (a running hub that saw the credential stays locked until then). Closing it needs a persistent flag in agents/core/security/token_store.py, the owner's security lane. A rotation, a revoke with --revoke-env, or an expired token keep the hub locked. - A managed user token alone now guards this machine too (ENV-163): an install that has only a store token needs it in the HUD ("store in this browser"), the CLI, the doctor and nerva_mcp_stdio.py. - Under a raw uvicorn start, uvicorn's own proxy knobs (FORWARDED_ALLOW_IPS, UVICORN_PROXY_HEADERS) are read before the app is imported, so a .env value for them is not in effect, while announce_trusted_proxies reports the file's value. - A trailing-dot name (localhost., 127.1.) counts as this machine, though the resolver treats it as a DNS name; a resolver that answered it with another address would receive the admin token. - The value-material shape misses uppercase hex, digitless base32 and short mixed ids, and withholds digit-bearing names with no underscore (contrived lines). - The data home is scaffolded (its README, a .env copied from .env.example) before the boot guards run, so a start they refuse still writes it. - Hub mode on this machine trusts the paths the hub names: a hub in a container names paths that do not exist on the host, and every plain custom key is then withheld with a reason that is false for it. - The scan for the hub's reads misses computed and mapped names (a URL key built from a prefix, a budget key read through a mapping); both are declared in .env.example or carry the prefix today. - JARVIS_HOST=0::0 or ::ffff:0.0.0.0 gives a URL judged not this machine (the proxy is used and the admin token withheld, the safe direction); JARVIS_HOST=localhost:9000 gives an invalid URL, as it did before. This row's admin/listing, validation or transport-auth behavior and remaining limitations are unchanged; its previously current mcp.py pin and explicit coordinates were reviewed. Independent #1233 review (historical scope): Built in #1207, then fixed after eight adversarial reviews. The first found the stdlib parser was python-dotenv's pre-1.2.3 grammar, while the lock pins 1.2.3: the doctor could print value material as key names, a named-pipe .env was no longer loaded, and a data home named in the repo .env was no longer followed. The second found that the doctor sent the admin credential to whatever answered at the hub address, that more keys than serve.py's four were read before any .env was loaded, and that a one-case line of value material could still be printed as a name. The third found that the start itself read 31 more names before the load (so ten .env knobs, the audit key and the public-profile gate among them, were shown as in effect and were not), that two read-again entries were false, and that the MCP transport ignored a user token kept in .env. The fourth found that the MCP transport and the HTTP user guard asked different questions, so a lapsed or revoked user credential locked every route but left MCP open to a local caller; that the coordinator built its Orchestrator before the load, so its audit rows went unkeyed beside the hub's keyed ones; that an IPv6 bind (JARVIS_HOST=::1) escaped both loopback checks; and that the CLI sent the admin token to any hub. The fifth found that the admin tier still trusted a loopback caller once no admin credential was active, so after the owner revoked every credential a local process with no token could mint a fresh user token over HTTP and reopen the user routes and MCP (older than H273, but it falsified this row's credential sentence); that a managed user token that had expired counted as never configured; that the CLI asked the owner to set an admin token it had withheld; and that the supervisor wrote its respawns apart from a run-log named in .env. The sixth found that the sentence about minting did not hold where no admin credential was ever configured, that the offline recovery wrote a tokens.db the hub never read when the data home was named only in a .env (and a packaged build had none to run), that the CLI's withheld message fired on refusals https would not fix, and that a named-pipe .env still split the run-log. The seventh found that the supervisor now told its child a default the hub never read (a named-pipe .env hid the runtime from the brief), that the packaged recovery revived env tokens that had been rotated away or revoked, and that the CLI still asked for a token that was set. The eighth found that the packaged recovery still missed a token in the start environment or a moved data home, and left a LAN-bound app unable to start, and that the new hint called a valid user token refused on an admin verb and proposed a rotate that revoked the owner's working admin token. Every effective configuration key now carries the layer that supplied it, the note says when a .env value is not in effect, and every surface the row names reports names and layers only. The table. load_layered_env (agents/core/env_provenance.py:365) loads the files. Precedence: the process environment (the shell, a systemd EnvironmentFile, docker -e), then the repo .env, then the data-home .env, and the first layer to set a key wins (override=False). It keeps python-dotenv's behaviour: - Each file is read once, whether a regular file or a named pipe, the way python-dotenv reads it. 1Password mounts a .env as a FIFO. - The load is python-dotenv's public load_dotenv on the text that was read. The names come from python-dotenv's own parser (dotenv.parser.parse_stream), which logs nothing, so a bad line is warned about once. No private python-dotenv API is used. - PYTHON_DOTENV_DISABLED is checked before each layer, as python-dotenv checks it on every call, so a repo .env that sets it stops the data-home layer. Its spellings are python-dotenv's own, kept in env_config.py, the repo's one home for env-flag parsing (agents/core/env_config.py:112); a parity test pins them against python-dotenv's own switch. - The data home is a callable resolved after the repo layer is loaded, so a JARVIS_USER_HOME set in the repo .env names it, as before. A first-run home is scaffolded before its .env is read. - A second load in one process keeps a file's attribution only while the environment still holds the value that load set (a private digest, never the value), and works out afresh what the files shadow. The same file as both layers is read once. - It records which layer supplied each key, by diffing the environment around each file, and the lower layers that also define it (shadowed: their value is ignored). That answers "why is my .env change not applied?". - files() records what the load did with each file: its kind (file, fifo, absent, the same file as the repo .env, or disabled), whether it is present, and whether it was read. provenance() (agents/core/env_provenance.py:541) is the queryable in-process table; a key that appeared after the load reads as set while running. The hub loads first. load_hub_env (agents/core/env_provenance.py:463) is the hub's own load, once per process, so a named pipe is read once: - serve.py calls it before it builds the server and runs its guards (serve.py:345). The server's host, port, log level and shutdown timeout, the posture guards and the bind guard see a .env value, so a token in .env satisfies the bind guard. - The lifespan calls it before its boot guards (agents/web.py:476). The data home, logging, the orchestrator with its audit log, memory and budget ledger, and the router's detect() all read after it: the audit key, the public-profile seed gate, turn embeddings, the budget, the router's URLs and cloud keys in a .env are in effect. The boot guards, the front door among them, judge the loaded environment, so the late re-check was removed. - The coordinator (the systemd jarvis-runtime unit, compose runtime-coordinator) calls it first in run(), before its run-log path and cycle (scripts/coordinator.py:173), and again, idempotently, before it builds its Orchestrator (scripts/coordinator.py:84): it shares the hub's data root, so it keys the audit chain the hub keys. The supervisor that spawns it (scripts/runtime_supervisor.py) does not load, since its child would then read every file key as the process environment's; it reads the run-log path through hub_value (agents/core/env_provenance.py:490), the value the files give without loading them, and it hands its child only a path it found (the process, or a regular .env), which the child's load does not override, so both write that one run-log (scripts/runtime_supervisor.py:84; review-H273g m4). A path in a named-pipe .env, which the supervisor never reads, is not handed down: the child reads the pipe as the hub does, so the cycles land where the brief reads them, and only the supervisor's own events stay in the default file (_child_env, scripts/runtime_supervisor.py:122; review-H273h m1). An empty value is unset on both ends. The reality-evidence harness does too (agents/core/observability/reality_evidence.py:183). - agents/run.py, the REPL, loads before its logging and its imports (agents/run.py:21), so a log file or scanner pattern in .env is in effect. - PluginManager.build asks for it too (agents/core/plugin_manager.py:254), for any other entry. scripts/install_smoke.py does not load before it builds its isolated hub (a temp data root, from the process environment); its PluginManager.build loads afterwards, as for any entry. - Log redaction is imported first, so its switch stays the boot environment's alone: a .env cannot turn it off. Keys read before the load. note_for (agents/core/env_provenance.py:526) flags what is still read before any file can be. That is what importing agents.web freezes or resolves: the ASGI root path, the rate limit, CORS, CSP, the router's auto-deep switch, the analytics cap, the graph's Neo4j defaults, the app and data roots, and the log-redaction switch (agents/core/env_provenance.py:60). A .env value for them is recorded but not in effect, and the note says to set it in the process environment. - What locates the hub's own files (JARVIS_APP_ROOT, JARVIS_HOME, JARVIS_MEMORY_DIR) is never taken from a file (agents/core/env_provenance.py:69). A .env value would have split the stores between two roots. It is recorded and kept out of the environment, and its own note says so (agents/core/env_provenance.py:100). - JARVIS_USER_HOME from the repo .env names the data home and its .env. When JARVIS_HOME is not set, the stores opened while the hub was imported stay under the default root, and its note says so (agents/core/env_provenance.py:72). - Read again after the load, so a .env value is in effect (agents/core/env_provenance.py:93): DEV_MODE; the admin and user tokens (every guard reads them per request, the MCP transport included); the OAuth client ids; the trusted proxies. The lists are measured, not declared: - A test spies on the environment in a subprocess across the import and the whole start up to the load, with the data root set either way. Every Nerva name read there must be listed, and every listed name must be read there. - A second spy runs the start and a few requests. Every read-again name must be read after the load, and no name listed as read before the load may be (tests/test_h273d_provenance_review.py:667). The two false read-again entries are fixed: - The MCP transport, the HTTP user guard and the MCP identity check ask one predicate, _user_credential_required (agents/web.py:293; agents/core/routers/mcp.py:419). A token from .env guards MCP on this machine and lets a remote client in. The question is whether a credential was ever configured (_ever_configured, agents/web.py:109): an env token, active or superseded; a rotation or a revoke with --revoke-env, which leave the store's persistent flag; an issued token, live or expired. Such a credential that has lapsed, been rotated away or been revoked locks MCP exactly as it locks HTTP. The admin guard asks the same question for its tier (_admin_configured, agents/web.py:137), and so does the owner flag on /chat, so where an admin credential was ever configured and every credential is revoked or has expired, no local process mints its way back in over HTTP. Recovery is scripts/token_recover.py rotate admin on the box, which loads the hub's .env files first so it writes the tokens.db the hub reads, and says which (review-H273g m2); a packaged build first removes every JARVIS_ADMIN_TOKEN and JARVIS_USER_TOKEN from both places the app reads them, the data home's .env (wherever the home is) and the environment the app starts from, unsets JARVIS_HOST for the restart (the boot guard refuses a LAN bind with no token), then removes security/tokens.db under its data root (JARVIS_HOME and JARVIS_MEMORY_DIR named), because that file is also what records the rotations and revokes that superseded env tokens (docs/PACKAGING.md; review-H273h m2, review-H273i m1). The check lists the token table once per store: once a tier shows configured it stays so for that store (review-H273g n1). Only a hub that never had a credential of the tier trusts a localhost caller without one (for the exception, see Known limits). - The OAuth routes use the plugin manager's copy of the OAuth module (agents/core/routers/oauth.py:36), which re-reads the client ids after the load. Key names come from python-dotenv itself whenever it can be imported (text_keys, agents/core/env_provenance.py:202): every binding in file order, a rebound key each time. The stdlib port (_port_keys, agents/core/env_provenance.py:143) is 1.2.3's grammar and is the fallback for a broken install. A parity test pins it on 25 edge cases, including the BOM, escaped backslashes and a key rebound without "=". A seeded differential fuzz of 4,000 random files pins it too. derive (agents/core/env_provenance.py:327) builds the same table offline. It follows a data home named in the repo .env, or built from ${VAR}, resolving every binding in file order as load_dotenv does: the environment wins over the file's earlier values, a rebound key takes its last value, and a last binding without "=" sets nothing (agents/core/env_provenance.py:294). It parses each file once, keyed on its size, times and inode, and never opens a named pipe. Each key comes with its layer, a label, the layers it overrides, whether /api/admin/env masks its value, and its note. It sends the admin token only to a hub on this machine or over https (agents/cli/client.py:156), never in clear text to another host, whether or not a user token is set; the user token goes to the hub it names. When it withheld the admin token and the hub refuses, it names that as one possible cause beside the user token, never as the only one (review-H273g m3). The hint reads the hub's own reason for the tier it wanted: a verb that needs the admin tier asks for JARVIS_ADMIN_TOKEN when only the user token is set, only a token of the wanted tier that was sent is named as refused, a hub with no token of the tier configured is named as such, and the recovery offered is the additive token_recover.py issue (rotate only for a leaked token, since it revokes every token of the tier; review-H273i m2); nerva status reads the same reason on its runnable and e-stop lines (_auth_hint, agents/cli/nerva.py:1048; review-H273h m3, review-H273i m2, n4). - The settings plane: every row says default, set, undeclared, or unreadable (an encrypted secret whose key is lost) (value_source, agents/core/settings_db.py:750). A value a selected product posture puts in effect is named beside the stored one (in_effect, overlay). An unknown stored posture is off, and the posture is read in the listing's own connection; a stored row that is not JSON (the posture included) no longer reads as off: the whole store is validated when it is first opened and before every full listing (_require_readable_store, agents/core/settings_db.py:595), and the listing raises SettingsUnreadable instead (tests/test_h273d_provenance_review.py:739). \`nerva config list\` prints both (agents/cli/nerva.py:1247). - The HUD's Admin "API keys & secrets" list shows each key's layer, the layers it overrides and its note (hydrateAdminKeys, frontend/src/api/live.ts:205; frontend/src/modes3.tsx:261). Hermes records provenance only for vault-supplied names, and its own notes ask for this per-key table; Nerva has it. Nerva has no managed or secret-source layer in the environment: vault secrets are injected at action time, not loaded into the environment. Known limits: - On Windows, key names are compared case-sensitively although the environment is not; that case is theoretical and not handled. - A raw uvicorn start binds where uvicorn's own flags say. JARVIS_HOST there, from a file or from the shell alike, reaches the Host-header guard and the boot guard's bind check, which judges that value rather than the address uvicorn bound. - In a process that loads more than once (tests), a value equal to one an earlier load set keeps that load's attribution. The hub loads once. - JARVIS_USER_HOME set only in a .env, with no JARVIS_HOME, still splits the stores: what the hub opens while it is imported stays under the default root, and the rest follows the home (autonomy.db opens under both). Its note says so on the route, in the doctor and in the HUD. Moving either half would move an existing install's history, so it is left, and set in the process environment it does not split. - The CLI sends the admin token to a hub on another machine when that hub is reached over https: the owner named that hub, and its admin verbs need it. The doctor, which only reads, never sends the admin token off this machine. Over plain http to another machine the admin verbs (the e-stop, approvals, tools, jobs) are refused, and the CLI says why. - A box that never had an admin credential trusts a direct localhost caller as admin, whatever happened to its user tokens: after revoke user --revoke-env, or once a user token has lapsed, a local process still mints a user token. The user-token lock binds callers from other machines; revoke all --revoke-env closes it for this one too (pinned, review-H273g m1). - A run-log path set only in a named-pipe .env reaches the coordinator and the hub, not the supervisor, which cannot read the pipe: its own spawned, child_exited and respawned events go to the default logs/runtime.jsonl, apart from the cycles. Setting the path in the process environment keeps them together. - A token issued with token_store issue and deleted by a revoke without --revoke-env leaves no trace in the store, and so does anything that empties it (purge_expired, which nothing in the hub calls, a deleted tokens.db, a new data root), so that hub reads as never configured for its tier at its next start and trusts a localhost caller again (a running hub that saw the credential stays locked until then). Closing it needs a persistent flag in agents/core/security/token_store.py, the owner's security lane. A rotation, a revoke with --revoke-env, or an expired token keep the hub locked. - A managed user token alone now guards this machine too (ENV-163): an install that has only a store token needs it in the HUD ("store in this browser"), the CLI, the doctor and nerva_mcp_stdio.py. - Under a raw uvicorn start, uvicorn's own proxy knobs (FORWARDED_ALLOW_IPS, UVICORN_PROXY_HEADERS) are read before the app is imported, so a .env value for them is not in effect, while announce_trusted_proxies reports the file's value. - A trailing-dot name (localhost., 127.1.) counts as this machine, though the resolver treats it as a DNS name; a resolver that answered it with another address would receive the admin token. - The value-material shape misses uppercase hex, digitless base32 and short mixed ids, and withholds digit-bearing names with no underscore (contrived lines). - The data home is scaffolded (its README, a .env copied from .env.example) before the boot guards run, so a start they refuse still writes it. - Hub mode on this machine trusts the paths the hub names: a hub in a container names paths that do not exist on the host, and every plain custom key is then withheld with a reason that is false for it. - The scan for the hub's reads misses computed and mapped names (a URL key built from a prefix, a budget key read through a mapping); both are declared in .env.example or carry the prefix today. - JARVIS_HOST=0::0 or ::ffff:0.0.0.0 gives a URL judged not this machine (the proxy is used and the admin token withheld, the safe direction); JARVIS_HOST=localhost:9000 gives an invalid URL, as it did before. The runtime (scripts/runtime_supervisor.py, which passes it to scripts/coordinator.py) takes --safe-mode too, since it runs heartbeats, owner jobs and agents on the same data root; deploy/systemd/README.md says to set JARVIS_SAFE_MODE=1 in the env file both units read and restart both. It leaves out the owner's layers (16 since H490, H594, H613, H464c, whose \`company_mode\` layer leaves the company-mode sweep out, and H592, whose \`personality_overlays\` layer keeps every /personality style overlay out of a turn (agents/core/cognition/personality_presets.py:270); LAYERS, agents/core/safe_mode.py:68). Plugin grants: JARVIS_PLUGIN_GRANTS, which only ever widens access under least privilege, is ignored (agents/core/plugin_gate.py:665). It covers container (JARVIS_CONTAINER override, Kubernetes, marker files and PID 1 cgroup, /run/systemd/container, $container), WSL, Termux, supervisor (s6, systemd with journal and watchdog, launchd), terminal and multiplexer as closed words, and a hashed machine id, which closes the gap the earlier remaining text named. _kind_word (agents/core/host_identity.py:212) maps only container-manager words to a kind, so 'wsl', 'proot' or any other word in /run/systemd/container or $container is not a container; detect_wsl (agents/core/host_identity.py:253) reads 'wsl' there as the WSL fact, so a WSL 2 host running systemd is reported as wsl2, not as a container. JARVIS_CONTAINER takes the env_config falsy spellings (and 'none') as not a container and ignores unknown words (agents/core/host_identity.py:225-228). WATCHDOG_USEC/WATCHDOG_PID digits are bounded by _decimal (agents/core/host_identity.py:298), and COLORFGBG is parsed with the same bounded ASCII _decimal (agents/core/host_identity.py:416-417), so a superscript digit or a 5000-digit string gives an unknown background and nothing else changes. detect() (agents/core/host_identity.py:478) isolates the terminal, machine-id, WSL and Termux facts through _isolated (agents/core/host_identity.py:469-474), which logs the exception type, so one bad cosmetic field never drops the container or supervisor facts. identity() (agents/core/host_identity.py:507-514) logs the exception type on a detector failure and returns HostIdentity(detected=False), which to_dict reports as {detected: false, reason: identity_failed} (agents/core/host_identity.py:179-181). notify_address (agents/core/host_identity.py:304) is the one NOTIFY_SOCKET parser, shared by sd_notify._address (agents/core/sd_notify.py:59-62) and detect_supervisor (agents/core/host_identity.py:341). Six declared settings rows (agents/core/settings_db.py:487-492), category \`loadset\`, hold comma lists: skills_disabled/skills_only, plugins_disabled/plugins_only, mcp_disabled/mcp_only, editable from the settings page and \`nerva config set\` (which says a loadset.\* key or a plugin switch applies at the next start). A disabled name does not load; a non-empty only-list loads only what it names; the disabled list wins (permits, agents/core/load_set.py:96). A list is read at call time (declared, agents/core/load_set.py:74), trimmed, de-duplicated and bounded to 256 names of at most 128 characters without control characters (parse_names, agents/core/load_set.py:43), and an unreadable store narrows nothing. For plugins the settings page's existing per-plugin \`plugins.\<id\>\` switches, which nothing used to read, count too: an explicit off is off (agents/core/load_set.py:84). SkillLoader.discover reads the lists once per pass (agents/core/skills/loader.py:710-711) and a skill named by its registry name or its folder is not registered at all, before any quarantine row (agents/core/skills/loader.py:789); a registration from an earlier pass is taken out when a later pass denies it, the per-pass snapshot is cleared in a finally, and in safe mode (the owner folder unread) no declared name is reported as unknown. PermissionGate switches off the plugins the lists name when it is built (apply_load_set, agents/core/plugin_gate.py:699), and PluginManager.build drops them from orch.plugins before binding oracle_bridge and Argus (_drop_switched_off, agents/core/plugin_manager.py:368), so the probes and the dashboard never reach a switched-off plugin. Each gate holds its own copies of the built-in manifests (agents/core/plugin_gate.py:693), so switching one off never reaches the module table or another gate, and the readers of a plugin's enabled state ask the live gate: CloudImageRuntime is wired with orch.permission_gate (_available, agents/core/cloud_image_runtime.py:542) and the capability board reads the gate's manifests (_plugin_records, agents/core/observability/capability_registry.py:155). The plugin toggle (toggle_plugin, agents/core/routers/plugins.py:99) keeps the choice in one place, the plugin's plugins.\<id\> settings switch when it has one and otherwise plugins_disabled; switched on, it leaves plugins_disabled and joins a declared plugins_only (persist_plugin, agents/core/load_set.py:140). It reads the lists fail-closed (read_setting), so an unreadable store is not overwritten, and answers \`persisted\` (false when the store refused or could not be read, the live toggle standing). It writes a SETTINGS_CHANGE audit row naming the keys, and a re-enable that cannot be audited is switched back off and answers 503 audit_failed. The MCP load registers only the permitted saved servers (agents/web.py:2062-2069); a switched-off one is held (_MCP_HELD, agents/web.py:2039) and written back unchanged by every save, so the saved configuration never loses it, and adding a server of that name or removing it answers 409 \`switched_off\` naming the list (_held_refusal, agents/core/routers/mcp.py:159). The lists only narrow: nothing is installed, approved, registered or written to the approval store, and a declared name that matches nothing installed is reported as unknown (finish, agents/core/load_set.py:121). The status rows carry it: /skills (agents/core/routers/skills.py:81), /plugins (agents/core/routers/plugins.py:88) and /api/admin/mcp (agents/core/routers/mcp.py:132) return \`load_set\` with the declared lists, what was switched off and what is unknown (status, agents/core/load_set.py:132). Safe mode (H275) applies first; the load set narrows further. tests/test_h285_load_set.py (49 cases, plus one in tests/test_cloud_image.py) covers the parsing and its bounds, the six declared rows, the permit table, an unreadable store, a disabled skill and an only-list with their status rows and unknown names, a skill named by its folder, a named-but-absent skill installing or approving nothing (asserted on a private approval store), the skills route, MCP servers switched off and still saved, an MCP only-list, the add and remove refusals for a held server, adding and removing other servers keeping the held one, the MCP list route, the gate's disabled and only lists, the settings-page switch and that only an explicit off counts, that the lists never enable or register, the toggle kept across a restart both ways, a plugin without a settings switch, enabling under an only-list, a toggle the store refuses, and the plugins route. 33 mutants over the parser, the permit table, the persistence, the three loaders, the refusals and the status rows: all caught (two after their cases were added: an explicit off, a refused write). Test manual: ENV-169, ENV-170. Adapted from Hermes: the lists live in the settings store Nerva already persists and edits rather than a YAML file, the plugin toggle writes them, and an MCP server switched off is kept in the saved list rather than dropped. | <a id="h288"></a>H288 | Scheduled and queued work, and its delivery destination | update | Echivalent | Reevaluat | The three cron gaps that kept this row partial are now closed. The two Kanban ideas the row said to take (a claim lease with a TTL, and a crash-grace window that never replays an authorized action) were already shipped and still hold. \*\*Plain cron runs have a wall clock.\*\* \`jobs.run_timeout_seconds\` (default 900, max 86400) is defined at agents/core/autonomy/jobs.py:69-81. Matching Hermes' HERMES_CRON_TIMEOUT, 0 means unbounded. \`_fire_once\` runs the whole ask/brief/remind action, delivery included, through \`_bounded_execute\` (jobs.py:1810). That method reads the setting (jobs.py:1830-1839) and wraps the run in \`asyncio.timeout\`. When the run's own deadline expires it raises \`JobRunTimeout\`; a timeout raised inside the run keeps its own message (jobs.py:1841-1852). An overrun is recorded through \`_failed\`, so the three-strike pause and the incident still apply. Each channel send has its own 30 s \`wait_for\` and marks \`last_delivery_status\` failed on timeout (jobs.py:2130-2145). The setting is seeded at agents/core/settings_db.py:394 and validated at 0..86400 at settings_db.py:1063-1064. Tests: - tests/test_h288_cron_timeouts.py:140-163: an overrunning run fails with JobRunTimeout and pauses after three strikes. - :125: a hung send is a failed delivery. - :167: an inner timeout is not mislabelled as the run deadline. - :101-121: 0 arms no deadline. \*\*Queued tasks have a finite budget by default.\*\* \`resolve_task_budget\` (agents/core/autonomy/executor.py:39-55) uses a positive JARVIS_TASK_MAX_SECONDS first, then the validated \`autonomy.task_max_seconds\` setting (default 1800, below the 3600 s reaper TTL; settings_db.py:504, validated at 1..86400 at settings_db.py:1065-1066), then the default. It never returns None. \`build_executor\` passes that budget into TaskExecutor and warns when the budget is not below \`autonomy.running_ttl_seconds\` (agents/core/autonomy_coordinator.py:2100-2121). \`execute\` applies \`budget_for(kind)\` with \`wait_for\` and returns \`wall_time_budget_exceeded\` on overrun (executor.py:177-200). The Kanban worker is registered \`self_bounded=True\` (autonomy_coordinator.py:2127-2135; register/budget_for at executor.py:95-114), so the card's own \`max_runtime_seconds\` decides its outcome. A TimeoutError raised by the handler itself is re-raised (executor.py:192). Tests: - tests/test_h288_cron_timeouts.py:202 and :215: the setting is seeded, validated and finite by default. - tests/test_h288_cron_timeouts.py:230: the built executor ships the finite budget. - tests/test_h288_kanban_budget.py:33-61: the Kanban kind is exempt while ordinary kinds stay bounded. - tests/test_h288_kanban_budget.py:128-149 and :145-173: with a real dispatcher, a card capped above the budget finishes done, and a card's own 1 s cap records TimeoutError on the board run rather than an executor cancel. \*\*jobs.db waits for a busy writer.\*\* The jobs store opens sqlite with \`timeout=30.0\` and \`PRAGMA busy_timeout=30000\` (jobs.py:790-793), the same values as the task queue (agents/core/autonomy/queue.py:403-405). Test: tests/test_h288_cron_timeouts.py:260-261. \*\*Lease, crash grace and no replay still hold.\*\* \`autonomy.running_ttl_seconds\` (settings_db.py:502, default 3600) is resynced on every tick (autonomy_coordinator.py:607-611). \`TaskQueue.reap_stuck_running\` (queue.py:5064-5094) fails a stranded RUNNING row with \`stuck_running_ttl\` and never re-queues it. \`AutonomyWorker._reap_stuck\` (agents/core/autonomy/worker.py:1025-1039) runs it at the start of each tick, even under a halt (worker.py:1685-1694). Tested by tests/test_q6_autonomy_killswitch_scope_reaper.py:91-139. In the jobs lane, a claimed request that was interrupted becomes \`unknown\` with "not replayed" (agents/core/autonomy/jobs_dispatch.py:203-209), tested by tests/test_job_dispatch.py:130. The row's rationale excludes the delivery-destination knobs, which per-job \`channel\`/\`deliver\` plus the owner chat id already cover. The ~14-knob Kanban board is a separate product lane, not part of this row. Re-run at this worktree: the H288, reaper, job-dispatch and executor-budget test files give 52 passed, 0 failed. | <a id="h297"></a>H297 | Execute a named tool call and return a bounded, well-formed result | keep | Echivalent | Reevaluat | Final review at HEAD 57ed6db (branch codex/hermes-progress-20261010). Both gaps in the ledger entry are closed on this branch. Contract that was already in place: - ToolRPCServer.handle (agents/core/tool_rpc.py:724) never raises. Unknown tools, bad arguments and denials come back as {ok:false, reason} dicts. - A successful result is cleaned of secrets and invisible characters before it is returned (agents/core/tool_rpc.py:917). - The agent runtime turns any result that is not strict JSON into a non_json_result error (agents/core/agent_runtime.py:1863, agents/core/agent_runtime.py:2271). - Oversized results go through the bounded spill/truncation envelope (agents/core/agent_runtime.py:1903-1908). Gap 1, bounded error text: closed. - A handler exception now comes back as reason tool_error plus an "error" field (agents/core/tool_rpc.py:906-909). The same happens on the approved-execute path (agents/core/tool_rpc.py:1000-1003). - That field is built by sanitize_error (agents/core/tool_rpc.py:349-380). It gives the exception type and message on one line, removes control and invisible characters, redacts known secret patterns with SecretScanner and the broker's own values, then cuts the line to MAX_ERROR_CHARS = 240 (agents/core/tool_rpc.py:221). It never includes a traceback. - A saturated worker pool for plain-function handlers is answered as tool_busy (agents/core/tool_rpc.py:903-904). - Hermes allows 2048 characters; Nerva caps at 240. That is tighter, not a gap. Gap 2, multimodal result envelope: closed. - A handler can return ToolContent, an ordered list of text and image parts (agents/core/tool_rpc.py:247). - _content_envelope (agents/core/tool_rpc.py:1148-1173) validates the parts and returns {ok, tool, result, content}. Text parts are scrubbed. A malformed part is refused as invalid_result. - Parts are bounded: at most 16 parts and 4 images, and each image at most 5,000,000 base64 characters (agents/core/tool_rpc.py:223-229). Each image's leading bytes must match a declared PNG, JPEG, GIF or WEBP type (agents/core/tool_rpc.py:240-245). - In the runtime, _split_images (agents/core/agent_runtime.py:2224) moves the image bytes out of the JSON the model reads and leaves a short descriptor in their place. The images ride beside the tool message only when the backend can read images, and the message then says the images are data, not instructions (agents/core/agent_runtime.py:1040-1046). - The Anthropic dialect sends them as image blocks inside the tool result (agents/core/llm/tool_dialects.py:375-381). - A real producer exists in production code: file_tools._read_image returns ToolContent (agents/core/file_tools.py:1982). - Round 4 hardening: - Only an HTTP 400 or 413 marks a turn as provider_rejected (agents/core/llm/anthropic.py:57, agents/core/llm/anthropic.py:381-382). Only that signal makes the tool loop detach every image and resend once (agents/core/agent_runtime.py:922-943). A 429, 5xx, 529, auth failure or timeout keeps the images attached. - A job pinned to one model counts each image at a flat IMAGE_TOKEN_COST = 1,600 tokens instead of its base64 length (agents/core/llm/tokenizer.py:19, agents/core/llm/job_selection.py:88, agents/core/llm/job_selection.py:128). Review history: the row passed two adversarial skeptics and was cherry-picked onto HEAD. The skipped fixes are recorded with reasons: matching on the wording of a 400 error, and retrying a transient error automatically. Honest limits: - The image tests run against a mocked HTTP transport, never the live Anthropic API. - A plain-function handler that times out cannot be interrupted. It keeps its worker thread until it returns, and the docstring says so. Test runs: tests/test_tool_rpc_h20_1.py, tests/test_tool_rpc_h297_envelope.py, tests/test_h297_bounded_images.py and tests/test_h297_production_images.py were run twice with a fresh JARVIS_HOME each time. | <a id="h303"></a>H303 | Read files and search a codebase | update | Parțial | Reevaluat | Document extraction beyond .pdf and .docx is not built: no .xlsx, .pptx or other extractor exists, and DOC_EXTS and the parser table list only those two (agents/core/local_docs.py:28, agents/core/file_tools.py:200-201). The Hermes row names 'PDF/docx/…' and the gap stays open. Honest limits of what is built: (1) regex search is Python \`re\`, not ripgrep, so ripgrep's linear-time completion is not available: a catastrophic-backtracking pattern that CPython cannot finish, and that the static (a+)+ guard does not catch such as (a\|aa)+$, stops at the 10 second deadline with stopped_by=deadline and returns only the rows of files whose search finished; regex semantics (\\w \\b \\s, Unicode classes, no PCRE or POSIX features) are Python's, and flavour-dependent constructs are refused rather than translated. (2) With no Python interpreter to start (a frozen build) regex=true returns regex_unavailable; literal and glob search still work. (3) .gitignore handling is the cheap subset: only the searched root's own .gitignore is read, only plain directory names or paths (wildcard lines are ignored), and any '!' line disables it entirely; the fixed NOISE_DIRS list is still pruned. (4) One directory holding millions of entries is still listed in full by os.walk before the entry, file and deadline caps run, so the caps bound the walk between directories, not inside one. (5) Content search skips files larger than max_bytes (default 2,000,000) and binaries, matches a literal on only the first 8 KiB of each line, and returns bounded snippets with path and line (no context lines); the result is bounded by match counts (at most 500 rows, 20 per file), not by a configurable character budget like Hermes's max_result_size_chars. (6) Line numbers are opt-in (line_numbers=true), not the default of every read, and are not applied to byte pages or images. | <a id="h310"></a>H310 | Search the web and read pages | update | Echivalent | Reevaluat | web_search and web_extract at the accepted Hermes contract, with the last blocker fixed so the claim is true in the real tool loop. AgentToolRuntime cuts every tool at 30 s (agent_runtime.py:278, :1460-1472) and register_tool has no per-tool budget, so web_extract carries its own call-level budget (web_tools.py:117-118: 22 s soft, 26 s hard; read_one at :946; the soft deadline reaches WebSearchPlugin.read_page(deadline=) at websearch.py:433 and _read_pdf at :557). PDFs queue two at a time (PDF_MAX_CONCURRENT=2, per-event-loop asyncio.Semaphore, thread BoundedSemaphore backstop) but only inside that budget: a PDF that does not fit answers parser_busy with a retry hint, a read still running at 26 s answers fetch_failed with a hint, and every page finished by then is returned. Five ordinary PDFs all read; five very large ones read the first few and answer the rest parser_busy, never tool_timeout. Proven through the real AgentToolRuntime._execute_rpc with the wall scaled down (test_five_slow_pdfs_answer_every_url_before_the_loop_cuts_the_call_off, test_a_hung_page_..., test_a_pdf_that_cannot_finish_in_the_budget_..., test_a_web_extract_call_answers_inside_the_tool_loops_own_wall, which reads the loop's default from its signature). A caller with no deadline (gatherer, scripts) keeps 90 s queue wait and 30 s parse. docs/WEB_SEARCH.md no longer claims a 90 s wait inside a call. A name that does not resolve now answers url_refused exactly like a private address, so a prompt-injected caller cannot probe which internal names exist (test_a_name_that_does_not_resolve_reads_like_a_private_address; the log keeps the difference). HTTP 408/425/429/5xx and timeouts are fetch_failed (retry); every other error status is the new reason http_error with status (do not retry), checked before the media type (test_permanent_http_errors_are_not_retryable_and_transient_ones_are). Unchanged and still tested: provider ABC and registry, no keyless rescue for unattended callers, narrow provider view, 15,000-char head+tail cut, five URLs per call, full text spilled with a footer that names file_read only when reachable, untrusted_output and taint, secret_in_url, tainted_turn, site_blocked, ungated registration, no x_search. ACCEPTED NARROWINGS, to be recorded as narrowings and not as exact equivalence: (1) the backend selector is the env var JARVIS_WEB_BACKEND (plus JARVIS_WEB_PROVIDER_TIER, JARVIS_WEB_RESCUE, JARVIS_WEB_BLOCKED_DOMAINS), not a runtime web.backend setting; changing it takes an environment edit, with no HUD toggle; (2) web_search declares 50,000 bytes (web_tools.py:109, :1023) and only web_extract declares 100,000 (:1034), and web_search rows are fitted to its ceiling with the dropped count in omitted; (3) the ceiling is bytes where Hermes counts chars, and the loop may still lower it to a small model's per-result budget; (4) llm.tool_loop_enabled ships default off, so the tools reach the model only after the owner turns it on (CHT-122); (5) kernel mediation of egress is opt-in (JARVIS_ACTION_KERNEL); (6) the registry takes first-party plugins only. KNOWN LIMITS, not built: one page hung inside pypdf cannot be interrupted from Python (two such hangs hold both slots and PDF reads answer parser_busy until they end), and the memory pypdf uses to decompress a stream or extract one page is not bounded by Nerva (the 2 MB cap bounds the download only); both are in docs/WEB_SEARCH.md, and a killable subprocess with a memory rlimit would be the hard bound. NOT LIVE-PROVEN: no keyed Tavily or SearXNG query, no real PDF with pypdf installed (pypdf is in no requirements file), no plugin-registered backend dialled, no real DNS outage, no HUD ask; every leg uses fakes, a fake pypdf module and httpx.MockTransport. Mutation pass from the previous round (93 killed, 0 survived) predates this round's code and was not re-run on the new branches; the new tests cover them directly.
