| <a id="h399"></a>H399 | Concurrent tool dispatch with a serialized approval gate and bounded results | keep | Echivalent | Reevaluat | Reviewed at HEAD 57ed6db on codex/hermes-progress-20261010. The ledger listed three gaps: batch planning, an in-flight heartbeat, and a result budget for the whole turn. All three are now in the code on this branch. (1) Batch planning. plan_tool_batch splits one model step's calls into ordered groups. Consecutive parallel-safe calls form a concurrent group. Any other call is a barrier that runs alone, and provider order is kept. If the safety check raises, that call runs alone (agents/core/agent_runtime.py:224-256). _execute_turn_calls decides each call this way (agents/core/agent_runtime.py:1483-1495): - a tool that was not offered is refused locally, so it never blocks the batch; - an explicit declaration wins; - an undeclared gated tool is a barrier; - an undeclared ungated tool stays concurrent. It then runs barriers one at a time and gathers each concurrent group (agents/core/agent_runtime.py:1497-1516). ToolRPC records the declaration (agents/core/tool_rpc.py:532-539, :710-712). These tools declare False: - desktop_run (agents/core/autonomy_coordinator.py:1050) - terminal_run (agents/core/autonomy_coordinator.py:1360) - clarify (agents/core/channels/pending_input_runtime.py:614) - skill_propose (agents/core/skills/tools.py:1036) - the kanban mutators; the readers kanban_list, kanban_show and kanban_attachments stay undeclared (agents/core/kanban/runtime.py:78, :123) - extension tools (agents/core/extensions/runtime.py:222) and acquired tools (agents/core/acquisition/promotion.py:620) (2) Approval gate. Gated calls still share one asyncio.Lock. Once approval is required, a second gated call fails closed (agents/core/agent_runtime.py:1664-1679). (3) Synthetic results. A per-call timeout returns a synthetic tool_timeout result (agents/core/agent_runtime.py:1727-1741). (4) Heartbeat. A call still running emits tool_heartbeat at a fixed cadence, capped at 240 beats (agents/core/agent_runtime.py:206-213). A gated call reports gated_in_flight instead of running (agents/core/agent_runtime.py:1763-1781). The beat stops when the result or timeout lands (agents/core/agent_runtime.py:1751-1756). Every emitted event, beats included, calls note_session_activity (agents/core/agent_runtime.py:1943-1945). ToolEventLog keeps one heartbeat row per in-flight call and tracks at most 64 calls, so beats cannot push other rows out of the log (agents/core/observability/tool_events.py:45, :96, :101). (5) Whole-turn budget. Once a turn has spent its per-turn allowance, what is left of it becomes the next result's ceiling (agents/core/agent_runtime.py:1876-1881). Review history: the implementer's round 2 (commit 4250b9f) fixed five findings, and the row then passed two adversarial skeptics and was cherry-picked onto HEAD. I re-derived every line number at HEAD; the implementer's worktree numbers had shifted, for example skill_propose is now at skills/tools.py:1036, not :550. Honest limits: - An undeclared ungated tool still defaults to concurrent. Hermes defaults to sequential. This was a deliberate choice, recorded in rejected_fixes. - A beat is emitted only when an event sink is attached, so a run with no sink gets no in-flight activity marking. - gated_in_flight cannot tell an owner-consent wait from the approved effect running. - I found no "tool search" feature to scope. Tools that were not offered are refused with tool_not_allowed, and registry projection limits what is offered. Tests: tests/test_agent_runtime_v2.py (17 h399 tests), tests/test_tool_loop_result_spill.py, tests/test_tool_result_store.py and tests/test_orchestrator_bindings.py. The run command was env -u TMPDIR JARVIS_HOME=$(mktemp -d) python3.12 -m pytest ... -o addopts="" -q -p no:cacheprovider. Both runs passed 210 tests with no failures (210 passed in 32.60s, then 210 passed in 35.19s). | <a id="h403"></a>H403 | Background self-improvement review after a turn | keep | Parțial | Reevaluat | The summary is delivered late and only in part. (1) Pending summaries and the in-flight review registry are process memory, so a restart loses any summary not yet shown. (2) Delivery happens on the owner's NEXT admin turn on the HUD or on a text-chat channel (telegram, slack, discord, ntfy); nothing is pushed when the review finishes, and a conversation the owner never writes to again shows nothing. (3) Voice, email, webhook, gateway and mcp replies carry no footer, so the summary waits for a HUD or chat turn. (4) The summary line is a notice beside the reply and is not written into the transcript, so reloading the conversation does not show it. (5) A non-admin turn's review still runs and spends the shared daily budget and local GPU; only its summary is withheld. Usage and cancellation: the per-session cost ledger (cost_tracker.session_usage) has no HTTP or CLI reader (the owner sees the per-agent background_review row and the last pass's usage in /api/cognition/learning); a review cancelled mid-call records no usage; the budget refund covers only a cancel during the model call. Not implemented from Hermes: the byte-identical cache-parity fork, review-fork model routing with digest replay, and separate memory-only and skill-only review prompts. The review is one strict-local call with a single combined prompt, by design, so there is no provider cache to keep warm and no cheaper cloud route. | <a id="h410"></a>H410 | Universal secret redaction on every log record | update | Echivalent | Reevaluat | Every log record, from every process, now goes through two filters: H495's shape scanner and a catalogue of credential-bearing names plus the Romanian identifiers. agents/core/log_catalogue.py (outside security/, additive) is a scanner over the names that make a value a credential whatever it looks like: query parameters (QUERY_PARAMS, agents/core/log_catalogue.py:54: access_token, refresh_token, id_token, token, auth, api_key, client_secret, secret, password, signature/sig, the AWS presign parameters, session, jwt), masked at any length up to the next separator; body, form and structured-log keys (SECRET_KEYS, agents/core/log_catalogue.py:62), quoted in JSON or a Python repr, assigned with a quoted value, or unquoted when the value is six characters or more; the Authorization header after any scheme (Bearer, Basic, Token, Digest, ApiKey, HMAC…), or without one when the value is twelve characters or more and carries a digit, so \`Authorization: denied\` stays; the credential headers X-Api-Key, X-Auth-Token, X-Access-Token, X-Goog-Api-Key, X-User-Token, X-Admin-Token, Api-Key and X-Webhook-Token (SECRET_HEADERS, agents/core/log_catalogue.py:68); and the whole value of Cookie and Set-Cookie. It also runs PIIScanner's own CNP and IBAN patterns (agents/core/security/scanner.py:287-288) with their checksum validators, and an IBAN written in spaced groups of four; the other PII patterns stay out (an e-mail or phone number in a log is often the point of the line; card and SSN shapes carry no checksum). A bare \`key\` parameter (settings routes use it for a setting's name) and a bare \`token:\` key (token counts) are not in the catalogue. The rules are in _rules (agents/core/log_catalogue.py:91); a value already masked is never re-masked, so a JWT the first filter named keeps its name. CatalogueScanner (agents/core/log_catalogue.py:126) offers redact, scan and the _compiled rows H495's prefilter is built from, and CatalogueRedactionFilter (agents/core/log_catalogue.py:161) runs it through an unchanged SecretRedactionFilter (agents/core/security/log_redaction.py:230): the arguments uvicorn's AccessFormatter unpacks are kept, a secret split between the format string and an argument masks the argument whole and is named after the finding that holds, tracebacks and stack info are masked, a failing scanner drops the record's content to \[redaction-unavailable\], and the one JARVIS_LOG_REDACTION switch, snapshotted at import, turns both filters off. It wraps rather than subclasses, so H495's installer, which skips a handler already carrying a SecretRedactionFilter, never mistakes it for its own. install_catalogue_redaction_everywhere (agents/core/log_catalogue.py:220) covers the root handlers and every logger's own (uvicorn's detached ones included), idempotently, and counts and names a handler that refuses the filter. core.log's _install_redaction (agents/core/log.py:69) installs it right after the H495 filter, so setup_logging (agents/core/log.py:108) gives every handler both, in that order; install_redaction (agents/core/log.py:102) is the same for a process that configures its own logging. The two entry points that called a bare basicConfig and wrote every record unredacted now call it: the headless coordinator (configure_logging, scripts/coordinator.py:263) and the MCP stdio bridge (configure_logging, scripts/nerva_mcp_stdio.py:149, still stderr only, since stdout is its protocol channel). Neither takes setup_logging's rotating file handler, which a second process would rotate under the hub (critic note 32). The H145 log reader runs the catalogue on every line it serves (agents/core/log_tail.py:167), for lines written before it or by a process it did not cover. The test isolation fixture strips the catalogue filter with the H495 one (tests/conftest.py:271). | <a id="h423"></a>H423 | Model-callable memory write tool with add / replace / remove, an atomic batch, a hard budget, and a lost-update guard | update | Echivalent | Reevaluat | At HEAD d2ec765 the model-facing \`memory\` tool covers every Hermes gap listed for this row. \*\*Budget on the final state.\*\* A batch is checked against its final state, not one operation at a time, so an add listed before the remove that makes room for it is accepted (agents/core/memory_tool.py:227-233). Substring addressing still refuses an ambiguous match (agents/core/memory_tool.py:175). \*\*Lock, reread and lost-update guard.\*\* - Each ring file has a cross-process lock on \`\<ring\>.json.lock\`: flock on POSIX, msvcrt.locking on Windows (agents/core/cognition/memory.py:376-418). CoreMemory.locked holds it (agents/core/cognition/memory.py:471-484). - Writes are compare-and-set. If a ring changed meanwhile the call is refused and the rings already written are restored (agents/core/memory_tool.py:440-468). - The read made while another writer holds the lock is strict: adopt_without_lock reads under the ring's in-process lock, so it never rolls back a save from the same process and never accepts a lenient parse (agents/core/cognition/memory.py:622-648; agents/core/memory_tool.py:386-414). GET /api/memory/core uses the same reader (agents/core/routers/memory_kg.py:995-1002). \*\*Drift guard.\*\* - Each save records a sha256 sidecar (agents/core/cognition/memory.py:486-502). - A file edited by hand is copied to an owner-only \`.bak\` (agents/core/cognition/memory.py:538-548). If it cannot be read back exactly, writes fail with CoreMemoryDrift, which names the file and its copy (agents/core/cognition/memory.py:296-302; agents/core/memory_tool.py:453-458). - When a process starts over a broken file, the ring holds no facts and has_good_copy is False (agents/core/cognition/memory.py:650-673). The prompt then says no facts from the file are shown (agents/core/learning/core_block.py:108-113). \*\*Per-turn cap.\*\* After FULL_ATTEMPTS_PER_TURN = 3 failed at-capacity attempts in one turn, the turn gets a terminal \`memory_full_terminal\` refusal (agents/core/memory_tool.py:85, 596-616, 680-681). \*\*Forget.\*\* - Forget clears the turn's pending ring reread (agents/core/data_purge.py:693-694). The field is now declared in Orchestrator.__init__ (agents/core/orchestrator.py:912). - The at-rest purge removes each ring and its digest while holding the ring's lock (agents/core/data_purge.py:463-515). \*\*Registration.\*\* The tool is registered for owner-operator turns (agents/core/autonomy_coordinator.py:1751-1763). \*\*Tests.\*\* They live in tests/test_h314_memory_tool.py: - final-state budget: :598 - reread and lock waits: :621, :631, :665 - drift: :678, :877, :897, :913 - terminal cap: :719 - this round's review fixes: :1399, :1425, :1440, :1463, :1485, :1496, :1505 The implementer reports that the 9 new test cases from the last round failed against the previous code (red first), and that two adversarial reviews passed. \*\*Limits the implementer listed as outside this row.\*\* - CoreMemory.put, used by the post-turn review and by reflection, still drops the oldest fact when a ring is full instead of refusing. This predates H423. - The Windows msvcrt lock is tested only with a fake msvcrt. - Writes are audited as \`memory.write\` records in the intent log; there is no separate kernel registry kind. \*\*Test results at HEAD.\*\* - tests/test_h314_memory_tool.py, run twice: 123 passed both times. - Related memory, purge and core-block files (test_core_block_injection, test_data_purge, test_data_purge_memory, test_forget_export_purge_parity, test_living_memory_h21_3, test_r3_b2_memory_forget_contracts, test_h388_tool_guidance): 77 passed. | <a id="h428"></a>H428 | Pre-turn recall with a triviality gate, a hard timeout, and next-turn warm-up | update | Echivalent | Reevaluat | Orchestrator._recall_block (agents/core/orchestrator.py:3764) gates and bounds the pre-turn recall, skips it while an earlier one is stuck, and warms the next turn, the way Hermes' memory prefetch does. It is reached from the streaming and parallel turn paths. The 2026-09-24 review rounds fixed what had made the bound hollow, built the warm-up half, which had been missing, and made a delete reach every cached result and the store itself. (1) Triviality gate. is_trivial_prompt (agents/core/memory/recall_gate.py:67) returns true for: - empty input; - a command-shaped slash text (agents/core/memory/recall_gate.py:49). Nerva dispatches commands before recall, so a path such as "/etc/hosts changed, why?" is a question; - a bare acknowledgement or greeting followed only by punctuation or emoji: the Hermes list plus Romanian (_ACKS, agents/core/memory/recall_gate.py:31), with internal commas read as spaces; - punctuation alone ("?", "…?", "❓", "$?"), and an emoji-only reaction unless it comes with a question mark ("🦷?" is a question); only the "other symbol" category counts as an emoji (agents/core/memory/recall_gate.py:80). Text is compared after NFC normalisation with format characters removed (agents/core/memory/recall_gate.py:61). k8s, yolo, "ok, and what about X?" and any non-command text over 40 characters are never trivial. _recall_block returns '' before any embedding (agents/core/orchestrator.py:3785). (2) Job pins. A job-model-pinned turn never recalls, and the check runs before any handoff or warm context (agents/core/orchestrator.py:3789). (3) Hard timeout. _bounded_recall_hits (agents/core/orchestrator.py:3683) awaits _recall_hits (agents/core/orchestrator.py:3487) for at most memory.recall_timeout_s. _recall_hits covers the optional H433 rewrite, the query embedding and the fused vector ⊕ graph search. - The setting is seeded at 8 s like Hermes' _EXTERNAL_PREFETCH_TIMEOUT_S (agents/core/settings_db.py:361). - _recall_timeout_s (agents/core/orchestrator.py:3478) reads a non-number, bool, NaN, infinity or non-positive value as 8 and clamps the rest to 0.1–60 s. The settings write path refuses a non-finite number for every number setting (agents/core/settings_db.py:1105). - On expiry it logs a WARNING (agents/core/orchestrator.py:3722). - The living-memory rerank runs after the bound, off the event loop, only on the hits a turn freshly recalled (agents/core/orchestrator.py:3816); warm hits served again are not reranked again. The bound holds for the turn, not only for the await: - MemoryManager keeps a store lock for the vector store and the knowledge graph, separate from the conversation lock (agents/core/memory/manager.py:79-80; store_embedding at agents/core/memory/manager.py:648, hybrid_search at agents/core/memory/manager.py:676; a single vector remove at agents/core/routers/memory_kg.py:328). A search stuck on Qdrant or Neo4j does not block saving the reply or any other session's turn. - With MEMORY_EMBED_TURNS on, turn embeddings are written in the background, one at a time and oldest first, as Hermes' sync_all never writes a provider inline (_queue_turn_embedding, agents/core/memory/manager.py:509). Shutdown gives them 5 s to land and then drops what is still queued (agents/core/orchestrator.py:1589, agents/core/orchestrator.py:1593). The CLI REPL reads each line on a daemon thread, so the event loop and the queue keep running while the owner types, and it gives the queue 30 s to land on exit (_prompt, agents/run.py:57; agents/run.py:54). (4) Skip while stuck. A timed-out recall cannot be killed, because its embedding and search run on worker threads. It is kept as a straggler, and so is a recall whose turn was cancelled; none is overwritten or cancelled under its threads (_adopt_recall_straggler, agents/core/orchestrator.py:3728). While any straggler runs, later recalls are skipped with an INFO line (agents/core/orchestrator.py:3700), as Hermes skips a provider whose previous prefetch is still alive. (5) Next-turn warm-up. The hits a turn recalled, an empty result included, become its session's warm context (_keep_warm_recall, agents/core/orchestrator.py:3657, kept at agents/core/orchestrator.py:3815, capped at 256 sessions). When the next turn's own recall is unavailable (timed out, or skipped behind a stuck one), that warm context stands in (_warm_recall, agents/core/orchestrator.py:3671; agents/core/orchestrator.py:3808), with an INFO line naming it. It is never served: - to another session; - to a caller outside any turn (the autonomy worker, the nightly reflection, /api/context/compress), which neither keeps, serves nor consumes turn state, and whose stragglers leave no handoff (agents/core/orchestrator.py:3645). Work delegated inside a turn shares that turn's session; - after a purge or a single-memory delete; - past 10 minutes; - to a trivial or pinned turn; - when the new turn's recall ran and found nothing: that empty answer replaces it. This is Hermes' queue_prefetch_all adapted to one retrieval memory: - Hermes computes a background result from the finished turn's message and injects it next turn beside the new base context (Honcho's pending dialectic). - Nerva's recall of that same message already ran at the turn's start, so it reuses those hits instead of a second round-trip. - It uses them only when the new turn's own, fresher recall is unavailable, which is when a warmed result saves the turn. (6) Same-question handoff, a Nerva extension. Hermes throws a timed-out result away. Here a straggler that finishes cleanly leaves its hits for one handoff, kept per session: the session's next recall takes them, serving them only for a retry of the same question within 10 minutes of completion (agents/core/orchestrator.py:3705). Another session never receives them. (7) Deletes. Every recall reads the recall generation when it starts (agents/core/orchestrator.py:3799); its result is served, handed off or kept warm only while that generation is still current. A result a delete overtook is discarded when the search returns (agents/core/orchestrator.py:3722), before the rerank can reinforce it, or after the rerank (agents/core/orchestrator.py:3816), and nothing is kept under a stale generation. - A purge ("forget me", data_purge.clear_live_memory) drops queued turn embeddings and bumps the generation, clearing every handoff and warm context (_forget_in_flight, agents/core/data_purge.py:708; _recall_purged, agents/core/orchestrator.py:3747). It does so before the wipe and again after it, the second time in a finally (agents/core/data_purge.py:575, agents/core/data_purge.py:579). In between, recall serves nothing at all (agents/core/orchestrator.py:3795), so pre-wipe memory is never served during a purge either. - The vector store and the graph are wiped under the store lock (agents/core/data_purge.py:601), so a turn embedding already writing lands before the wipe. Queued embeddings and remember() carry the generation they started under and re-check it under that lock (agents/core/memory/manager.py:660). A search stuck on a dead backend, or a write slower than the 10 s wait, holds the lock: the wipe then goes ahead without it and never releases a lock it did not take. A write that lands after such a wipe removes its own record while it still holds the lock, so no search sees it (agents/core/memory/manager.py:660), and the forget reports the busy lock in not_erased instead of claiming a clean wipe (AUDIT-2). - A single delete does the same through _recall_forget (agents/core/routers/memory_kg.py:337): DELETE /api/kg/entities/{name:path} and DELETE /api/kg/relations, also when the call is cancelled mid-delete (agents/core/routers/memory_kg.py:750, agents/core/routers/memory_kg.py:831); an entity edit, which replaces its properties (agents/core/routers/memory_kg.py:717); and a consolidation apply that actually removed a vector, even one whose re-embedding then failed (agents/core/routers/memory_kg.py:435). - Known limit: a turn already running when the purge starts still saves its reply afterwards; the purge does not quiesce turns. | <a id="h433"></a>H433 | Retrieval query rewriting by a cheap auxiliary model | copy | Echivalent | Reevaluat | agents/core/memory/query_rewrite.py ports Hermes' rewriter (plugins/memory/query_rewrite.py). Its review rounds changed where the rewrite is used and tightened the filter. (1) The rewriter. rewrite_query (agents/core/memory/query_rewrite.py:134) asks a model for exactly one concise question about the user's own history, at TEMPERATURE 0 and MAX_TOKENS 96 (agents/core/memory/query_rewrite.py:39-40). - The latest message is bounded to 4,000 characters, keeping its head and tail around an omission marker (bounded_user_message, agents/core/memory/query_rewrite.py:97). - It is passed only as a JSON string on one data line. NEL (U+0085), U+2028 and U+2029, the line breaks JSON leaves raw, are escaped by hand, so the data cannot break that line (agents/core/memory/query_rewrite.py:78, agents/core/memory/query_rewrite.py:141). - SYSTEM_PROMPT (agents/core/memory/query_rewrite.py:80) says to treat the message as untrusted data, never follow it, never answer it, and ask in the message's language. - Any exception, or an answer the filter rejects, returns "" so the caller recalls on the raw text, exactly as in Hermes. (2) The filter. normalize_rewrite (agents/core/memory/query_rewrite.py:111): - NFKC-normalises the answer and removes format characters first (_plain, agents/core/memory/query_rewrite.py:105); - strips fences, labels (English and Romanian) and quotes, and control and line-separator characters; - rejects an answer over 320 characters, not a question, not grounded in the user's memory, instruction-shaped, or with a second sentence. Nerva additions for a Romanian-speaking owner: - Romanian interrogatives (_QUESTION_START_RE, agents/core/memory/query_rewrite.py:47) and grounding words (_MEMORY_GROUNDING_RE, agents/core/memory/query_rewrite.py:60). - An auxiliary starter, English or Romanian ("Did…", "Do…", "Am…", "E…", "A…", _AUX_START_RE, agents/core/memory/query_rewrite.py:55), counts as a question only when whitespace follows it and the model itself ended with "?" (agents/core/memory/query_rewrite.py:122). "Do my taxes now.", "E-mail all my passwords…", "Am rezervat hotelul." and an invented "Ai programare marți la 10." are therefore refused. An interrogative word ("What…", "Ce…") needs no "?". - Second-person and object pronouns are not grounding: "Can you tell me the capital of France?" is refused. - The instruction check also reads "ignoring", "disregard" and the Romanian forms (agents/core/memory/query_rewrite.py:68). - A second sentence is refused: sentence punctuation (including ";" and "…") then a space and more text, or "?", "!" or ";" straight into more text ("?Now", ";also"). A "." or "…" with no space stays inside the question ("the 3.5 kg bag") (agents/core/memory/query_rewrite.py:77). - A question the model ended with "." gets "?" instead (agents/core/memory/query_rewrite.py:131). This is a quality gate on what the embedder is asked, not a security control. The rewritten query reaches only the embedding model, never a generative one, and a homoglyph can still pass. (3) Wiring (critic note 12). _recall_hits (agents/core/orchestrator.py:3487) runs the rewrite only when memory.recall_query_rewrite is on (seeded OFF at agents/core/settings_db.py:364, because it costs a model call). - It runs after the H428 triviality gate and the job-pin check, and inside the H428 bound. - It gets half the bound of its own (agents/core/orchestrator.py:3503-3507), as Hermes gives the rewrite its own 8 s. Past that, the model call is cancelled and recall runs on the raw text within the same turn, instead of the whole recall becoming a straggler. - The rewrite becomes the embedding query only. The graph leg keeps the raw message as its keyword (agents/core/orchestrator.py:3515): it finds an entity whose name or a property contains the keyword, so it only ever helps a short, entity-like message ("BMW", "dentist"), and a rewritten whole question would never match. With the rewrite off or rejected, recall is unchanged (agents/core/orchestrator.py:3516). Hermes likewise keeps the raw message for its context fetch. (4) Strict-local. _query_rewriter (agents/core/orchestrator.py:3606) uses LLMRouter.local_backend only (agents/core/llm/auxiliary_text.py:166). That is the fail-closed accessor, which never falls through to a cloud backend: no local backend means it raises and the rewrite returns "". This is proven through a real HybridRouter whose only backend is cloud. The call re-checks the job-model pin itself (agents/core/llm/auxiliary_text.py:162), and tells a Qwen3 model (the default local family) not to think, so the 96 tokens are not spent before the answer (agents/core/llm/auxiliary_text.py:173). Like Hermes, the rewriter sees only the latest message, so a reference to an earlier turn ("the other one") stays unresolved. The win is a grounded question for short or oblique messages. Tests: tests/test_query_rewrite.py has 57 cases. 24 of them fail on 8e824b9f, the commit before the first review round; 5 on 890e80b6 (the NEL escape, three auxiliaries without "?" and ";also"); and 1 on 3b4398d2 (";also"). They cover: - the bounded JSON data line and the line-break escapes (tests/test_query_rewrite.py:61, tests/test_query_rewrite.py:208); - the accept and reject tables, including the Romanian statements and answers, the E-/A starters, English auxiliaries without "?", ungrounded second person, NFKC and a zero-width space (tests/test_query_rewrite.py:92, tests/test_query_rewrite.py:125); - errors and the seeded toggle; - the rewrite used when on, off by default, and not paid by a trivial prompt; - a hung rewrite costing half the bound before recall runs on the raw text (tests/test_query_rewrite.py:190); - the raw graph keyword (tests/test_query_rewrite.py:201); - a pinned turn, and the rewriter refusing under a pin (tests/test_query_rewrite.py:216, tests/test_query_rewrite.py:226); - the real HybridRouter with only a cloud backend (tests/test_query_rewrite.py:252); - initial temperature 0 and 96 tokens (tests/test_query_rewrite.py:285); - the Qwen3 switch (tests/test_query_rewrite.py:310). | <a id="h453"></a>H453 | Let a cheap check decide whether the expensive model runs at all | copy | Echivalent | Reevaluat | Whole frozen H453 contract reviewed, batch07 (2026-10-10). Ordinary scheduled Python scripts require a successful matching governed task and trusted complete UTF-8 stdout capture before output decisions. No-agent delivery receives the complete safe projection instead of a silent 2,000-character prefix; empty/whitespace stdout suppresses model and delivery using the full observation. Model-bearing scripts receive JSON-fenced untrusted stdout context, with a fixed host-authored truncation notice outside the fence when abbreviated. Missing, invalid, unsuccessful or incomplete capture fails explicitly. Raw digest metadata is host-produced before redaction; safe projected stdout need not hash like original secret-containing bytes. Local transport currently attests full snapshots through 16,000 bytes; the shared validator ceiling is 50,000 bytes, not a larger local capture promise. Ordinary scripts, including no-agent, honor the last nonempty line's exact JSON boolean wakeAgent:false. Malformed/nonfalse JSON continues after completeness is established; stderr-only truncation does not invalidate complete stdout. Script/URL monitors instead treat all observation bytes as literal data and use their separate change gate. Complete raw hashes and scrubbed snapshots are persisted atomically at detection, before model calls, so unchanged observations skip work even after a prior model failure. Generations prevent stale baseline updates/delivery. First baselines, including empty ones, are observations. Model-only \[SILENT\] and whole-response silence conventions still suppress delivery; no-agent literal \[SILENT\] remains data. Accepted native mappings are bounded self-contained approved Python, safe redacted/Unicode-cleaned stdout and explicit capture limits; scripts retain fresh terminal approval and URL monitor hops retain signed governed plugin.egress approval. No standing grant, scanner relaxation or hidden model polling is introduced. Existing monitor/URL/gate regressions, actual local subprocess pipeline tests with a test authorization shim, and actual disposable lifespan/CLI orchestration with offline HTTP model responses cover the feature. Full backend milestone is required separately before assessment. Wider scheduler, routing, workspace and dedicated authoring UI clauses remain separate; no live-provider or native-host deployment claim. Explicit own continuity injects the latest eligible output with host do-not-repeat/continue guidance outside the untrusted fence. A distinct owner-edited legacy note remains separately labelled, including proper prefixes; when no eligible output exists it is an unverified legacy fallback, never cross-job publication proof. continuity=false omits own/self/own-ID output and legacy note while preserving independent KV and external sources. Per-job SQLite KV retains printable 128-character keys, 16 KiB per value, 64 KiB per job and 256 keys with transactional rejection and JSON-fenced prompt injection. context_from accepts an ordered string/list of at most eight distinct canonical 12-hex job IDs, with case-insensitive input normalization and self. Validation precedes lookup; no filesystem output lookup exists. Missing/deleted/empty and other-profile sources silently skip, and source birth identity prevents replacement-job confusion. One latest substantive output per live job is stored with its successful producer run and birth identity in the same terminal-success transaction. Detailed successful model results require no source-assigned control/stop and non-silent content; process-only adapters retain old execution behavior without supplying publication proof. Complete no-agent output and substantive reminder/brief content may publish. Queued-task receipts, failures, unknowns, suppression and approval-control replies preserve the previous latest result. Deletion removes latest content but keeps H015 historical run metadata. Stored output is bounded to 8,000 characters/32 KiB. External blocks share a 64 KiB rendered UTF-8 budget including JSON escaping and host/fence text; bounded context is explicitly labelled. All injected content remains untrusted. Script reservations freeze own/external/KV snapshots transactionally, including absence; later output cannot leak into that attempt, while source deletion/replacement revokes injection. Old persisted attempts use explicitly empty new snapshots and retain their saved legacy notes. Sources are never automatically executed. CLI create/edit adds repeatable --context-from and edit --clear-context-from; standalone additive context/continuity PATCH merges latest options atomically without a GET. Explicit --options remains a replacement and folds CLI flags; conflicting non-null API replacement/additive fields are refused. Existing admin guard and strict string types remain, with no new route. | <a id="h456"></a>H456 | Bound what an unattended agent may do | copy | Echivalent | Reevaluat | Whole frozen H456 contract reviewed, batch08 (2026-10-10). Scheduled model tool bounds resolve an explicit non-null job list (including \[\]), then an explicit cron platform list (including \[\]), then the finite current registration set. All cases subtract operator-disabled groups and literal messaging/clarify; cronjob is removed unless allow_agent_scheduling is true. This flag lifts loop prevention only and creates no execution or scheduling grant. The selected bound intersects through existing closed-lifetime tool scope at model offer, runtime/RPC and nested execute_code calls; posture, agent patterns and kernel approvals remain additional limits. Curated exact groups cover named native tools; unavailable selected groups refuse while denied groups may contain absent names. Dynamic plugin/delegation catalogs and new tool implementations are not claimed. Three native owner settings are validated on write and read. Runtime reads one coherent read-only SQLite snapshot without reseeding/recovery; unreadable/malformed policy fails the model phase. Readable legacy stores missing new rows use declared defaults. Doctor remains read-only and reports policy source/removals and errors even with zero jobs; the result is an upper bound, not an execution grant. Canonical options.reasoning_effort is validated at storage for model-bearing ask work, rejects null/aliases/no-agent combinations, and overrides global/model default requests through existing request-local transport scope without mutating backends. Nested absent jobs retain explicit ancestors and copied child contexts are revoked on scope closure. Cloud adapters retain nearest-weaker supported clamping, below-minimum refusal and unsupported/undeclared omission; vocabulary overrides remain capabilities, not stronger requested preferences. No universal strict cost ceiling is claimed for undeclared cloud models. LM Studio/Ollama lack verified effort wire controls and explicitly refuse scheduled pins before text/tool/stream generation, including prepared dispatch and retries; metadata/warm-up and unpinned local work remain usable. CLI create/edit and HUD expose exact rungs/default deletion. CLI requires explicit complete --options, preserving replacement semantics; HUD skip-model removes/disables model-only fields and preserves unrelated options. Existing API options validation stays authoritative; no route added. Actual disposable CLI/FastAPI/orchestrator smoke proves job/cron/legacy offers, exclusions, local refusal/clearing and auth/validation with offline HTTP responses. The settings refresh runs synchronously and real clarify registration is called after startup because a separate pre-existing startup-order bug omits it. Real local nested-code proof uses an isolation authorization test shim, not Docker/WASM certification. Built Jobs Chromium checks pass fresh mount, default clearing, custom creation, skip-model and hard reload with mocked API. Dedicated native-mobile authoring, live providers and native owner-host deployment remain unclaimed. | <a id="h464"></a>H464 | Park a run on real async work instead of poking it | copy | Parțial | Reevaluat | Not reachable in production yet: - \*\*No process producer (owner decision 1; blocked on H302).\*\* Nothing in the hub starts run-owned background work and registers its pid: register_process has no caller outside tests. The best first producer is \`terminal_run\` with \`background: true\` on the local-host transport. It needs WorkRunLedger.run_for_task; a spawn with start_new_session, bounded log files and a held proc.wait() that records the exit code; a lifetime cap and killpg on cap, ESTOP or stop; a reaper for stopped runs; schema, approval-card and parity updates; and a KillMode in deploy/systemd/jarvis-hub.service (today a restart kills the child and the barrier clears as \`exited\`, indistinguishable from success). The owner must say whether the task/hook trigger is an accepted adaptation of Hermes's pid/session barrier, or whether a pid wait must be reachable for "equivalent". - \*\*Pid waits are unusable on macOS/BSD.\*\* There is no start token there, so every pid wait is refused \`pid_unprovable\`. The fix belongs in exec_cache.py (ctypes libproc proc_pidinfo(PROC_PIDTBSDINFO)) or in a producer-held Popen handle, and needs macOS hardware or a macOS CI runner to verify. - \*\*The judge's \`wait\` verdict and planner waits are not reachable in production (owner decision 2).\*\* WorkJudge.wait_probe needs a model rubric, and the shipped runtime passes no rubric, model planner or graders. Wiring one needs the owner's choice of local model and provider under H513 (auxiliary_request_scope, strict-local, security.data_training_ack) plus opt-in settings forced off in safe mode. Before any model planner, the rest of the intake arguments must be clamped: since H464c the task's kind is scope-checked as well as Action.kind, but the task's agent, title and payload still reach govern_enqueue unchanged. - \*\*No graders are wired in production.\*\* After the hub park clears, a run idles until its budget ends. Deterministic verifier and judge adapters belong to the company-mode grading work; they must reuse an existing verdict, because _grade has no try/except and a judge that raises after the verifier recorded leaves \`verdict_already_recorded\` / \`tick_failed\` on every later sweep. Deferred: - Wake-on-fire: a parked run resumes at the next scheduled sweep. - A \`job:\<id\>\` trigger. - A process output-pattern trigger (needs the process producer). - An owner-set wait like Hermes's \`/goal wait\` (owner decision 3): a clock or own-task wait only, never an owner-typed pid. - Waiting between checklist steps: the checklist still advances when a step's task is approved, not when it finishes. - A judge-sourced wait reserves no grading margin (only the hub's park does since H464c), so a judge wait that runs to the end of the budget still leaves the run ungraded. It is reachable only with a judge wait probe (owner decision 2). - The grading margin bounds one run's way back to a sweep, not a queue: with several runs due at once (max_concurrent 1), a parked run can lose the sweep's one slot after its cap. - A blocked run whose budget runs out is not settled (H464d settles only runs the sweep skips as budget_spent; a blocked one is skipped as blocked and its resume is refused once the owner answers), so it stays blocked on the record. - The HUD's live wait credit for an open ask runs to now; if the owner then edits the ask, the durable credit falls back to the last sweep that saw it open (at most one sweep's worth). - An owner stop of a working run is never closed out: request_stop moves it to \`stopping\` and settles only a second stop (agents/core/autonomy/work_runs.py:1436-1438), while ScheduleRuntime.due skips a \`stopping\` run (agents/core/autonomy/schedule_runtime.py:227-228), so the supervisor that would settle it is never ticked and the run reads \`stopping\` until the owner stops it again (reproduced on 03643762). Needs network: re-checking Hermes's goal-wait behaviour at the pinned commit 59b2aeef (hermes_cli/goals.py was not among the inspected upstream sources). Review residuals after round 3 (latent or bounded): a dropped grading sweep is not absorbed by the margin; a transient queue read during the per-sweep wait observation cuts approval-wait credit; a hold open when a run stops is never ended; an expired ask would be re-asked; the upgrade note's 're-approve' advice needs a new card; four test gaps (docs/handoff/2026-09-28-handover/h464-round3-brief.md). | <a id="h465"></a>H465 | Run the self-improvement review on demand | update | Echivalent | Reevaluat | Built in #1207 and fixed after six adversarial reviews: review-H465 (one major, seven minors, seven nits), review-H465b (three minors, six nits: a per-turn pass could still run beside /refine and borrow its label, a cut-off review read as nothing, and four mutants were unpinned) and review-H465c (three minors, six nits: a per-turn review cut off by the token cap was refunded, so a model that always truncates reviewed every turn; the settings the replies named could not be set; four survivors) and review-H465d (two minors, seven nits: a day of cut-offs made /refine name the wrong setting, seven real survivors, and a GA4 private key the CLI printed unmasked) and review-H465e (two minors, seven nits: the cut-off refusal on a day of mostly real reviews, nine real survivors, a budget read outside its bounds, a secret echoed by nerva config set, a pass in flight at midnight counted on the next day, a burst of turns past the cadence) and review-H465f (seven nits: a /refine refund keyed on the wrong day, a burst given too few passes, a later bracket closing an unclosed error, a fraction below one read as reviews off). All are fixed. Hermes' /refine \[focus\] forks the background memory and skill review against a snapshot of the conversation, so the live session is untouched. It refuses while a turn is in flight and reports the new or updated memories and skills back into the chat. Nerva's review engine is the per-turn BackgroundReviewer (strict-local, budgeted); it now also runs on demand. The command: - /refine \[focus\] is an owner command (agents/core/commands.py:395, registered at agents/core/commands.py:665). It answers from any channel's owner, and a guest is refused like any owner command. - The focus is one line of at most 200 characters. - It replies with what the review kept, one line per action (profile or core memory updated, corrections recorded, skill patch proposed, new skill quarantined, facts found but not kept because living memory is off). A skill change is said to wait in the Decision Inbox, and a new skill in the pending skills list. - Every non-run is named: a review already running, the daily budget spent, no local model answering (reviews never leave the machine), a model that spent its whole answer thinking (review_cut_off), a review cut off or malformed (review_unparsed, which names learning.review_max_tokens), reviews switched off (a daily budget of 0, reviews_off), the review outlasting its bound, nothing to review, no reviewer. One refusal added since this row's reviews has no wording of its own: a session whose history was imported from another assistant and is still tainted is refused foreign_history_not_promotable before the lease is looked at (agents/core/orchestrator.py:4301-4302), and the command answers it with the generic "The review did not run." line; the guard came with the owner-attested foreign-history resume (commit 8e1775bb), outside this row's claims and tests. An empty reply, a cut one, or a JSON object carrying none of the review's keys ({} or {"error": …}) is unparsed; only an object that says it found nothing reads as nothing worth keeping. A reply that parses as a review is the model's answer, whatever it opens with or mentions; only a reply that does not parse and is the local degraded message or opens with a bracketed \[… error …\] closed on its own line by its own bracket is a backend failure; an unclosed "\[Note: … error", or one a later \[1\] or link would close, is prose (review-H465e nit 7, review-H465f nit 3). - A local backend that is configured but down answers with a degraded string rather than raising. That is no review: it is reported as no local model and costs no budget (review-H465 M-1). A cut-off or malformed /refine costs none either; a per-turn pass cut off the same way does spend its unit, since the model ran to its cap, so the daily budget still bounds local GPU use when a model always truncates, and it is logged at INFO once a day, naming learning.review_max_tokens as the cause of a thinking cut-off and as a possible one of a malformed answer; a /refine cut-off does not use that line up. When such cut-offs are at least half of the day's spent units, /refine answers daily_budget_cut_off and says that, if they were cut off, the token cap is what to raise rather than the budget; one cut-off among real reviews is plain daily_budget (review-H465e m-1). A pass still waiting on the model at midnight refunds or counts against the day it spent its unit on, never the next (review-H465e nit 4), and GET /api/cognition/learning counts cut_offs_today. The unit is spent in run() after the budget is checked again there, so a burst of passes that all saw budget left in should_run cannot pass it; the cadence is checked there again too, so a burst of turns cannot pass it either (review-H465e nit 6), and a pass uses up only the turns that admitted it, so a burst gets the passes the same turns one at a time would (review-H465f nit 2) (_cut_off, agents/core/learning/background_review.py:523). - It runs whether or not the per-turn learning loop (cognition.review_enabled) is on: the owner asked, as Hermes' manual /refine does. Orchestrator.refine (agents/core/orchestrator.py:4279): - It reads a snapshot of the session's history and never writes to it. - The snapshot is conversation_snapshot (agents/core/learning/background_review.py:98): the newest turns whole and contiguous, each cut at 2,000 characters, up to 12,000 characters in all. Slash commands and the hub's replies to them are left out, so a chat of commands only has nothing to review. This replaces the per-turn review's last-6-turns, 300-character window for this path. - In flight, as it really behaves: every path that dispatches /refine holds the session's turn lease first. A /refine sent while another turn runs therefore waits for that turn (up to the lease's 180-second bound) and then reviews the conversation as it stands; it is not refused (review-H465 m-1 corrected the earlier claim). The review itself is bounded at 150 seconds (REFINE_TIMEOUT_S), below that wait, so the chat is busy for at most that long. - A direct caller holding no lease while another turn does is refused turn_in_flight: the lock is locked and the key is not among this context's held leases (agents/core/orchestrator.py:4304). No new in-flight set was added (critic note 1). - A review's result is the reviewer's last_result, which GET /api/cognition/learning shows (reviewer.status()); a refusal does not overwrite it. Each action is logged. The learning loop's knobs are declared settings (category learning, agents/core/settings_db.py:385): review_max_tokens (512, 1–32768), review_daily_budget (20, 0–1000), review_cadence (every_turn, every_n_turns, idle_gap), review_every_n (3), review_idle_gap_s (90) and review_max_facts (3), with the defaults the code already used, bounded in _LEARNING_INT_BOUNDS (agents/core/settings_db.py:998). The admin settings API, the HUD and nerva config set can change them; nerva config get shows a number named …max_tokens as the number it is, not masked as a credential, and masks every key the settings store encrypts (the GA4 service-account JSON among them), and nerva config set echoes such a value masked too (review-H465e nit 3). A model id is masked only under a hinted name: llm.default_model shows as typed. Every knob reads within its declared bounds whatever the stored row (a row from before the bounds, restored or hand-edited, reads as the default), the review's model call's token cap included (bounded_learning_int, agents/core/settings_db.py:1017). A declared 0 for review_max_facts or review_idle_gap_s is honoured, not read as unset; corrections have a cap of their own (3), so a review_max_facts of 0 keeps no facts, still records corrections, and /refine says what it found but did not keep (_number, agents/core/learning/background_review.py:293). BackgroundReviewer.run_on_demand (agents/core/learning/background_review.py:335): - It skips the cadence gate but spends the daily budget, rolling over at midnight, and refunds it when no review was had (a model down, a cut-off answer, a timeout, a cancellation), on the day the pass spent it (review-H465f nit 1). A budget of 0 means no reviews and /refine says so (reviews_off); 2.5 reads as 2, and a value that is not a number or lies outside 0–1000 (text, infinity, a boolean, a hand-edited -3, a fraction below one) is logged once and 20 used (agents/core/learning/background_review.py:268). A per-turn pass that does not run leaves a DEBUG line naming why. It keeps the strict-local model, and is bounded at REFINE_TIMEOUT_S (150 s, below the lease's 180-second wait); no setting raises it. - It neither resets nor delays the per-turn cadence. It runs one at a time and never beside a per-turn review: a /refine while a per-turn pass runs is refused busy, and a per-turn pass that would start while /refine runs is skipped, not deferred. The exclusion is taken in run() itself (agents/core/learning/background_review.py:394), so a per-turn pass spawned before the /refine, still waiting on the memory lock, is refused on_demand when it enters. A cancelled review leaves no busy flag. - Its proposals, approval cards and new skills are labelled refine, not background_review; the label is passed down per pass, never kept on the instance. An injection-flagged correction is not recorded (on both paths). Facts found while living memory is off are counted after the injection scan, and said only to the owner who asked. - run gains a focus slot in REVIEW_PROMPT ("Focus for this review: …", absent when there is none, so the per-turn prompt is byte-identical) and a context bound, which this path sets to the snapshot's. Tests: tests/test_h465_refine.py (35 cases), tests/test_h465c_refine_review.py (9, the second review), tests/test_h465d_refine_review.py (31, the third review), tests/test_h465e_refine_review.py (37, the fourth review), tests/test_h465f_refine_review.py (34, the fifth review), tests/test_h465g_refine_review.py (18, the sixth review), tests/test_nerva_cli.py (a token budget shown unmasked), and tests/test_slash_commands.py pins the command in the owner's list. They cover: - the focus slot and its bound; - cadence skipped while the budget is spent, and the day's rollover; - one review at a time, and facts written; - the snapshot's bound, order, cutting and junk; - a whole snapshot reaching the prompt; - the reviewer receiving this session's snapshot while the session stays unchanged; - busy while another turn holds the lease, and not busy inside the command's own lease; - the empty and unavailable cases; - the owner-only command and its report, each named refusal, and /help; - the review's cases: a degraded reply is no review and costs no budget; the timeout; a cancelled review; mutual exclusion and the cadence kept; facts found with living memory off; an injected correction; the refine label; commands left out and contiguity; a chat of commands only; a refusal keeping the last result; the focus cut and where a new skill waits; a guest told /refine is the owner's. Mutation: 20 mutants; 18 were caught at once, and the other two after cases were added (the snapshot's bound reaching the prompt, the day rollover). The review's 28 mutants left four real survivors (a cancelled review's flag, the snapshot's contiguity, a refusal overwriting the last result, the focus cut); all are now caught. The first round's 19 mutants were all caught. The second review's 29 mutants left four real survivors (a new skill's label, a setting raising the bound, a garbage bound setting, a timeout's stored result): the bound setting is gone and the other two have cases. The third round's 14 mutants were all caught. The third review's 36 mutants (29 killed) left four real survivors (an empty reply, a reply cut after an inner }, a thinking cut-off's stored result, a cancelled /refine staying cancelled); all four have cases. That round's 22 mutants: 21 caught, one equivalent (an explicit unset check the except branch already covers, since removed). The fourth review's 40 mutants left seven real survivors (the documented values accepted, a search for an error anywhere, a /refine cut-off using up the day's line, a skip reason other than on_demand); each has a case, the day's line after a /refine only since the fifth round. That round's 19 mutants were all caught, two after their cases were added. The fifth review's 51 mutants left nine real survivors (the cut-off refusal's threshold, which pass logs the day's line, the orchestrator's bounded token cap, the rollover of cut_offs_today in both entry points, a /refine cut-off counted among them, the corrections cap, the found-not-kept count against injected and agent facts); each has a case. That round's 20 mutants were all caught. The sixth review's 40 mutants left two real survivors (a regex closed by a later bracket or line), each with a case now. This round's 6 mutants: four caught, two equivalent (the refund's day check and its reset, since nothing rolls the day while a /refine runs, and a /refine refunds at most once). | <a id="h473"></a>H473 | Named multi-folder projects that give work a stable repo and branch convention | skip | Echivalent | Reevaluat | Final review at HEAD 57ed6db (branch codex/hermes-progress-20261010). The Hermes \`project\` command tree is ported: create, list/ls, show, add-folder, remove-folder, rename, set-primary, use, archive, restore and bind-board (agents/core/kanban/cli_upstream/projects_commands.py:21-62), all dispatched against a durable per-profile store (agents/core/kanban/cli_upstream/projects_commands.py:236). The owner reaches it as \`nerva project ...\` (agents/cli/nerva.py:196, agents/cli/nerva.py:4929-4937), which posts to POST /api/kanban/projects/command (agents/core/routers/kanban.py:63-65). The store persists the active-project pointer (agents/core/kanban/upstream/projects_db.py:633-640). Cards on a board bound to a project get a worktree under the repo and a deterministic branch name (agents/core/kanban/upstream/kanban_db.py:1285-1291, agents/core/kanban/upstream/projects_db.py:734). The one open gap was that the repo-discovery cache had no owner surface. That gap is now closed: - Two new verbs are registered, \`discover --depth N\` (0-8, default 4) and \`repos\` (read-only) (agents/core/kanban/cli_upstream/projects_commands.py:63-67, agents/core/kanban/cli_upstream/projects_commands.py:417). - \`discover\` walks the file roots breadth-first to find git repos. It does not follow symlinks, skips hidden and generated directories, and re-resolves every hit through the file scope. It has a directory budget, a repo budget and a per-directory entry budget, and reports when any of them truncates the scan (agents/core/kanban/upstream/projects_db.py:775-819, agents/core/kanban/upstream/projects_db.py:763-772). It then replaces the discovered_repos cache (agents/core/kanban/upstream/projects_db.py:68-71, agents/core/kanban/upstream/projects_db.py:838-847). - The scan runs off the event loop via asyncio.to_thread (agents/core/kanban/projects_cli.py:108-111). - The cache is keyed only by a digest of the file roots, and the scan depth is stored separately (agents/core/kanban/upstream/projects_db.py:755-760, agents/core/kanban/upstream/projects_db.py:90). The "cleared" message appears only when rows from other roots were actually dropped (agents/core/kanban/upstream/projects_db.py:830). - \`repos\` reads the cache without writing to it. If the roots have changed, it hides the old rows and reports them as stale instead of deleting them (agents/core/kanban/upstream/projects_db.py:850-866, agents/core/kanban/cli_upstream/projects_commands.py:400-409). Tests: - \`discover\` fills the cache: tests/test_hermes_projects_cli.py:398 - Rows from old roots are hidden and kept until the next \`discover\`: tests/test_hermes_projects_cli.py:435 - A non-default depth is listed and \`repos --depth\` is rejected: tests/test_hermes_projects_cli.py:462 - The scan runs off the event loop: tests/test_hermes_projects_cli.py:483 - The per-directory entry cap: tests/test_hermes_projects_cli.py:518 - Owner-only access: tests/test_hermes_projects_cli.py:531 - Scan budgets and scope: tests/test_hermes_projects_cli.py:546 - The real \`nerva project discover --depth 2\` verb, then \`repos\` through the owner HTTP route; an unauthenticated call gets 401: tests/test_hermes_kanban_surfaces_wiring.py:164-193 - The project lifecycle: tests/test_hermes_projects_cli.py:24 - The store and discovery: tests/test_hermes_kanban_projects.py:264 - A board inheriting its project: tests/test_hermes_kanban_board_projects.py:31 Review history: the first revision (r1, bf7ba5e) drew reviewer findings. \`repos\` deleted rows and depended on depth, the scan blocked the event loop, and the first scan printed a "cleared" message. r2 fixed all three with tests written red-first, passed two adversarial skeptics, and was cherry-picked onto HEAD. Honest limits: - There is no desktop or web Projects view of the discovered repos. The owner surfaces are the CLI verb and the HTTP command route. - On a roots change, \`repos\` reports the cache as stale rather than deleting it. The next \`discover\` replaces it. - I did not run the guard suites myself; their 133 passes are the implementer's figure. Only the four row test files below were run here. Test runs: tests/test_hermes_projects_cli.py, tests/test_hermes_kanban_projects.py, tests/test_hermes_kanban_board_projects.py and tests/test_hermes_kanban_surfaces_wiring.py were each run twice at HEAD. Run 1: 95 passed. Run 2: 95 passed. No flakiness. Partially satisfied children: \`.api-model-routing\` — \`ChatRequest\` (\`agents/web.py:1140\`) is \`extra="forbid"\` and accepts only \`agent\`/\`reasoning\`/\`session_id\`, so per-request \`model\`/\`provider\` and \`model_routes\` alias precedence (including the 400-on-provider-conflict rule) do not exist; only the \`reasoning\` override is governed and live (\`agents/web.py:1400\`). \`.api-models\` — no \`/api/model/options\` provider-aware picker payload with refresh/cache-bust semantics; \`/api/models/local\` and \`/api/models/info\` (\`agents/core/routers/models_llm.py\`) are both behind \`admin_guard\`. \`.api-artifacts\` — digest guarantees are subtype-specific: \`BinaryArtifactStore.read\` validates stored size, MIME and expected SHA-256 for \`ba-\*\`; new cloud-finalized catalog \`md-\*\` records now persist the already-verified completion digest and compare it with exactly the bytes returned by catalog delivery/export. New ComfyUI and local OpenAI PNG catalog rows also bind their producer-computed digest. Legacy rows and other producers that do not supply a canonical digest stay unbound; stable-ID retries do not backfill them. Catalog export metadata distinguishes verified/unbound. New ComfyUI, local OpenAI and cloud standalone generated PNGs persist strict expected-digest sidecars through a shared reserved-ID publisher, checked by the shared delivery/edit reader. Malformed bindings and mismatched bytes refuse. Missing sidecars preserve legacy-unbound reads; cloud task recovery independently checks its completion SHA even without a sidecar. Metadata deletion is indistinguishable from legacy, and same-ID collisions with nonparticipating publishers can reduce availability. These routes use the shared owner/user guard model; no per-credential tenant isolation is claimed. Expected-digest binding for other unsupplied producers and legacy rows/standalone IDs, plus any wider accepted scope contract, remain separate work; raw blob responses and gallery controls do not expose the new export integrity status. Out of scope by the row's own rationale, not gaps: \`POST /v1/chat/completions\` (explicitly refused) and \`POST /v1/responses\` (same chat-façade family; any façade must re-enter the governed \`POST /chat\` path at \`agents/web.py:1335\`). Namespace continuation: the new exact \`GET /v1/capabilities\` API coexists with the unchanged \`GET /v1\` legacy HTML; route and OpenAPI gates cover the addition. | <a id="h480"></a>H480 | Send a message to any configured channel from a script, with no model call | copy | Parțial | Reevaluat | Atașamentele \`MEDIA:\<path\>\` nu sunt purtate: o rută care citește căi locale și le trimite pe un canal e egress de fișiere și trebuie să ajungă în spatele Action Kernel-ului, cu un director-sursă delimitat, înainte să existe. Cerința structurală „fără gateway pornit” rămâne o divergență documentată: \`nerva send\` trece prin hub ca să existe IntentLog și rate-limit. Corpurile peste 4.000 de caractere sunt refuzate, nu fragmentate (Hermes fragmentează per platformă). Slack și Discord rămân reply-only (restul H018); email-ul e exclus deliberat. Nu există adresare \`platform:chat_id\[:thread\]\` / \`platform:#canal\` ca la Hermes: \`--channel telegram\` înseamnă întotdeauna chat-ul owner-ului. Precedența diverge deliberat: la Hermes argumentul câștigă în fața \`--file\`, aici ambele deodată e eroare de utilizare. Erorile nu au prefixul \`hermes send:\`. \`JobRunner._send\` își păstrează propria rezolvare a destinației (lot-ul jobs). Fără probă live pe un canal real din această sesiune: verificarea a fost prin hub fals și prin ChannelManager-ul real cu adaptoare false. | <a id="h481"></a>H481 | Refuse a catastrophic shell command no matter who approved it (hardline floor + risky-pattern tier + de-obfuscation) | update | Parțial | Reevaluat | \*\*The middle tier does not exist.\*\* The row asks for three stacked layers; this is the first, with its matching repaired (and repaired again in PR #1177). There is still no ~40-rule severity/reversibility-tagged risky-pattern catalogue feeding the approval card's description, so \`rm -rf ~/projects\` is neither hardline nor pattern-classified — re-checked 2026-09-19 on 494a13b2: \`hardline_match("rm -rf ~/projects")\` and \`hardline_match(\['rm','-rf','/home/x/projects'\])\` both return None, and the module carries no severity/reversibility/catalogue vocabulary at all — and the owner's card still says "run this argv" rather than "recursive delete", which the row's rationale names as the point. No user-editable \`approvals.deny\` fnmatch list at hardline level (no \`fnmatch\`/\`deny\` in the module). No parser limits that themselves hardline-block and save an oversized payload to a file for manual review (128k chars / 4096 separator-free / 25k segments); \`MAX_ARG_CHARS = 4000\` is argv validation, not a refusal. \*\*Variants Hermes produces and this still does not:\*\* NFKC normalisation, \`$HOME\`/\`$HERMES_HOME\` folding, grep-pattern span masking, and \`python -c\` / \`perl -e\` / \`node -e\` payload extraction — the last left alone on purpose, since \`jobs_scripts.snapshot_script\` legitimately builds \`\[sys.executable, '-I', '-c', source\]\`. \`$()\`/backtick substitution is now extracted in ONE place only: #1177's \`_substituted\` narrows a heredoc BODY line to its substitutions, so \`cat \<\<EOF\` / \`$(rm -rf /)\` / \`EOF\` refuses; an ordinary line is still not expanded, so \`echo $(rm -rf /)\` and a backtick \`rm -rf /\` inside an assignment return None (a \`$(mkfs.ext4 …)\` is caught only through \`_CMD\`'s \`(\` anchor). The row's own examples \`$(printf mkfs).ext4 /dev/sda\` and \`echo bWtmcw==\|base64 -d\|sh\` still return None. \*\*Gaps this module knows it still has, listed honestly rather than as a complete set:\*\* nesting deeper than \`_MAX_SHELL_DEPTH\` (depth-3 \`sh -c "sh -c 'sh -c …'"\` returns None, pinned by test); a quote at a word BOUNDARY (\`'mkfs.ext4' /dev/sda\`) rather than inside a word; \`powershell -EncodedCommand\` base64; a \`cmd /c\` payload split across several argv items; an obfuscated shell HEAD in argv form (\`\['s""h','-c',…\]\`), because the de-obfuscation pass runs after payload extraction and its output is not fed back through it; and, since #1177, two in the false-refusal direction — a \`case\` label with a leading \`(\` (\`(shutdown) echo bye ;;\`) is still read as a command, and a \`case\` nested inside another is not modelled: its inner first label IS stripped (\`case $1 in\\na) case $2 in\\nreboot) echo r ;;\\nesac ;;\\nesac\` went power_cycle→None), so the docstring's 'not handled' is about the region boundary, not a guaranteed refusal. \*\*Refusals #1177 cleared in the dangerous direction — closed by this slice (H481, 2026-09-22).\*\* The \`case\`-label strip fires only inside a real command-position \`case WORD in … esac\` region now, so \`(echo case in; reboot); echo esac\` and the \`$IFS\`-spliced \`(echo case in; mkfs.ext4$IFS/dev/sda); echo esac\` / \`wipefs$IFS-a$IFS/dev/sda\` refuse again; and \`_heredoc_feeds_a_shell\` now also sees a body a shell consumes AFTER the redirection through a pipe (\`cat \<\<EOF \| sh\`, \`cat \<\<EOF \| bash\`, \`cat \<\<EOF \| grep … \| sh\`) or via a file a shell later runs (\`cat \<\<'EOF' \>x.sh; sh x.sh\`), so those refuse — and, after the review round, so do \`(sh x.sh)\`, \`{ sh x.sh; }\`, \`if true; then sh x.sh; fi\`, \`cat x.sh \| sh\`, \`sh -c '. x.sh'\`, \`. x.sh\`, \`source x.sh\`, \`tee x.sh \<\<EOF; sh x.sh\`, a quoted \`\> "x.sh"\` target, \`sh /dev/stdin \<\<EOF\`, \`bash -c sh \<\<EOF\` and \`cat \<\<EOF \| eval "$(cat)"\`, each verified to run the body. Pinned in tests/test_local_transport.py, reproduced against /bin/sh, /bin/dash and /bin/bash first, and screened by a 671,995-case differential fuzz vs origin/main whose every difference is explained by the two changed mechanisms (numbers in the summary; the earlier \`refusals_cleared = 0\` claim is withdrawn). Still open in this direction, listed in \`_detection_variants\` and pinned as misses: a heredoc body written to a file run by a bare path (\`… \>x.sh; ./x.sh\`), by a variable-carried name (\`for f in x.sh; do sh $f; done\`) or by the environment (\`BASH_ENV=x.sh bash -c :\`); a heredoc opened inside a command substitution (\`eval "$(cat \<\<EOF …)"\`, read as quoted text); \`xargs -I{} sh -c '{}'\` (each line becomes the command line); and a \`;\` inside a \`( )\` group of a pipe stage (\`cat \<\<EOF \| (cd /tmp; sh)\`). \*\*Two pre-existing false positives are unchanged\*\* (\`git commit -m "fix;mkfs.ext4 handling"\` → mkfs; \`grep -r "(shutdown" docs/\` → power_cycle), and \`_PATH_PREFIX\` added a third class no approval can lift: a path to a script whose basename starts with a hardline name — \`./mkfs.sh\` (mkfs), \`./reboot.sh\`, \`./scripts/shutdown.sh --dry-run\`, \`/opt/app/bin/halt\` (power_cycle) — all None on 1c5054ea, all refused on 494a13b2 (bare \`reboot.sh\` already refused before; the prefix extends it to every path spelling). This slice left that (c) class unclosed on purpose: any name- or path-only rule that cleared \`./mkfs.sh\` or \`/opt/app/bin/halt\` would also clear a TRUE refusal — \`./mkfs.sh\` is structurally \`mkfs.\<suffix\>\` exactly like the real \`/sbin/mkfs.ext4\`, and \`/opt/app/bin/halt\` is \`\<path\>/\<hardline-name\>\` exactly like a copied \`/tmp/mkfs.ext4 /dev/sda\` — so it needs approval-context (is the target a workspace script or a real system binary) the pure static floor does not have. \*\*And a measured cost, re-measured after #1177 removed the breadth cap\*\* (\`_MAX_SHELL_EXPANSIONS\` and the \`MAX_ARG_CHARS\` re-expansion guard are gone; every level-1 payload is unwrapped again): on a maximal 64x4000-character argv the pass is roughly unchanged (79.6 ms on the pre-#1177 module vs 82.3 ms after, same machine, best of 5), but a command made of 2,000 nested \`sh -c "sh -c 'echo ok'"\` segments (57k chars) goes from 196 ms to 380 ms — synchronous, on the event loop, before every exec. The docstring's linear-in-input argument holds (each level's payloads are disjoint substrings); an independent re-run on another machine saw 79.0→80.6 ms and 125→151 ms, so the constant grows for nested input but the factor is machine-dependent and no test pins either number. This slice's first pass claimed no measurable cost on that maximal 64x4000-character argv (78.7 → 78.4 ms); the review showed the claim held only for input with no \`case\` word and never exercised the redirect-target branch, which was quadratic. Re-measured after the review round (best of 3, same machine, origin/main → this branch): the maximal 64x4000 argv 62.0 → 58.6 ms; the same argv filled with case/in prose 18,207 → 105 ms (main's own \`\\bcase\\b.\*?\\besac\\b\` was super-linear there too); 4000 chars of \`case x in\` 21.6 → 6.5 ms; eight 4000-char argv items of prose 316 → 14 ms; 400 \`cat \<\<EOF \| sh\` blocks (12 KB) 39.8 → 64.9 ms; 400 \`cat \<\<E \>x\` blocks in 4000 chars 25 → 39 ms (2,471 ms on the first pass); 1,600 such blocks (33.6 KB) 132 → 201 ms (97.5 s on the first pass); 2,000 nested \`sh -c\` segments 146 → 148 ms; 300 real \`case\` statements 57 → 60 ms. The heredoc-with-target shapes cost about 1.5x main, linear, because the statement lines after a heredoc are tokenised once and shared; nothing else pays. Six test items pin wall-clock bounds (0.25–2 s) two orders of magnitude above these; no test pins a ratio. \*\*Adversarial review of the original slice found four more defects, all fixed and each reproduced first\*\* against real /bin/sh, /bin/dash and /bin/bash: (1) \`_shell_c_payloads\` demanded the word after the wrappers BE the shell, so \`env FOO=1 sh -c 'mkfs.ext4 /dev/sda'\` — and \`sudo -u root sh -c …\`, \`nice -n 10 sh -c …\` — skipped the whole \`sh -c\` screening while deleting \`FOO=1 \` made the same string \`hardline_denied:mkfs\`; \`_CMD\` had been widened for that assignment prefix and the unwrapper had not. (2) \`_unquoted_lines\` read a backslash-newline as a statement separator when it is a line CONTINUATION, so \`mk\\\` + newline + \`fs.ext4 /dev/sda\`, which all three shells splice into \`mkfs.ext4\`, was seen as two harmless fragments. (3) every heredoc body line became a command position, so \`cat \> x.yaml \<\<'EOF'\` / \`shutdown: graceful\` / \`EOF\` was refused as \`power_cycle\`; body lines were joined as data in the flat text. \*\*#1177's second review showed that fix was incomplete in three ways, all closed there:\*\* \`segments\` still tokenised every body line, so \`cat \> README.md \<\<'EOF'\` / \`rm -rf / will destroy the box\` / \`EOF\` stayed a \`recursive_root_removal\` refusal; the rule had no exception for a heredoc a SHELL consumes, so \`bash \<\<EOF\` / \`mkfs.ext4 /dev/sda\` / \`EOF\` returned None (a bypass the heredoc work itself opened); and any \`\<\<\` — inside quotes, inside \`$(( ))\`, a \`\<\<\<\` here-string, or with a delimiter that never returns — opened a heredoc and switched the newline screening off for every following line. (4) \`{\` anchored bare, so \`jq '{reboot: .needs_reboot}'\` was a \`power_cycle\` refusal; POSIX requires whitespace after \`{\` for a brace group, and \`{ mkfs.ext4 /dev/sda; }\` is still refused. Each fix is red-proofed on its own. [d1](../agents/core/environments/terminal_contract.py) [d2](../tests/test_local_transport.py) |

| <a id="h495"></a>H495 | Never let a credential reach a log, a transcript, an approval card or an export | update | Parțial | Reevaluat | This is one of the row's seven paths. Hermes applies \`redact.py\` to logs, verbose output, tool output, approval prompts, gateway messages, transcripts and memory; this slice covers LOGS. Still owed, and the rationale calls them the part that matters most: the hash-chained audit DB (a \`cat .env\` from \`terminal_run\` still writes a live credential into an append-only log that by design cannot be edited), the decision-inbox approval card the owner reads on a phone, task payloads, terminal output, and the observability exports — which Hermes scrubs unconditionally with no knob, returning \`\[redaction-unavailable\]\` rather than raw text. Also absent: the second mask mode (a syntactically INVALID \`«redacted:ghp_…»\` sentinel for file reads, so an agent cannot write a masked-but-plausible key back and silently kill the credential), \`code_file=True\` sparing source constants, \`_mask_control_split_tokens()\` for tokens smuggled across ANSI/zero-width characters, and the shared \`.env\` basename list. The two silent-degradation paths named at review are now CLOSED, after the SAST gate forced the question: a handler whose \`addFilter\` fails is counted and published through \`uncovered_handler_count()\` and a warning naming how many handlers are writing unredacted, and a \`loggerDict\` walk that raises warns that coverage fell back to root-only. The one silent swallow left is the filter's own last-ditch blank (\`# nosec B110\`), where a \`logging.Filter\` that raises would take down the caller's log call and the scanner has already failed. \`install_log_redaction()\` remains exported although the \`everywhere\` variant is what production uses. \*\*A later slice's full-suite run surfaced one more thing about this control, recorded here rather than fixed:\*\* the scanner's \`high_entropy_secret\` pattern matches an ordinary filesystem path. Under \`-n auto --dist loadfile\` a warning naming a pytest tmp file arrived as \`truncated: \[REDACTED:high_entropy_secret\].md\`, which is what a real operator would see when a log line names a file with a long random-looking segment — a debuggability cost the module docstring already warns about in general terms, now with a concrete case. Separately, \`setup_logging()\` installs the filter on every handler of every logger and nothing took it back off, so every later test on the same xdist worker ran under a live redactor. The installer is PRODUCTION code, not the tests: \`agents/run.py\` calls \`setup_logging()\` at module level, so importing it installs the filter during pytest COLLECTION — before any fixture runs — and eight test files import it; \`agents/web.py\` calls it from the FastAPI lifespan, so any test that drives the app installs it again; five test files call it directly on top of that. There is no list of leaking files to fix. The cleanup therefore lives in \`tests/conftest.py\` as an autouse fixture that strips unconditionally BEFORE each test as well as after — a snapshot-and-restore fixture, which is what the two neighbouring isolation fixtures do and what this was first written as, treats a collection-time install as pre-existing and preserves it for the life of the worker. That version went green locally and RED in CI on exactly the test it was meant to fix. The first attempt at it matched by \`isinstance\` and silently did nothing: \`agents/\` is on \`sys.path\`, so \`core.security.log_redaction\` and \`agents.core.security.log_redaction\` are two module objects over this one file with two distinct \`SecretRedactionFilter\` classes, and the root handler was carrying the other one. The match is by class name now, and four paired tests pin both halves — including the alternate import path, which is the case the first attempt missed. | <a id="h497"></a>H497 | Let a stranger reach the assistant only after the owner says so | update | Parțial | Reevaluat | \*\*The row names four hardening gaps; (a) is closed, (c) is closed for the deeplink path, (b) is open and (d) is half closed.\*\* (c) \*revocation reaching live adapters\*: \`revoke_deeplinks()\` and \`unpair()\` now act on the one object the Telegram adapter redeems from and the gateway consults on every message, so there is no second copy for a link or an approval to survive in — pinned by \`test_revoking_on_the_shared_store_reaches_the_live_telegram_adapter\`. Slack and Discord have no deeplink path and gate through the same gateway instance. Still outstanding, from the row itself: (b) \*no lockout after N failed attempts\* — the row wants a 1 h lockout after 5 failed approvals, checked BEFORE the pending lookup so a code already in flight cannot be brute-forced past it; there is still only a rate limit and an in-memory guess budget, both of which reset on restart. (d) is half closed: the chat command registry does split owner and user tiers on channels — \`_channel_principal\` makes only a configured owner sender an admin principal and every ADMIN-tier command refuses anyone else with "owner command" (agents/core/commands.py:177-183) — so a paired stranger gets only the user-tier commands; still missing is the always-allowed floor's \`whoami\` (no such command exists), so the row's \`{help, whoami}\` floor is not met. \*\*Unaddressed from the Hermes column:\*\* pairing-code GENERATION (8 characters from a 32-char unambiguous alphabet via \`secrets.choice\`) and the code's 1 h TTL — the code here never expires; "max 3 pending per platform" (the store bounds 200 globally); "1 request per user per 10 min" (it is 5); \`unauthorized_dm_behavior\` treating inbox-shaped platforms differently from chat-shaped ones; and the ordered authorization union (allow-all flag → pairing approvals → per-platform allowlist → global allowlist → global allow-all → default DENY), which is still an ad-hoc sequence in \`is_allowed\`/\`gate_inbound\`. \*\*Two honest limits of the second slice.\*\* The store itself still has no defence against a second instance — the guarantee is one instance per process by construction, and the premise test says so in words. And an install that had relocated its data root (\`JARVIS_HOME\`) and paired senders through the HUD kept them in \`\<cwd\>/memory_logs/sender_pairing.json\`; the store now opens under the data root, so those senders are held once more until re-approved (the owner's allowlisted ids never lived in that file and are unaffected). \*\*And the limit carried from the first slice.\*\* Stretching is a work factor, not a wall: a four-digit code goes from milliseconds to minutes, an eight-character mixed-alphabet code becomes infeasible, and \*\*nothing enforces a floor on what the owner types\*\* — \`PairingCodeBody\` caps the length at 128 and sets no minimum — while generating the code for them, the row's own prescription, is not implemented.
