| <a id="h501"></a>H501 | Warn about a dangerous deployment posture before it becomes an incident | update | Echivalent | Reevaluat | Nerva now warns about a dangerous host posture, as Hermes does, on top of a network half that was already stronger. assert_safe_bind (agents/core/boot_guards.py) still refuses an unauthenticated non-loopback bind and prints the exact env vars that fix it, and GET /api/security/posture still reports the secrets backend, skill signing, sandbox isolation and guardrails honestly. agents/core/host_posture.py adds the host half: three read-only checks that never block and never change anything, each answering ok, warn or unknown (it could not tell, never a false green), with a reason, what it saw and the fix. check_root (agents/core/host_posture.py:71) warns when the process runs as root (euid 0) on any host, headless included, or elevated on Windows (IsUserAnAdmin). check_sshd (agents/core/host_posture.py:168) reads /etc/ssh/sshd_config the way sshd does (_SshdScan, agents/core/host_posture.py:120): Include files are read in place, relative paths from /etc/ssh, each pattern's hits in lexical order, at most 16 deep; Keyword value, Keyword=value and trailing comments are accepted and keywords and values are case-insensitive; the first PasswordAuthentication outside a Match block wins, so a drop-in Included at the top overrides the main file; a Match block (to the end of its file, an Include inside it conditional) never sets the global value but a Match block that turns passwords on warns too; an absent directive is the sshd default yes and warns; no sshd_config is ok; an unreadable file is unknown unless the answer was read elsewhere; an unrecognised value is unknown. check_container_storage (agents/core/host_posture.py:241) first decides whether this is a container and then finds the mount the data root (resolved through symlinks) lives on in /proc/self/mountinfo (parse_mountinfo, agents/core/host_posture.py:216, with its octal escapes, and mount_of, agents/core/host_posture.py:230, taking the longest containing mount point and the later of two stacked mounts): the container's own root filesystem or a tmpfs/ramfs warns, a volume or bind mount is ok, no mountinfo or no mount is unknown. The container decision (changed by H283) is no longer the check's own: with the default marker=True it calls host_identity.container_marker() (agents/core/host_posture.py:244-250, agents/core/host_identity.py:525), the one host detector the system prompt also uses. That detector still reads host_posture.in_container (agents/core/host_posture.py:192: /.dockerenv, /run/.containerenv, or a docker, kubepods, containerd, libpod or lxc cgroup of PID 1) and adds KUBERNETES_SERVICE_HOST, systemd's /run/systemd/container file and the container env word, and the operator's JARVIS_CONTAINER override (agents/core/host_identity.py:218): none/0/false/no/off/disable/disabled says not a container and makes the storage check ok (not_in_container), a yes or a known kind says container; an unknown word is ignored and the markers decide; WSL and proot are not containers. run_checks, report and log_startup (agents/core/host_posture.py:280, :294, :302) run the three independently, a failing check becoming an unknown row. The hub logs each warning once per process at start, after logging is set up, off the event loop (host_posture.log_startup, agents/web.py:506, lifespan). GET /api/security/posture (admin) gains host: the three findings and a warnings count (agents/core/routers/security.py:396). python scripts/doctor.py and nerva doctor show them as the advisory rows host_not_root, sshd_no_passwords and container_storage at the end of the report: a warning is warn with the fix and never fails the verdict, a check that could not tell or could not run is skip, never ok (check_host_posture, scripts/doctor.py:302). The module is stdlib only at import (host_identity is imported lazily inside the storage check), so the doctor can use it on a broken install. The shipped Dockerfile has no USER, so a stock container now shows the root warning; running the image as a non-root user is left to the deploy. Tests: tests/test_h501_host_posture.py (42), with real sshd_config trees in a temporary directory (drop-ins read first and last, lexical order, absolute and quoted Includes, Match blocks in the main and in an included file, a trailing comment naming a file, an Include loop) and real mountinfo text; tests/test_h283_host_identity.py::test_the_doctors_container_check_reads_the_same_detector pins that the storage check follows KUBERNETES_SERVICE_HOST and the JARVIS_CONTAINER=none override. 55 mutants: 53 killed after five cases were added; the other two were dead code, removed (that mutation run predates the H283 change). Not live-proven: no run inside a real container, on a real sshd host or on Windows; the checks are proven against real file trees and mountinfo text. | <a id="h502"></a>H502 | Refuse an MCP server entry that is a backdoor wearing an MCP costume, and never hand one the owner's keys | copy | Parțial | Reevaluat | \*\*The documented per-server \`env\` migration path does not exist as a reachable surface.\*\* \`MCPServerConfig\` has no \`env\` field (\`routers/mcp.py:145-157\`, no \`model_config\`), \`POST /api/admin/mcp\` drops the key (pydantic's default \`extra="ignore"\`), and neither \`to_config\` (\`client.py:909-923\`) nor \`load_from_config\` (\`:814-849\`) writes or reads one — the module docstring says as much at \`client.py:41-44\`. The only remedy an owner can actually reach is the \*\*host-wide\*\* \`JARVIS_MCP_STDIO_ALLOWED_ENV\` (\`:92-98\`, "Host-wide, not per-server"), which is a strictly weaker grant than the per-server one the docs describe: an owner whose forge server needs \`GITHUB_TOKEN\` must allow it for every stdio server on the host. Whether to ship on that or build the per-server surface first is a product decision, written up as \`docs/OWNER_TASKS.md\` §P28.3 with both options. \*\*Related and also owner-level:\*\* \`XAUTHORITY\` and \`DBUS_SESSION_BUS_ADDRESS\` are both on \`STDIO_ENV_ALLOWLIST\` (\`client.py:173\`), and today one is listed-but-silently-dropped (\`_SECRET_LIKE\` at \`:174-176\` matches the \`AUTH\` in \`XAUTHORITY\`) while the other is listed-and-handed-over — they should be consistent in one direction or the other. \*\*And the honest ceiling, stated wherever the guarantee is:\*\* this is \*\*defence in depth, not a security boundary\*\*, and since #1179 the module states that ceiling by TWO routes rather than one (\`client.py:17-36\`). The child is same-UID with no namespace, so a server that can run a subprocess reads the withheld variables straight out of \`/proc/\<ppid\>/environ\`; and the baseline narrows the \*\*filesystem\*\* not at all — \`cwd\` defaults to the hub's own working directory, so \`open(".env")\` hands back exactly the keys that were withheld, which \`cwd_secret_files()\` now says out loud at connect (WARNING, filenames only, \`client.py:584-590\`) rather than leaving the owner to infer a protection from the withheld count alone. What the baseline buys is that a \*careless\* or \*curious\* server does not get them by accident, and that an owner's \`JARVIS_\*\` settings are not ambient in a third party's process. It does not stop an adversary, and the row says so rather than implying otherwise; closing the filesystem route as well as the \`/proc\` one needs real process isolation (separate UID, namespace or container — \`client.py:33-36\`), which is not shipped. \*\*Unaddressed from the row:\*\* there is no refusal of an MCP entry that is a backdoor wearing an MCP costume — no command allow-listing, no signature or provenance check on the spawned binary (the docstring itself calls the screener "still-unshipped", \`client.py:34\`), and \`POST /api/admin/mcp\` still stores \`req.command\` verbatim after checking only transport, trust tier, tool-filter shape and bounds, and duplicate name (\`routers/mcp.py:188-241\`, \`:184\`); the only shape check is \`_command_argv()\`'s shell-metacharacter/NUL refusal at connect (\`client.py:538-548\`), which is not a screener. #1179 changed none of this — it explicitly chose disclosure over refusal. This slice hardens what the child \*receives\*; the row also asks who the child is allowed to \*be\*. [d1](../agents/core/mcp/client.py) [d2](../agents/core/routers/mcp.py) [d3](../tests/test_mcp_transports.py) |
| <a id="h503"></a>H503 | Unpack an archive from another machine without letting it write outside the destination | update | Echivalent | Reevaluat | archive_safe is the only module in Nerva that reads an archive. Backup verify and restore unpack through extract_tar_path (agents/core/archive_safe.py:573; agents/core/backup.py:809, agents/core/backup.py:891). Marketplace install_from_zip unpacks through extract_zip_bytes (agents/core/archive_safe.py:637; agents/core/skills/marketplace.py:816). The old backup._safe_extract and the marketplace _safe_targets+extractall pass are gone. An AST scan (tests/test_archive_safe.py:702, with probes at tests/test_archive_safe.py:688) fails when any other product module imports tarfile or zipfile outside a write-only allowlist, opens an archive for reading or calls an extract-family method. normalize_member (agents/core/archive_safe.py:122) folds backslash to '/' first. It then refuses empty, NUL, POSIX-absolute, Windows-absolute, UNC and drive-lettered names, and any '..' or empty part. Only regular files and directories are written. Symlink, hardlink, device, fifo and sparse tar members raise (agents/core/archive_safe.py:504), and so do symlink, device, fifo, socket and encrypted zip entries (agents/core/archive_safe.py:596). _Planner (agents/core/archive_safe.py:182) validates every member before the first write: name, type, in-archive conflicts and duplicates, member count and declared bytes (agents/core/archive_safe.py:257). It also checks the destination's existing content (agents/core/archive_safe.py:286): a link on the way to a member is refused, and so is a directory where a file goes (tests/test_archive_safe.py:365, tests/test_backup.py:471). The pre-scan reads the stream to its end (agents/core/archive_safe.py:522), so a bad gzip CRC, trailing data or a corrupt header part-way through is a refusal, not a shortened tree (tests/test_archive_safe.py:482, tests/test_archive_safe.py:517). Bytes are counted again while streaming (agents/core/archive_safe.py:389). The byte budget is clamped to free space plus the blocks of the single-link files the archive replaces (agents/core/archive_safe.py:314), so an in-place --force restore fits (tests/test_backup.py:443). PAX and GNU long-name header payloads are capped before tarfile reads them, 1 MiB each and 256 MiB in total (agents/core/archive_safe.py:461, agents/core/archive_safe.py:483; tests/test_backup.py:515). A link or hardlinked name at a member's path is unlinked and the file is created O_EXCL\|O_NOFOLLOW, never written through (agents/core/archive_safe.py:373; tests/test_archive_safe.py:323, tests/test_archive_safe.py:349). Backups take their caps from JARVIS_BACKUP_MAX_MEMBERS and JARVIS_BACKUP_MAX_BYTES (agents/core/backup.py:142); skill packages use SKILL_PACKAGE_LIMITS (agents/core/skills/marketplace.py:42). On the producing side, create_backup writes both the encrypted and the plaintext branch through atomic_write, a sibling temp file that is fsynced and then os.replace'd (agents/core/archive_safe.py:654; agents/core/backup.py:584, agents/core/backup.py:589). Archives are GNU-format tar (agents/core/backup.py:643). The export walk skips symlinks (agents/core/archive_safe.py:715; agents/core/backup.py:562). publish_skill uses it on the staged copy it signs (agents/core/skills/marketplace.py:392); the copy itself is built from the bytes of one source snapshot, which refuses a linked folder, a link or non-regular member and a file that changed while read (agents/core/skills/marketplace.py:375), which has its own test (tests/test_marketplace_governance_hf12_12.py:219). Every other name, hardlinked ones included, is archived as its own regular member (agents/core/backup.py:603, agents/core/backup.py:627; tests/test_backup.py:388). verify and restore compare the manifest's file_count with what the archive held (agents/core/backup.py:836; tests/test_backup.py:430). install_from_zip stages inside skills_dir, runs the signature gate there, and only then renames the tree into place (agents/core/skills/marketplace.py:854, agents/core/skills/marketplace.py:885). A non-zip upload is a 400 refusal (tests/test_marketplace_governance_hf12_12.py:194). Staging left by a killed install is swept once it is an hour old (agents/core/skills/marketplace.py:773; tests/test_marketplace_governance_hf12_12.py:203). Restore is no longer only an operator CLI action. An admin route (agents/core/routers/backup.py:98) queues a backup.restore card at the irreversible tier (agents/core/backup.py:1596); after a human accepts it, the staged restore is applied by apply_pending_restore (agents/core/backup.py:1446) from the boot hook (serve.py:131) or the offline nerva backup restore (agents/cli/nerva.py:1776). That path still unpacks through restore_backup with force (agents/core/backup.py:1574), so every extract_tar_path check above applies (tests/test_backup_inplace_restore.py:270, tests/test_backup_inplace_restore.py:293). The module CLI restore prints 'partial restore' when a failure came after the first write (agents/core/backup.py:1793; tests/test_backup.py:484) and 'nothing restored' only when nothing from the archive was written: a pre-scan refusal (agents/core/backup.py:1797; tests/test_backup.py:259), or a refusal before extraction starts, a key that cannot decrypt the archive or a non-empty target without --force (agents/core/backup.py:1798, agents/core/backup.py:1800; tests/test_backup_cli.py:137, tests/test_backup_cli.py:154). The CLI verify and restore take a name from list or a path whose real location is an archive directly in the backups directory; a copy elsewhere, a '..' out of it or a link out of it names no backup, so the CLI cannot point the extractor at an arbitrary file (agents/core/backup.py:754, agents/core/backup.py:1785; tests/test_backup_cli.py:97). The admin restore card and the staged apply take only a name matched against the backups listing (agents/core/backup.py:1602, agents/core/backup.py:1554). tests/test_backup.py:606 pins that no other product module, script or subprocess calls restore_backup directly, and tests/test_backup_inplace_restore.py:414 pins that only serve.py and agents/cli/nerva.py call apply_pending_restore. The pre-scan also refuses a component longer than the destination's NAME_MAX or a path past PATH_MAX, which the existing-path walk cannot see under a new directory (agents/core/archive_safe.py:251; tests/test_archive_safe.py:726), and a write the destination refuses mid-restore (permissions, a full disk) is a named ArchiveRejected marked partial, never a traceback (agents/core/archive_safe.py:445; tests/test_archive_safe.py:738). A restore leaves the archive's manifest in the target; create_backup never archives a top-level backup_manifest.json from the data root (agents/core/backup.py:651), so a backup of a restored root carries one manifest and verifies, restores and serves the forget purge's verified pre-snapshot (tests/test_backup.py:640, tests/test_backup.py:679). A backup of a restored root made before this change carries that name twice; verify and restore accept exactly that one repeat, last wins as tarfile resolved it, and count the dropped copy against the manifest's file_count (agents/core/backup.py:810, agents/core/backup.py:853; tests/test_backup.py:655). The repeat is bounded: the dropped copy still counts against the member and byte caps, and a third copy or any other duplicate is refused (agents/core/archive_safe.py:220, agents/core/archive_safe.py:223; tests/test_archive_safe.py:768, tests/test_archive_safe.py:775, tests/test_archive_safe.py:790). Known limit: backups made on main from a data root holding a symlink or hardlink fail verify and restore by design. Those claims and tests/test_backup_cli.py are merged in; every backup.py citation had moved (H010 code plus main's additions) and was re-pointed and checked at HEAD; the ambiguous 'nothing restored' citation is now agents/core/backup.py:1797. tests/test_backup.py, tests/test_backup_cli.py and tests/test_archive_safe.py pass at HEAD (155 passed). | <a id="h507"></a>H507 | Warn the model when the code it just wrote contains a known-dangerous pattern | copy | Echivalent | Reevaluat | Code the agent writes is checked against a table of known-dangerous patterns, and the findings go back to the model and the owner. Nothing is ever refused. agents/core/code_guidance.py holds 26 rules (RULES, agents/core/code_guidance.py:89), each scoped to the file types it applies to. They cover unsafe deserialization (pickle/dill/joblib/marshal loads; yaml.load without SafeLoader, and yaml.unsafe_load; torch.load without weights_only=True); command and code injection (os.system/popen, shell=True, Python eval/exec, JS eval and new Function, child_process.exec and execSync, require('child_process').exec, a bare exec( in a file that imports child_process, a Go exec.Command of a shell); SQL built from an f-string or \`%\`; tempfile.mktemp; XSS sinks (innerHTML/outerHTML assignment, document.write, dangerouslySetInnerHTML); and crypto and TLS footguns (ECB mode, createCipher without an IV on any receiver, verify=False, unverified SSL contexts, CERT_NONE, rejectUnauthorized: false, NODE_TLS_REJECT_UNAUTHORIZED=0, InsecureSkipVerify: true, md5/sha1 over a password). They also cover XXE parser flags and a remote \`\<script\>\` without integrity=. A separate check (_workflow_findings, agents/core/code_guidance.py:189) flags \`${{ github.event.\* }}\` inside a GitHub Actions \`run:\` step, on the run line or in its \`\|\`/\`\>\` block, whose column is the run key's own, so a \`- run: \|\` step's env:, with: and if: keys end it and are never flagged. The guards keep the usual false positives quiet: \`model.eval()\` and \`obj.eval()\`, \`def eval(\`, \`yaml.load(..., Loader=SafeLoader)\`, \`torch.load(..., weights_only=True)\`, \`regex.exec()\`, an \`===\` comparison with innerHTML, \`hashlib.md5(data)\`, a script with integrity=, whole-line comments and non-code files. Every rule is linear: a guard reads the call's balanced arguments across lines, at most MAX_CALL_CHARS (400) of them and at most MAX_CALLS_PER_LINE (8) calls a line (_call_args, agents/core/code_guidance.py:211; _guarded, agents/core/code_guidance.py:226), or the tag it matched. scan (agents/core/code_guidance.py:265) returns \`{rule, line, message}\`, at most 20 findings over the first 1 MB, with lines split at \`\\n\` only (CRLF and CR normalised), and stops after SCAN_SECONDS (0.5 s; agents/core/code_guidance.py:50); a scan cut by size or time ends with a \`scan-incomplete\` finding at the first line it did not finish, so a cut scan never reads as clean. \`.env\`, \`.env.\*\` and the shell dotfiles are scanned as shell. The findings go to five places. On the file_write approval card, FileTools.classify_mutation (agents/core/file_tools.py:1561) adds \`code_warnings\` (rule@line, at most 200 characters), \`code_warning_count\` and a title notice (\`code not fully scanned\` when a limit cut it), scanning the name as spelled and the file the write lands on (a symlink, a \`./\` or \`//\` spelling; labels, agents/core/code_guidance.py:296, names each finding once and in line order); it never sets a class, so H506's approval binding is untouched, and an instruction-file notice and the warning share the title. The gated call's \`approval_required\` answer carries \`code_warnings\`/\`code_warning_count\` (_ANSWER_LABEL_KEYS, agents/core/tool_rpc.py:213), and the tool loop's pause reply names them as warnings, not refusals (_approval_reply, agents/core/agent_runtime.py:2055): the loop ends the turn there, so the model reads them on its next turn and the owner at once. On an ungated write's result (FileTools.write_file, agents/core/file_tools.py:1308), the model reads \`code_warnings\` with a \`code_guidance\` note that they are warnings; an approved write's result lands on the approved task's record, which no model turn reads. A refused write carries none, and a failing scan never fails a write. For a marketplace install (agents/core/skills/marketplace.py:858; install and install-zip answer \`code_warnings\` when there are any, agents/core/routers/skills.py:495) and a generated skill (agents/core/skills/loader.py:1267), scan_tree (agents/core/code_guidance.py:340) walks the folder, skipping symlinks; only code files count toward its 200-file bound, a file past 1 MB is read as cut, the whole walk stops after TREE_SECONDS (2 s), and the file a bound stops at gets a \`scan-incomplete\` finding. skill_propose answers the generated skill's \`code_warnings\` (agents/core/skills/tools.py:891), and generate_skill resets them first (agents/core/skills/loader.py:1107), so a skipped generation never keeps another's; the background-review and \[learn:\] generation paths only log them (their main.py is a fixed template). The owner's switch is \`security.code_guidance\` (read by enabled, agents/core/code_guidance.py:161: on by default, only an explicit off turns it off and an unreadable store keeps it on; the settings row is seeded on in settings_db DEFAULTS, and safe mode forces it back on: safe_mode.FORCED_SETTINGS, agents/core/safe_mode.py:117). An aliased child_process module (\`cp.exec\`) is not flagged. tests/test_h507_code_guidance.py (136 cases) covers every rule firing, the guard cases, the cross-language scoping, the finding shape, the table size, the workflow rule with a blank line in a block and every non-run key, the bounds, the labels, the switch, the real ToolRPC card and approved execution, a clean and a non-code write, the shared instruction notice, a failing scan, a refused write, scan_tree (symlink, bounds, switch), generation, install with the route, and the setting row. The review round added crafted megabytes (one per quadratic rule) scanned in under a second and a card labelled promptly through the ToolRPC intake, the time and size cuts, the pause reply driven through the agent loop, skill_propose's warnings and the reset, the symlink and path spellings, a package padded with assets, the \`- run: \|\` block, the wrapped and nested calls, the child_process and createCipher spellings, CR/form-feed/U+2028 lines, the dotfiles and the safe-mode switch. The review round's 44 mutants were all killed, ten after seven cases were added. A separate check (_workflow_findings, agents/core/code_guidance.py:189) flags \`${{ github.event.\* }}\` inside a GitHub Actions \`run:\` step, on the run line or in its \`\|\`/\`\>\` block, whose column is the run key's own, so a \`- run: \|\` step's env:, with: and if: keys end it and are never flagged. The guards keep the usual false positives quiet: \`model.eval()\` and \`obj.eval()\`, \`def eval(\`, \`yaml.load(..., Loader=SafeLoader)\`, \`torch.load(..., weights_only=True)\`, \`regex.exec()\`, an \`===\` comparison with innerHTML, \`hashlib.md5(data)\`, a script with integrity=, whole-line comments and non-code files. Every rule is linear: a guard reads the call's balanced arguments across lines, at most MAX_CALL_CHARS (400) of them and at most MAX_CALLS_PER_LINE (8) calls a line (_call_args, agents/core/code_guidance.py:211; _guarded, agents/core/code_guidance.py:226), or the tag it matched. scan (agents/core/code_guidance.py:265) returns \`{rule, line, message}\`, at most 20 findings over the first 1 MB, with lines split at \`\\n\` only (CRLF and CR normalised), and stops after SCAN_SECONDS (0.5 s; agents/core/code_guidance.py:50); a scan cut by size or time ends with a \`scan-incomplete\` finding at the first line it did not finish, so a cut scan never reads as clean. \`.env\`, \`.env.\*\` and the shell dotfiles are scanned as shell. The findings go to five places. On the file_write approval card, FileTools.classify_mutation (agents/core/file_tools.py:1561) adds \`code_warnings\` (rule@line, at most 200 characters), \`code_warning_count\` and a title notice (\`code not fully scanned\` when a limit cut it), scanning the name as spelled and the file the write lands on (a symlink, a \`./\` or \`//\` spelling; labels, agents/core/code_guidance.py:296, names each finding once and in line order); it never sets a class, so H506's approval binding is untouched, and an instruction-file notice and the warning share the title. The gated call's \`approval_required\` answer carries \`code_warnings\`/\`code_warning_count\` (_ANSWER_LABEL_KEYS, agents/core/tool_rpc.py:213), and the tool loop's pause reply names them as warnings, not refusals (_approval_reply, agents/core/agent_runtime.py:2055): the loop ends the turn there, so the model reads them on its next turn and the owner at once. On an ungated write's result (FileTools.write_file, agents/core/file_tools.py:1308), the model reads \`code_warnings\` with a \`code_guidance\` note that they are warnings; an approved write's result lands on the approved task's record, which no model turn reads. A refused write carries none, and a failing scan never fails a write. For a marketplace install (agents/core/skills/marketplace.py:858; install and install-zip answer \`code_warnings\` when there are any, agents/core/routers/skills.py:495) and a generated skill (agents/core/skills/loader.py:1267), scan_tree (agents/core/code_guidance.py:340) walks the folder, skipping symlinks; only code files count toward its 200-file bound, a file past 1 MB is read as cut, the whole walk stops after TREE_SECONDS (2 s), and the file a bound stops at gets a \`scan-incomplete\` finding. skill_propose answers the generated skill's \`code_warnings\` (agents/core/skills/tools.py:891), and generate_skill resets them first (agents/core/skills/loader.py:1107), so a skipped generation never keeps another's; the background-review and \[learn:\] generation paths only log them (their main.py is a fixed template). The owner's switch is \`security.code_guidance\` (read by enabled, agents/core/code_guidance.py:161: on by default, only an explicit off turns it off and an unreadable store keeps it on; the settings row is seeded on in settings_db DEFAULTS, and safe mode forces it back on: safe_mode.FORCED_SETTINGS, agents/core/safe_mode.py:117). An aliased child_process module (\`cp.exec\`) is not flagged. tests/test_h507_code_guidance.py (136 cases) covers every rule firing, the guard cases, the cross-language scoping, the finding shape, the table size, the workflow rule with a blank line in a block and every non-run key, the bounds, the labels, the switch, the real ToolRPC card and approved execution, a clean and a non-code write, the shared instruction notice, a failing scan, a refused write, scan_tree (symlink, bounds, switch), generation, install with the route, and the setting row. The review round added crafted megabytes (one per quadratic rule) scanned in under a second and a card labelled promptly through the ToolRPC intake, the time and size cuts, the pause reply driven through the agent loop, skill_propose's warnings and the reset, the symlink and path spellings, a package padded with assets, the \`- run: \|\` block, the wrapped and nested calls, the child_process and createCipher spellings, CR/form-feed/U+2028 lines, the dotfiles and the safe-mode switch. Because DNS rebinding makes the browser treat those responses as same-origin, an attacker page still reads the full Prometheus body (route templates, request counters, latency buckets) and the /readyz body naming the configured LLM backend and the agent/channel counts. It drops the file-mutation verifier footer (_VERIFIER_FOOTER, agents/core/voice/speech_text.py:42), \<think\>/\<thinking\>/\<reasoning\> blocks (an unclosed one to the end, and everything before a closing tag that never opened), fenced code (\`\`\` or ~~~, an unclosed fence to the end) and HTML tags. \[text\](url) reads as its text, !\[alt\](url) as its alt, and a bare or \<autolinked\> URL as "link". Headings, list items, task boxes, block quotes and table rows lose their markers and end with a full stop (_line, agents/core/voice/speech_text.py:133); table cells read with commas; separator rows and rules are dropped. Bold, italic, strikethrough and inline-code markers go and their words stay (_inline, agents/core/voice/speech_text.py:122), with word guards so 2\*3\*4 and my_var_name survive. Symbols are said in the reply's language (_symbols, agents/core/voice/speech_text.py:113, WORDS, agents/core/voice/speech_text.py:88): & as and/și, % as percent/la sută, -\> =\> as to/spre, degrees as degrees/grade; the language comes from the request, else a ro-RO voice, else the engine default (speech_lang, agents/core/voice/speech_text.py:104). Verifier footer (the clause the 2026-10-10 repair closed). Only the pinned producer's exact shape is removed from speech, and only from speech: the whole warning sentence with the warning sign (with or without U+FE0F), a positive count of at most twenty digits, and a contiguous block of at least one two-space-indented bullet with text, on its own lines, LF or CRLF. Preceding and following prose is kept. Near misses stay spoken exactly as ordinary prose: a header with no bullet, an empty bullet, a count of 0, a count of twenty-one digits, no warning sign, a lone leading space, and ordinary talk about verification. The visible chat text is untouched. Wiring. TTSEngine.speak normalises before any backend, Fish included, and synthesises nothing when nothing is left (speak, agents/core/voice/tts.py:213, normalised at agents/core/voice/tts.py:229; speech_for, agents/core/voice/tts.py:208). speak_stream normalises the whole reply before splitting sentences (agents/core/voice/tts.py:312), so a code, reasoning or footer block spanning sentences is dropped whole, and each sentence is then normalised again without change. Through TTSEngine.speak this covers the wake-word VoicePipeline, VoiceChannel.send and chat voice notes: speakable() is for_speech plus its cap (agents/core/channels/spoken_reply.py:69). POST /tts answers 204 with X-Nerva-Speech: nothing_to_say instead of synthesising (agents/core/routers/voice.py:76), and /tts/stream frames carry the spoken sentences. SpeechStreamFilter (frontend/src/speech-text.ts:155) drops a fenced block, a reasoning block or a footer whose markers arrive split across token deltas, holding back only a bounded tail that could still become one, and flushes cleanly. frontend/src/voice.ts uses it on the live sentence stream (frontend/src/voice.ts:297) and normalises each sentence (frontend/src/voice.ts:318); a 204 is silence, never an empty clip or the fallback voice (frontend/src/voice.ts:330). Hermes are opt (faster-whisper local, \`local_command\`, Groq, OpenAI, Mistral Voxtral cu diarizare și timestamp-uri pe cuvânt, xAI, ElevenLabs Scribe, DeepInfra) plus provideri pe comandă de shell, un ABC \`TranscriptionProvider\`, selecție explicită strictă cu auto-detect doar la o instalare neconfigurată vreodată, un plafon pe lungimea promptului Whisper, trunchierea liniștii înainte de upload ca să scadă octeții trimiși, un picker și \`POST /api/audio/transcribe\`. Nimic din astea nu e livrat. Nu din lene: clauza de guvernanță a rândului spune că orice STT în cloud trece prin \`plugin.egress\` și trimite vorbirea înregistrată a owner-ului în afara cutiei — e aceeași clasă de dezvăluire ca TTS-ul în cloud și trebuie clasificat, nu pus ca implicit de config. Cache-ul motorului stă tot în \`routers/voice.py\`, care e casa greșită pentru el; canalul îl importă în loc să-l dubleze, iar mutarea lui e o schimbare separată. NEVERIFICAT pe servicii reale: niciun model Whisper încărcat cu adevărat. [d1](../agents/core/voice/stt.py) [d2](../agents/core/voice/hallucination.py) [d3](../agents/core/channels/inbound_voice.py) |
| <a id="h530"></a>H530 | Not turn a silent recording into a message | copy | Echivalent | Reevaluat | Whisper nu tace când nu aude nimic — inventează. Pe liniște întoarce o propoziție fluentă din datele de antrenament: generice de subtitrare („Subtitles by the Amara.org community", „Subtitrarea: ..."), formule de încheiere („Thanks for watching!", „Mulțumesc pentru vizionare!"). Pentru o casetă de dictare e o enervare; aici e un control de siguranță, exact cum spune clauza de guvernanță a rândului: un mesaj vocal devine o tură \*inbound\*, o tură inbound poate cere lucruri, deci un transcript halucinat e o instrucțiune pe care n-a autorizat-o nimeni, intrată într-un sistem guvernat. \`hallucination.py\` o oprește. Designul e dictat de asimetria erorilor: a pierde un mesaj real e inacceptabil (cineva zice „mulțumesc" și dispare fără răspuns), a lăsa unul să treacă costă o tură ignorabilă. De aici două niveluri, nu o listă: frazele distinctive (\`CANNED\`) cad pe text; cele pe care oamenii chiar le spun (\`AMBIGUOUS\`) cad doar când durata \*decodată\* arată că înregistrarea era prea scurtă ca să le conțină — iar un apelant care nu știe durata le păstrează. Potrivirea e pe transcriptul întreg, niciodată pe substring; regula pentru generice cere marker ȘI vocabular exclusiv de generic, fiindcă prima variantă (doar markerul) mânca „am văzut pe amara.org un film bun". Filtrul rulează în \`STTEngine.transcribe\` și întoarce \`\[silence\]\` — santinela care exista deja și pe care fiecare apelant o tratează ca „nu s-a spus nimic" — deci ruta de dictare din browser o primește gratuit, nu doar calea nouă de pe Telegram. CORECTARE la auditul din 07.09: verdictul „missing" era pe jumătate greșit. A doua cerință a rândului — auto-stop pe liniște (VAD), ca utilizatorul să nu apese o tastă — EXISTĂ de mult în \`frontend/src/voice.ts\`: \`recordUtterance\` eșantionează RMS la 60 ms și oprește după \`SILENCE_MS\`, cu plafon dur și abandon când nimeni nu vorbește. Auditul a dat un \`rg -i 'vad'\` peste \`frontend/src/\` și a raportat „nimic relevant"; linia 111 spune „VAD" în litere. Ce lipsea cu adevărat era dovada: nimic nu o testa, fiindcă harness-ul comun folosește un MediaRecorder care se oprește singur și scurtcircuitează intervalul. \`voice-vad.test.tsx\` folosește unul care NU se oprește niciodată singur — dacă o tură se termină acolo, doar detectorul de liniște a putut-o termina — și acoperă fereastra de liniște, plafonul, abandonul și faptul că vorbirea continuă resetează ceasul. Named speech compatibility review: the Whisper hallucination filter and decoded-duration handling remain on the native transcribe path; named commands preserve the existing exact-sentinel behavior. Hallucination and speech selection regressions pass. [d1](../agents/core/voice/hallucination.py) [d2](../agents/core/voice/stt.py) [d3](../frontend/src/voice.ts) |

| <a id="h537"></a>H537 | Search the web and pull clean page content | update | Echivalent | Reevaluat | Rescue-versus-policy classification and the operator site policy are consistent across callers. A DNS resolution failure or empty DNS answer from an owner-configured search backend is ProviderFailure('dns_failed') via web_providers.classified()/is_dns_failure (rescued once, reported as provider_failed, retryable); allowlist, kernel e-stop and SSRF 'unsafe address' refusals stay PolicyBlock and are never rescued (test_a_dns_failure_is_a_failure_not_a_policy_block). This is a different surface from page reads: the search URL is the owner's, so there is no name oracle, while a model-chosen page URL that does not resolve now reads url_refused like a private address (H310). This round: (a) WebSearchPlugin.search() (websearch.py:394) now drops rows from JARVIS_WEB_BLOCKED_DOMAINS sites, so the gatherer, research handler and tech scout follow the same policy as the tools (test_search_rows_from_blocked_sites_are_dropped_for_direct_callers_too); search_detailed stays unfiltered so web_search still reports its blocked count; (b) a rescue provider that was asked and also failed is attributable (SearchOutcome.rescue_tried, websearch.py:385; web_search carries rescue_tried), because a second party saw the query (test_a_failed_rescue_names_the_second_party_that_saw_the_query). Unchanged: provider ABC and manifest-checked registry, built-ins cannot be replaced or removed, providers get a two-value view, keyless DuckDuckGo is never a rescue target for unattended callers, the 15-minute cache never pins an empty answer. Residual risk: the DNS match depends on the wording of two messages in security/ssrf.py and http_client.py (a reword reverts to PolicyBlock; the test fails). Not live-proven: nothing dialled; fakes and MockTransport only. | <a id="h545"></a>H545 | Let the editor hand the agent MCP servers that exist only for that session | copy | Lipsă | Reevaluat | Every accepted part is missing: (1) an ACP session entry point (session/new, load, resume, fork) that accepts an mcpServers array; this depends on H542. (2) A session-scoped MCP registry layered over the global MCPManager, so that a server registered for one session is invisible to every other session and is torn down when the session ends. (3) Off-loop registration (asyncio.to_thread) with a bounded discovery join (default 1.5 s), so a dead server cannot block session creation. (4) A scheduled late refresh that re-reads the session's tool list after slow discovery finishes. (5) Governance: session-supplied servers pass through the same outbound MCP authorization gate as configured servers (H554, still partial), and their trust tier is capped at no wider than a configured server's. | <a id="h551"></a>H551 | Choose which of a server's tools the model may see | copy | Echivalent | Reevaluat | Filtrele allow/deny pe nume și glob (\`tools_allow\`/\`tools_deny\`, potrivite cu \`fnmatchcase\` pe numele original al uneltei) restrâng atât listarea, cât și apelarea uneltelor MCP; deny prevalează (\`tool_visible\`, agents/core/mcp/client.py:631-638). \`_list_tools\` nu oferă o unealtă ascunsă (:596-601), iar \`MCPServer.call_tool\` răspunde \`tool_filtered\` înainte să plece vreun frame (:616-617), deci scoaterea unei unelte din filtru o revocă imediat, și la apel, nu doar la înregistrare. Un filtru malformat îngustează, nu lărgește: un allow care nu e listă devine \`\[\]\` (\`_clean_tool_patterns\`, :124-135). Limitele (64 de pattern-uri / 128 de caractere, :120-121) sunt fail-closed. Ruta de add (\`admin_mcp_add\`, agents/core/routers/mcp.py:214-223) refuză cu 400 \`{"error": "invalid_tool_filter", "field": ...}\` un \`tools_allow\` sau \`tools_deny\` peste limite, în loc să-l taie (\`tool_patterns_over_bounds\`, client.py:142-158), la fel ca pe o valoare care nu e listă sau pe o intrare goală. Un deny care nu poate fi păstrat (peste 64 de pattern-uri, un pattern peste 128 de caractere, sau care nu e listă) venit dintr-un config editat manual prin \`load_from_config\` îngustează serverul la nimic (\`tools_allow = \[\]\`) și loghează un avertisment (:407-418), pentru că un deny tăiat ar face din nou vizibilă unealta pe care o numea. Filtrele fac round-trip prin \`to_config\`/\`load_from_config\` (:808-809, :852-853). Teste (tests/test_mcp_tool_filters.py, 13/13 verzi): listare și deny prevalează (tests/test_mcp_tool_filters.py:47-57), unealtă filtrată refuzată la apel pe nume (tests/test_mcp_tool_filters.py:60-70), filtru malformat → nimic și round-trip de config (tests/test_mcp_tool_filters.py:73-84), ruta primește filtre și refuză formele malformate (tests/test_mcp_tool_filters.py:98-109), ruta refuză 129 de caractere / 65 de intrări pe ambele câmpuri (tests/test_mcp_tool_filters.py:121-129) și acceptă un filtru exact la limită (tests/test_mcp_tool_filters.py:132-138), un deny imposibil de păstrat ascunde toate uneltele cu avertisment (tests/test_mcp_tool_filters.py:141-147), iar un config editat manual cu deny peste limite se încarcă fail-closed fără să atingă serverul vecin (tests/test_mcp_tool_filters.py:150-159). | <a id="h557"></a>H557 | Make a third-party tool schema safe and unambiguous for every model provider | copy | Echivalent | Reevaluat | Every third-party MCP tool schema is now repaired once, when the tool is registered and before any provider sees it, and each tool gets a provider-legal, prefixed name. MCPTool keeps the server's raw schema for diagnostics only and stores \`normalize_mcp_input_schema(input_schema)\` as \`input_schema\` (agents/core/mcp/client.py:350-385). \`_list_tools\` builds every listed tool through that constructor and replaces the previous listing instead of appending to it (agents/core/mcp/client.py:603-629). The normalizer is in agents/core/mcp/schema_normalize.py:323-360: - It promotes a root \`definitions\` block to \`$defs\`. A name defined differently in both blocks gets a fresh key (agents/core/mcp/schema_normalize.py:330-346). Every \`#/definitions/\` ref is rewritten. Only the root meta-keyword is promoted, so a property that happens to be called \`definitions\` stays as it is. - It collapses a Pydantic nullable \`anyOf\`/\`oneOf\` to its single non-null branch and drops \`default: null\` (agents/core/mcp/schema_normalize.py:127-167). - It infers a missing \`type\`, gives every object an explicit \`properties\` map, and prunes \`required\` to names that are actually declared (agents/core/mcp/schema_normalize.py:288-320). - It flattens a root \`anyOf\`/\`oneOf\`/\`allOf\`/\`$ref\`/\`enum\`/\`not\` so the root is always a plain object (agents/core/mcp/schema_normalize.py:356-357, agents/core/mcp/schema_normalize.py:554-589). \`mcp_provider_name\` builds \`mcp__\<server\>__\<tool\>\`. Anything outside \[A-Za-z0-9_\] becomes \`_\`, and a name over 64 characters is cut and given a digest suffix (agents/core/mcp/schema_normalize.py:601-611). \`MCPManager._provider_index\` renames pairs whose names collide after sanitizing and withholds any name that is still shared (agents/core/mcp/client.py:766-802). \`model_tools\` offers the normalized schema under the prefixed name. It withholds a tool whose name shadows a built-in or that the server's trust tier would refuse, and marks non-read-only tools as gated (agents/core/mcp/client.py:804-833). \`_resolve\` dispatches a prefixed name through the index, refuses a reserved built-in name, and returns \`ambiguous_tool\` instead of picking whichever server matched first (agents/core/mcp/client.py:851-888). The owner's include/exclude filters still match the original tool names (agents/core/mcp/client.py:631-638). These rows reach the model: - MCPModelBridge reserves the built-in names and takes the \`model_tools()\` rows (agents/core/mcp/model_bridge.py:83-91), then registers, re-registers or revokes them on the ToolRPC allowlist in \`sync\` (agents/core/mcp/model_bridge.py:113-147). - AutonomyCoordinator wires the bridge into the agent tool loop as its per-turn \`tool_sync\` (agents/core/autonomy_coordinator.py:1835-1840). - Gemini still applies its own projection on top of the repaired schema (agents/core/llm/tool_dialects.py:709-730). Tests: - \`definitions\` promotion: tests/test_mcp_schema_normalize.py:78-85. - Nullable collapse: tests/test_mcp_schema_normalize.py:101-112. - Anthropic, OpenAI Chat, OpenAI Responses and xAI all ship the repaired schema under a legal name (tests/test_mcp_schema_normalize.py:264-291). - Name shape and truncation: tests/test_mcp_schema_normalize.py:344-357. - Disambiguation after sanitizing: tests/test_mcp_schema_normalize.py:376-382. - A model call is dispatched end to end and its result is fenced: tests/test_mcp_schema_normalize.py:475-492. - Production coordinator wiring: tests/test_mcp_schema_normalize.py:1075-1121. - Root combinators are flattened on all five paths: tests/test_mcp_schema_normalize.py:1238-1247. - Name ambiguity is no longer first-wins: tests/test_mcp_hardening.py:41-74. | <a id="h574"></a>H574 | Shell completion and native search-index extensions | skip | Echivalent | Reevaluat | Both halves of the Hermes row are now in the code. Shell completion. \`nerva completion bash\|zsh\|fish\` is declared at agents/cli/nerva.py:748-749, and agents/cli/nerva.py:4784-4796 sends it to agents/cli/completion.py. That module walks the live argparse tree (agents/cli/completion.py:47-76), so a parser extension appears without touching the generator. It strips control characters out of each command's help text and caps it at one bounded line (agents/cli/completion.py:37-44). The root -p/--profile option completes the profile directories found on disk when the user presses Tab, plus \`default\`; the attached \`-pNAME\` form and the \`--profile=\` form are skipped or completed (agents/cli/completion.py:94-128). The bash, zsh and fish emitters (agents/cli/completion.py:131, :235, :327-430, dispatched at :433-443) emit every name, help line and path as quoted literal data. Real-shell tests cover: - help text in the listing: tests/test_cli_shell_completion.py:148-164 and tests/test_cli_fish_completion.py:88 - profile-name completion followed by the command path: tests/test_cli_shell_completion.py:209-228 and tests/test_cli_fish_completion.py:118-130 - hostile help text: tests/test_cli_shell_completion.py:180 and tests/test_cli_fish_completion.py:97 - parser extensions: tests/test_cli_fish_completion.py:69 CJK search. Python's sqlite3 cannot register a C FTS5 tokenizer, so agents/core/memory/cjk_fts.py does the same segmentation in Python on both sides of the index. On the stored side, every CJK run is rewritten as its unigrams and overlapping bigrams under a stock unicode61 tokenizer (agents/core/memory/cjk_fts.py:93-110). On the query side, a 1-character run matches its unigram, and a longer run must contain all of its bigrams, each quoted so FTS5 syntax in user text is never parsed (agents/core/memory/cjk_fts.py:116-135). MemoryStore keeps a memory_fts index: - It is backfilled, and rebuilt when the segmenter version changes (agents/core/memory/store.py:342-396). - A CJK query goes through MATCH and the candidates are re-checked for the exact substring, instead of the old LIKE scan (agents/core/memory/store.py:595-633). Session transcripts get a per-turn FTS5 index in agents/core/memory/session_index.py: - sync reindexes changed snapshots and drops orphans (agents/core/memory/session_index.py:438-486). - An incremental save hook updates the index (agents/core/memory/session_index.py:489-520). - A removal hook drops a deleted session's rows (agents/core/memory/session_index.py:523-555). - Deleted text is erased through FTS5 secure-delete (agents/core/memory/session_index.py:184). session_search answers from that index over the whole history (agents/core/memory/session_search.py:303-380). Tests: - 1- and 2-character CJK queries run MATCH and never LIKE (tests/test_memory_cjk_search.py:75-89). - A 1-character query reaches a session older than the old 200-session scan cap, which the scan misses (tests/test_session_search_index.py:65-82). - Erasure and owner-only file modes are covered in tests/test_session_index_erasure.py:84 and :236. Every page request still reads and hashes the whole admitted file (up to 50 MB) to find its cache entry, and the cache is per FileTools instance and in memory only. The budgets bound extracted text (32,000,000 bytes) and wall-clock time checked between pages/blocks, but not parser memory or decompression inside one page, nor the CPU of a single page's extraction; bulk ingestion remains separate. Garbled-text and image detection are heuristics: well-formed but wrong text, inline images, images nested in form XObjects and vector charts are not detected. Only the first 16 gap, garbled and image ranges are listed, with explicit omitted counts; no OCR is performed. Paging is by byte offset or whole-line window, but the output is not line-numbered. A missing parser is named (\`parser_missing\`) rather than installed lazily. Independent #1233 remaining limits: Formats stop at .pdf and .docx: no .ipynb, .xlsx, .doc, .ppt, .odt, .rtf or .epub, and the text comes back plain rather than converted to Markdown. There is no size refusal for documents (Hermes refuses over 50 MB): the whole file is parsed again on every page request, and max_bytes bounds only the text returned. There is no scanned-page coverage warning naming the page ranges that yielded no text, which the row calls the clever half. Paging is by byte offset, not a line offset/limit window. | <a id="h579"></a>H579 | Pull a file or slice of a file into a message inline (@ context references) | copy | Echivalent | Reevaluat | The owner's own chat attaches @file:path, @file:path#L10-40 and @file:"a b.md" for the turn. agents/core/context_refs.py holds the rules. expand (agents/core/context_refs.py:209) finds a reference that starts a word or follows an opening bracket, quote or backtick, and not one inside a word or a path (x@file:, a/@file:, @@file:) (_REF_RE, agents/core/context_refs.py:49); a double-quoted path may hold spaces, #L7 is one line and #L2-L3 a range, and trailing punctuation or a closing quote is not part of it. The routes keep the owner's message as typed: commands, skills, LLM-backend control, the router and memory see only it. The "--- Attached Context ---" section is bound to the turn (bind_attached, agents/core/context_refs.py:251; agents/web.py:1386 on /chat, and inside the stream task at agents/web.py:1484) and appended after the message only in the model prompt (attached_block, agents/core/context_refs.py:266; Orchestrator._build_agent_turn_text, agents/core/orchestrator.py:4017), so the file text is never stored as the owner's words, replayed in a later turn's history or embedded. Hermes keeps the expanded message in the user turn; Nerva shows the attachment to the model for the attaching (tainted) turn only. Each file's text is in a fence longer than any backtick run in it, so no line of it can close the fence (_fence, agents/core/context_refs.py:194), under a header that names the file as typed and the lines actually attached, \`(line 7)\` or \`(lines 2-3)\`, as attached file content, not instructions; injection patterns and a forged Attached Context marker are flagged in that header (\`flagged: …\`, _flags, agents/core/context_refs.py:180), not withheld. Each path is resolved through the same FileScope as file_read (_attach_one, agents/core/context_refs.py:133), so outside the file roots, .. traversal, a symlink escape and a secret-looking path such as .env are refused. A missing file, a directory, a binary file (a NUL in its first 8 KB), a bad line range, a range past the end, an unreadable file, an over-long name, a denied stat and an unknown ~user each become a one-line warning in the same section instead of failing the message. With JARVIS_FILE_ROOTS unset, the file tools' default root \<data home\>/workspace is used; only an unusable JARVIS_FILE_ROOTS makes the section say nothing was attached. The limits are 8 distinct references per message, 64 KB per reference and 128 KB in all, counted in bytes. A cut reference says so, and a repeated one is attached once. A line range skips the lines before it a 64K-character chunk at a time, up to 64M characters into the file (MAX_SCAN_CHARS; past it, the warning "line N is too far into the file"), keeps at most the byte budget and never reads a line whole (_read_lines, agents/core/context_refs.py:105); invalid UTF-8 is read with replacement characters. The expansion runs on /chat and /chat/stream (agents/web.py:1375, agents/web.py:1608), off the event loop, so both the HUD and nerva chat get it; the one message that skips it is a raw checkpoint command (\`/rollback\` or \`/checkpoints\` as the whole message, checkpoint_command_name), which never becomes a model turn, so nothing is read, bound or tainted for it. It never runs for a channel message, as Hermes' gateway does not expand either. A turn that attached anything is tainted: handle_input and handle_input_stream call _taint_attached_context (agents/core/orchestrator.py:397, :2372, :2593), which raises the turn's action origin to recall:untrusted. An action planned from attached content therefore escalates GRANT to QUEUE at the kernel, while an inbound turn keeps its more specific origin. complete (agents/core/context_refs.py:272) lists in-scope completions for what follows @file:, with directories ending in / and a path with a space quoted (a name no reference could name is left out). It shows dot files only when asked and never secret paths or links out of the roots, is bounded to 50 entries, and returns nothing for a prefix over 1,024 characters. GET /api/context-refs (agents/core/routers/commands.py:63, user-guarded, read-only) serves it and the reference types, and answers 503 file_roots_unusable when the roots cannot be used. The HUD composer (frontend/src/cockpit.tsx:229, :284, frontend/src/context-refs.tsx) offers the reference types while \`@\` or \`@fi\` is typed (Tab takes \`@file:\`), then the in-scope paths; a list is shown only for the text it was fetched for. tests/test_h579_context_refs.py (70 cases) covers the bounds, parsing, whole files, line ranges (single, L-form, past the end), every refusal and warning, a symlink, punctuation, word starts, dedupe, the byte cut, the shared budget, the reference limit, an unreadable file, invalid UTF-8, the roots, an explicit scope and the marker; completion (prefixes, dot files, secrets, roots, a long prefix, a file or missing folder, the bound); both routes, the completion route, the turn taint on both paths, and an inbound turn. The review round added attached text never read as the owner's command (a slash command, a skill, a backend switch) and never stored or carried to a later turn, through the real routes; a file that cannot close its fence; injection and a forged marker flagged; a range in one huge line bounded in memory and a range of many short lines linear; a range too far into a file; quoted paths and their completion; references after brackets and quotes and not inside words; the distinct-reference limit; the header's path and lines; paths the system refuses to look at; and the roots. frontend/src/test/context-refs.test.tsx has 6 cases. | <a id="h586"></a>H586 | Paste or attach a screenshot into the conversation (vision & image paste) | update | Echivalent | Reevaluat | Both intake halves of the accepted adaptation exist: the HUD composer and the terminal. useComposerImages (frontend/src/composer-images.tsx) takes image paste and drag-drop (frontend/src/composer-images.tsx:113-114) plus a file chooser, and accepts at most eight PNG/JPEG/GIF/WebP images of up to 4 MiB each (frontend/src/composer-images.tsx:4-5); the shared InputBar wires paste and drop in (frontend/src/cockpit.tsx:247). Each draft is first reviewed against the server (prepare / selected-prepare with image digests, destination binding, data-policy and remote/training/cost acknowledgements), and App.submit sends an image draft to runVision (frontend/src/app.tsx:538, frontend/src/app.tsx:504). runVision picks one of three routes (frontend/src/vision-turn.ts:8): POST /api/vlm/composer/describe-prepared (agents/core/routers/composer_vision.py:499), POST /api/vlm/composer/chat-prepared for a selected main route (agents/core/routers/composer_vision.py:584) or POST /api/vlm/composer/selected-chat for a selected Ollama route (agents/core/routers/composer_vision.py:1092); the router is registered at agents/web.py:1743. All three routes check data-URI signatures and bound raster decoding (validate_raster, agents/core/routers/composer_vision.py:61) and refuse a malformed body with its first reason instead of FastAPI's echoing 422 (_BoundedValidationRoute, agents/core/routers/composer_vision.py:28). describe-prepared and chat-prepared also refuse a non-local destination without the owner's acknowledgement (agents/core/routers/composer_vision.py:718) and call VLMBackend.generate_vision_checked (agents/core/llm/vlm.py:460); selected-chat is local Ollama only, refusing any remote acknowledgement (agents/core/routers/composer_vision.py:985-987) and streaming /api/chat itself (agents/core/routers/composer_vision.py:1051); the H277 native adapters (OpenRouter, DeepInfra, Nous, Claude, Gemini, Responses, xAI), empty-reply recovery and reply normalization sit behind that guard. The terminal: \`nerva chat --image PATH\` (repeatable, up to eight) and \`--clipboard-image\` (agents/cli/nerva.py:641-644) turn the chat verb into a vision turn (dispatch at agents/cli/nerva.py:4013, _vision_turn at agents/cli/nerva.py:4390) that refuses --agent/--session/--reasoning and never posts to /chat. Files are typed by signature (_image_mime, agents/cli/nerva.py:4127; _read_image, agents/cli/nerva.py:4137); the clipboard is read by wl-paste, xclip, pngpaste/osascript or PowerShell (_clipboard_command, agents/cli/nerva.py:4218; _clipboard_image, agents/cli/nerva.py:4328) under a bounded, deadline-killed reader (_run_reader, agents/cli/nerva.py:4243), and an off-machine destination needs --remote-vision naming it (agents/cli/nerva.py:4479). Governance gap found on this re-read: the previous verdict rested on isolation (the vision answer a client-only transcript entry, ordinary turns posting only {message, agent} to /chat/stream). Since #1233/#1246 that holds only for describe-prepared and the terminal. The chat-prepared and selected-chat routes commit the image-derived question/answer pair into the durable conversation (orch.complete_selected_image_turn at agents/core/routers/composer_vision.py:619-623 and agents/core/routers/composer_vision.py:1065), and later text turns in that session post to /chat/stream with the session_id (frontend/src/app.tsx:431-432) and read that history. That history is now governed (H586 fix, 2026-10-12, c9f67240, 0631eeb9, 9a485766, 44b53b51, 0bc59ec5 and 307b33eb): every later chat turn runs _guard_media_history (agents/core/orchestrator.py:2445-2463) at both turn entries (agents/core/orchestrator.py:2563 and agents/core/orchestrator.py:2807), which reads the session history and, when any turn carries media, raises the turn's action origin through mark_turn_recall_tainted, so a side-effecting action derived from that history is queued for approval (ASK) instead of auto-granted, and an unreadable history marks the turn too; one-shot completions (process/process_detailed: the autonomy _llm executor, nightly reflection, the summarize route) run the same guard inside an action-origin binding scoped to the call (agents/core/orchestrator.py:2310-2312), so the mark never leaks to the caller; image turns are embedded with taint metadata (taint_source external:image, agents/core/memory/manager.py:344-347), so recalling the image reading in any later turn taints that turn through the existing RAG guard, and a session_search hit on a turn carrying media is flagged image_derived and taints the turn too (agents/core/memory/session_search.py:241-242 and agents/core/memory/session_search.py:410-414; the FTS5 index path keeps each turn's media flag, agents/core/memory/session_search.py:362-363, so an indexed hit is flagged the same way), and, since the model's call runs search_sessions in a worker thread whose own mark cannot reach the turn, the production mechanism is the registered tool handler declaring tainted on its result (agents/core/memory/session_search.py:451-453), which the agent tool loop reads as declared_taint and turns into the turn's mark; and a session holding a media turn is never promoted to durable memory, like a foreign import: _session_has_media (agents/core/orchestrator.py:2465-2470) stops the per-turn learning review (agents/core/orchestrator.py:4185 and agents/core/orchestrator.py:4342), the LivingMemory feed (agents/core/orchestrator.py:4423) /refine, which answers image_history_not_promotable (agents/core/orchestrator.py:4301-4302), and nightly reflection, whose KG/core-lesson consolidation skips a window holding a committed image turn (agents/core/autonomy/reflection.py:169-170); /undo, on the web (agents/core/orchestrator.py:2008-2010) and on channels (agents/core/channels/session_lifecycle.py:251-253), copies the kept turns with their media provenance, so an undo cannot launder the image reading into trusted history. tests/test_h586_image_history_taint.py pins the QUEUE verdict through the real kernel authorize (with a stubbed history and with a real MemoryManager after a committed image turn), the untouched text-only origin, the fail-safe mark, both entries' call order, a one-shot completion over image history running tainted without leaking the mark, the tainted embedding read back through rag_guard, and the refusals of review, LivingMemory and /refine, a web /undo keeping the provenance (guard, promotion gate and tainted re-embedding) and nightly reflection skipping the image window and a session_search hit on an image reading tainting the turn, directly and through ToolRPCServer.handle (13 cases, red before the change). Stated limits: the guard reads the held history, which keeps the newest 100 turns, so a media turn that has aged out of it no longer marks later turns (its embedding stays tainted), and with the opt-in memory.compression_summarizer the per-session summary cache can carry image-derived text past that window. The owner can add more as \`\<data root\>/personalities/\<name\>.md\`, and an owner file may shadow a built-in. Owner files go through the same injection scan as a SOUL body on every turn (agents/core/cognition/personality_presets.py:123-143). Empty, oversize, non-UTF-8 or unreadable files are never applied, and they are reported with the reason (agents/core/cognition/personality_presets.py:91-120). \*\*Per-session and global choice.\*\* PersonalityOverlayStore keeps a choice for each conversation and a hub-wide default in personality_overlays.json. A conversation's own choice, including an explicit \`none\`, wins over the hub-wide default (agents/core/cognition/personality_presets.py:163-238). The owner-tier \`/personality\` command (agents/core/commands.py:558-631, registered at agents/core/commands.py:663-664) does five things: - lists the presets and what is in force; - switches the current conversation mid-session with \`\<name\>\`; - runs the conversation on the plain SOUL with \`none\`/\`off\`; - forgets the conversation's choice with \`default\`/\`reset\`; - sets or clears the hub-wide default with \`global \<name\|none\>\`. No form writes a SOUL file or a prompt version. \*\*Position in the prompt stack.\*\* overlay_block (agents/core/cognition/personality_presets.py:261-278) wraps the preset in a delimited block. The block says it changes tone and form only. _build_agent_turn_text adds it right after the SOUL persona block and before agent context, core memory and the project convention files (agents/core/orchestrator.py:4024-4043, helper at agents/core/orchestrator.py:3930-3938). Because it rides in the per-turn text, the cached system prompt is unchanged. \*\*Safe mode.\*\* In safe mode no overlay is applied and the \`personality_overlays\` layer is noted (agents/core/cognition/personality_presets.py:270-272, layer at agents/core/safe_mode.py:89-90). The command refuses every write (agents/core/commands.py:599-602). \*\*Deleting a conversation.\*\* It drops that conversation's choice (agents/core/orchestrator.py:2161-2166). \*\*Documentation.\*\* docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:902-923 documents the SOUL-vs-preset separation and the safe-mode behaviour. \*\*Tests.\*\* tests/test_personality_presets.py covers: - mid-session switching and every reset form (tests/test_personality_presets.py:131-145); - refusal of unknown and blocked presets (tests/test_personality_presets.py:157-164); - the owner-only tier (tests/test_personality_presets.py:168-170); - the SOUL and its version history staying untouched (tests/test_personality_presets.py:174-183); - the prompt-stack order on the real turn builder (tests/test_personality_presets.py:190-211); - safe-mode suppression and write refusal (tests/test_personality_presets.py:234-266); - ignored-file reporting and both forget paths (tests/test_personality_presets.py:269-300). tests/test_h490_safe_mode_posture.py:61 pins the new layer's position. With tests/test_soul_local_override.py and tests/test_h10_22_prompt_versioning.py, the four files gave 111 passed under python3.12. There are 6 built-ins against Hermes' 14. Hermes' custom presets are covered by unlimited owner files, so this does not count as a remaining gap. Every file is resolved through FileScope (outside the roots, symlink escape and secret paths refused), must be a regular file (a FIFO is never opened), and is bounded to 20 KB, with 40 KB and 12 files a turn and 8 rules a directory (agents/core/project_context.py:65-68), shared by parallel tool calls under the turn's lock; a cut says how much was shown, a file past the budget is named, and files past a count cap are counted (load_file, agents/core/project_context.py:220; collect, agents/core/project_context.py:239; render, agents/core/project_context.py:274). Each file's text and name are scanned with detect_injection_normalized, plus Unicode TAG characters (decoded and scanned) and the fence's markers (_detect, agents/core/project_context.py:122). A flagged file becomes a \[BLOCKED ...\] line naming the rules (injection_flag_names) with none of its text, and a flagged name is withheld; other names have non-printable characters escaped and undecodable bytes replaced. The caveated block, which holds the files in the untrusted-data fence, sits after the core-memory block in _build_agent_turn_text (agents/core/orchestrator.py:4037-4043); _begin_project_context (agents/core/orchestrator.py:407-435) builds it off the event loop at turn start in both turn paths (agents/core/orchestrator.py:2580 and agents/core/orchestrator.py:2832) and marks the turn recall-tainted when any file was given, so an action planned from it escalates GRANT to QUEUE. A noted directory's files are in every later turn of the session, so those turns are tainted too: web_search, web_extract and memory writes refuse until the setting is off or the hub restarts. A guest's turn is given none of them. It is off with llm.project_context_files (agents/core/project_context.py:74) and in safe mode (layer project_context, agents/core/safe_mode.py:82, named on the HUD banner; enabled, agents/core/project_context.py:312). tests/test_h594_project_context.py: 66 cases. | <a id="h652"></a>H652 | Add a tool to the agent, understand how a turn executes, and export turns as training data | keep | Echivalent | Reevaluat | Current e074fbc6 reread: plain generation records the trajectory prompt only after final rendered system/steering and prepared-route checks accept the actual candidate. Refused or stale steering cannot be recorded as a completed provider request. Existing owner-private trajectory files, tool-loop degradation and export evidence retain their scope; no physical wire capture or objective-success claim is added. Each turn can now be saved in full and exported as training data. Saving is opt-in through NERVA_SAVE_TRAJECTORIES. Agent.generate_response opens a per-turn recorder (agents/core/agent.py:986). On the plain path it records the prompt with steering folded in (agents/core/agent.py:1144). The tool loop records the guided system prompt and the tool definitions it offered to the provider (agents/core/agent_runtime.py:777-778). After an H672 compaction fold it records the refreshed offer and the rebuilt system prompt again (agents/core/agent_runtime.py:877 and :861). TrajectoryRecorder.note_tools keeps the union of every tool offered during the turn, capped at MAX_TOOLS (agents/core/trajectory.py:168-188). to_record writes one redacted, clipped record per turn that holds the system prompt, the tools, each step with its tool calls and results, the reply and the exit reason (agents/core/trajectory.py:229-259). Trajectory files are owner-only. _append_private creates the directory as 0700 and opens the file with O_CREAT\|O_NOFOLLOW\|O_BINARY and mode 0600 before it writes any byte. It also narrows a file or directory that an earlier version left wider (agents/core/trajectory.py:368-391). A backend failure can come back through the tool loop as a plain ToolTurn whose exit is model_response. Such a turn is now recorded as degraded with completed=false, using the strict llm.base.is_backend_failure_reply signal. A real answer that opens with "\[" stays completed (agents/core/agent.py:1006-1025; agents/core/llm/base.py:221). There are two export shapes: - to_sharegpt renders the Hermes ShareGPT shape: a system turn carrying a \<tools\> block, \<tool_call\> and \<tool_response\> JSON, a think block on every gpt turn, and the parallel results of one step joined into a single tool turn (agents/core/trajectory.py:479-503). - to_messages renders OpenAI SFT rows with a tools column (agents/core/trajectory.py:506-529). Both are served by the admin route GET /sessions/{id}/trajectories (agents/core/routers/sessions.py:222-249) and by \`nerva sessions export ID --sharegpt\` (agents/cli/nerva.py:3454-3477). So the export is no longer only the standalone training/prepare_data.py script, which writes one user/assistant pair per trace (training/prepare_data.py:21). Tools self-register through ToolRPCServer.register_tool (agents/core/tool_rpc.py:477). Adding a tool is now covered by a public developer doc with a skill-vs-tool rule, the two places to change, and a checklist (docs/developer/adding-a-tool.md:12, :54, :140). How a turn executes, including the loop's invariants, is documented in docs/developer/agent-loop.md:11-160, and ARCHITECTURE.md points to both (docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:977-980). The CLI wrapper hooks are a recorded design difference, not a missing feature. docs/decisions/2026-10-21-no-cli-extension-hooks.md says nerva is a one-shot verb CLI over the HTTP API with no TUI to hook into. It maps each customisation Hermes users reach for to an existing governed place in Nerva, and states when to revisit the decision. Tests: - tests/test_trajectory_export.py:328-348 checks that the offered tools are saved and exported in both formats. - tests/test_trajectory_export.py:426 checks that the saved human turn on the plain path is the steered prompt. - tests/test_trajectory_export.py:558-572 covers the CLI export. - tests/test_trajectory_export.py:199-251 checks that files and directories are 0600/0700 from creation with no window before the first write, that wider existing files are narrowed, and that files are written in binary mode. - tests/test_trajectory_export.py:138-160 checks that a Gemini or LM Studio failure returned through the tool loop is saved as degraded and not completed, while bracketed answers stay completed. - tests/test_h652_developer_docs.py:64-110 pins the docs, the static nerva dispatch with no dynamic code loading, and the decision record. | <a id="h665"></a>H665 | Editing several skills in one atomic, rollback-on-failure batch | update | Echivalent | Reevaluat | Final review at HEAD 57ed6db. The gap in the ledger entry was "no ordered multi-skill operations batch with all-or-nothing rollback, nor a teaching payload on the failing op". That gap is closed on this branch. What is in the code now: - normalize() takes one ordered operations array. Each operation names its own skill and uses one of create, patch, write_file, remove_file or delete (agents/core/skills/batch.py:50, agents/core/skills/batch.py:167-222). - A create that comes after another operation on the same skill is refused with skill_batch_create_not_first (agents/core/skills/batch.py:208-213). - A delete in a batch of more than one operation is refused with skill_batch_delete_not_alone (agents/core/skills/batch.py:214-218). - run_batch applies every operation to staging copies first and touches nothing live until every operation and final check passes (agents/core/skills/batch.py:693-742). It then swaps the live folders one at a time. If the swap or the signature/approval renewal fails, it reverses every folder already swapped and reports skill_batch_apply_failed with rolled_back (agents/core/skills/batch.py:756-782). Replaced folders are archived (agents/core/skills/batch.py:783-793). - A failing operation returns a teaching payload: failed_op, hints and file_preview (agents/core/skills/batch.py:90-100). A patch whose old_string does not match also gets the closest line and a preview of the file at that point (agents/core/skills/batch.py:460-475). - Owner path: POST /api/skills/batch, admin only, with dry_run (agents/core/routers/skills.py:1027). - Model path: skill_propose {operations} does a dry run and records the batch with one approval card for the whole set (agents/core/skills/tools.py:941-1022, agents/core/skills/batch.py:860-876). - Only the bound card's own status in the queue applies the batch, and it applies against the skill fingerprints that were checked (agents/core/skills/batch.py:889-917, agents/core/routers/actions.py:147-160). The approval judge never scores a batch card (agents/core/autonomy/approval_judge.py:644-646). This meets the governance requirement of one approval, not N. Review history, in brief: - Two adversarial skeptics passed the row. - Round 4 fixed a binary-diff hole. _diffs now decodes the old and new bytes separately (agents/core/skills/batch.py:529, agents/core/skills/batch.py:555-560). Text that replaces a binary file is shown whole with every line marked as added (agents/core/skills/batch.py:534-538). Non-UTF-8 added bytes are flagged added_unreadable (agents/core/skills/batch.py:544-546), and skill_propose refuses those with skill_batch_unreviewable (agents/core/skills/tools.py:993-1000). - The skeptic's last finding was a removed binary file shown as "binary file replaced by text". It was fixed with the red-first test tests/test_skill_batch.py:590, so it now reads "(binary)". - The frontend now builds the diff only when the owner opens the fold (frontend/src/panels/skill-batches.tsx:73, frontend/src/panels/skill-batches.tsx:81, frontend/src/panels/skill-batches.tsx:85). Honest limits: - The model path cannot propose a change that adds non-text bytes. The owner route can. - Rollback during the swap is best effort. If a folder cannot be renamed back, it is reported as not_rolled_back and its old copy is kept in staging for the owner, not hidden. Tests, each run twice at HEAD: - tests/test_skill_batch.py: 40 passed and 40 passed (one unrelated warning). - frontend vitest src/test/skill-batches.test.tsx: 10 passed and 10 passed.
