| <a id="h670"></a>H670 | The default identity prompt is a behavior contract, and it lives in one file | update | Echivalent | Reevaluat | The shared identity band exists. agents/_identity/IDENTITY.md is one behaviour contract: the reply-sizing rule (match length to the weight of the ask), earned depth, the named prohibitions (no filler, no restating the request, no re-summarizing, no narrating visible tool calls), the anti-sycophancy line ('agree because it is right, not because the owner said it') and 'say when you do not know'. Its reply rules govern the agent's own replies to the owner: text drafted in someone else's voice (an email, a post, a message written as the owner) keeps that voice, greetings and sign-offs included, and a persona's warmth or curiosity lives inside the answer (review-H670 m-5); its honesty rules hold for everything an agent writes, drafted text included (review-H670b m-1). Its leading maintainer note (stripped before the model sees it, _strip_maintainer_note, agents/core/agent.py:453) says never to add 'be targeted and efficient in your exploration', and why. The repo-root SOUL.md mirrors the text, so agents working on the repo read the contract the product ships; a test keeps the two equal. identity_path (agents/core/agent.py:438) resolves it as soul_path_for does a persona: the data home's souls/IDENTITY.local.md, then a gitignored agents/_identity/IDENTITY.local.md, then the shipped file. read_identity (agents/core/agent.py:481) runs it through the same H387 helpers as a SOUL (the injection scan on the uncapped body, then the cap), announces a flagged or truncated contract (its blocked and quarantined stubs name the contract, not a persona), caps it at its own 4,000 characters (IDENTITY_MAX_CHARS, never above the persona's cap, so the two bands stay within the persona cap plus 4,000), and reads it once per settled file signature for the whole process. An override that cannot be read (not UTF-8, a directory, no permission) is reported at ERROR and the shipped contract used instead, cached against the shipped file's signature so an edit of it is seen; a contract that cannot be located or read at all leaves the agent without it; none of these stops an agent from being built. Agent.system_prompt (agents/core/agent.py:572) is the contract first, then the machine context when there is any (hint_block, agents/core/environment_hint.py:85: what Nerva detected about the host from H283 host_identity under its own heading, then the operator's JARVIS_ENVIRONMENT_HINT under its own heading; each is empty when nothing was detected or set), then the agent's persona (any part may be empty; an agent without a SOUL still gets the contract). Every place a system prompt is built uses it: Agent.process (agents/core/agent.py:1177) and the synthesis path in agent.py, and the orchestrator's two sites (agents/core/orchestrator.py:2957, agents/core/orchestrator.py:5306) through _system_prompt_of (agents/core/orchestrator.py:531). At a compaction boundary refresh_soul (agents/core/agent.py:741) re-reads the contract as it re-reads the persona (_refresh_identity, agents/core/agent.py:610): a few stats when unchanged; when the file that resolves is absent, vanishes before the read or cannot be read, the contract in force is kept, reported at the boundary as failed-open and warned once per episode (an override absent for an instant resolves to the shipped file for that boundary, as a persona's does); and a moved contract reported as rebuilt, so an edit reaches running agents without a restart. The contract in force at start is committed to the prompt VC (SoulVersionStore) as _identity (_record_identity_version, agents/core/orchestrator.py:513), a no-op when unchanged or empty, so its history is recorded and diffable through /api/admin/prompts/_identity/... beside the personas; what is served is the file (a rollback in the VC does not change it), and an edit picked up at a boundary is recorded at the next start. The prompt-size report counts it as a shared component every call pays (identity_component, agents/core/prompt_size.py:136), followed by the host-detected (agents/core/prompt_size.py:149) and environment-hint (agents/core/prompt_size.py:158) components, and the packaged build ships it through its agents/\*/\*.md glob (overrides, \*.local.md, never ship). IDENTITY.md and its .local overlay are in the H506 instruction-file class (INSTRUCTION_BASE_NAMES, agents/core/file_tools.py:368), so a file write to them asks as an instruction file; a test derives the class from every name the contract's and a persona's loaders can resolve. The data home's README lists souls/IDENTITY.local.md. Persona SOULs and Persona.prompt_block (agents/core/cognition/persona.py:142) stay the character layer on top. tests/test_identity_contract.py (18 cases) covers every rule's presence, the banned line's absence and the kept warning, the mirror, the scan verdict, every active agent's system prompt starting with the contract (and, with the host pinned to 'nothing detected' by an autouse fixture and no operator hint, exactly contract then persona), an agent without a persona, the orchestrator's helper and all four sites, both overrides and their order, the scan and the cap on an override, an edit reaching a running agent at the boundary, the one-stat unchanged path, a failed re-read keeping the last-good contract, the version record (once, and a failing store never stopping a start) and one read shared across agents; tests/test_h670b_identity_review.py (21 cases) covers the first review: the instruction-file class, a contract absent or vanishing at a boundary, a non-UTF-8 or unreadable override, the contract's own cap, no empty version, the start-time record, the contract's scope, a mid-file comment, the prompt-size component, the ERROR on a flagged contract, the stubs' wording and CHT-117; tests/test_h670c_identity_review.py (14 cases) covers the second review: honesty unscoped, a shipped contract that stops being UTF-8, a vanish before the real read, the hub's start recording the contract, one warning per episode and a second one, a reader that raises, the fallback following a shipped edit, a directory override, a permission error at load and at a boundary, the fallback rules once when both bands are blocked, and the docs. The first review (one major: the contract was outside the instruction-file class; seven minors: a missing contract emptied at a boundary, a non-UTF-8 override stopped every agent, the two bands exceeded the cap, the VC's rollback and A/B claim, the contract's unscoped rules against drafting personas and trait directives, six untested survivors, CHT-117 naming a retired agent; six nits) is answered; its six real survivors are pinned. The feature's 17 mutants were caught but one equivalent; the first review round's 15 were caught, one only against a stand-in (the vanish case, now driven through the real read). The second review (no major; three minors: the scope lifted the honesty rules from drafted text, a shipped contract that stopped being UTF-8 emptied the contract at a boundary, three real survivors; eight nits) is answered; its 31 mutants' three real survivors are pinned, and this round's 10 were all caught, two after their cases were added (a reader that raises, a second warning episode). Known limits: the prompt-size report measures the shipped contract, not an override in force (as it measures shipped personas); PromptRefresh.text is still the persona alone; the contract's scan verdict is reported only in the log (a persona's also reaches GET /api/agents/{id}/soul); the data home's README is written once, so an existing install does not get its new row. | <a id="h672"></a>H672 | A never-ending session picks up config, skill and tool changes at the compaction boundary | copy | Parțial | Reevaluat | \*\*The boundaries are opt-in, so on a shipped default nothing migrates\*\*: the conversation-level commit exists only with \`memory.context_compression\` on (default off) and the in-turn fold only with \`llm.tool_loop_enabled\` on (default off) — a default install still needs a restart for a persona edit, exactly as before. \*\*Execution-admission scope:\*\* production coordinator-wired agent-loop calls now recheck live profile authorization before preflight/intake, including between folds. This does not cancel an already-running tool or rewrite queued approvals; direct/script RPC and approved task execution retain their existing contracts. A standalone runtime wired only with \`tool_profile\` must explicitly supply the separate \`execution_profile\` hook to gain this check. The model's offered schemas and gate/taint views still refresh only at their existing boundaries. \*\*The persona migration is process-wide\*\*: \`orchestrator.agents\` is every agent and \`agent.soul\` is the one dict every session's system prompt reads, so the session that commits migrates the persona for all sessions (the boundary log line says so); refreshing only the routed agents would need the route at \`_history_for_prompt\`, which it does not have. The staged shared-route plan still measures the pre-publication persona. The final managed plain/stream dispatch now rechecks the expanded rendered request and refuses excess before sending. This containment does not prospectively reallocate history; a post-CAS refusal retains the accepted summary, clock and refreshed persona. The probe trusts the kernel's signature; what the builder reads outside the file (the scan patterns) is code and needs a restart. The prompt half covers the SOUL only: Nerva's plugin and skills sections live in the user prompt and were already per-turn, so there is no plugin section in the system prompt to fail open — the fail-open is exercised on the SOUL builder. The in-turn boundary does not rebuild \`messages\[0\]\`: a persona change reaches the \*next\* turn, not the loop in flight. "A newly configured MCP server appears without a restart" now holds at the turn boundary for every tool the MCP manager currently lists: the production coordinator wires \`MCPModelBridge.sync\` as the runtime's \`tool_sync\` (agents/core/autonomy_coordinator.py:1831-1840), and \`_run_turn\` awaits it before resolving the offer at the top of every turn (agents/core/agent_runtime.py:731-733), bounded to 5 s and keeping the registered offer if it fails (agents/core/agent_runtime.py:1518-1527); the sync registers, re-registers or revokes the bridge's tools on the ToolRPC allowlist (agents/core/mcp/model_bridge.py:113-147). The in-turn fold does not run that sync, so an MCP tool added or removed mid-loop reaches the offer on the next turn, not at the fold; whether the MCP manager itself connects a newly configured server without a restart was not verified by this row. The lineage row stays at \`nerva.context-compaction.v1\`; the boundary note is a log line plus the runtime event, not a field on the row. \`refresh_tools\` compares names, so a tool whose schema changed under the same name is adopted only because the fresh list is taken whenever the set moved, never on its own. The stale comment at \`agents/core/file_tools.py\` saying \`_load_soul\` runs no injection scan predates H387 and is left for a hygiene commit (it would drift five unrelated rows). Nine ledger rows cite \`agent.py\`, \`agent_runtime.py\` or \`orchestrator.py\` and were drifted by this branch (and by #1188 on main: its registry path in \`orchestrator.py\`, and the pairing kwarg, refusal branch and lifespan hand-over in \`telegram.py\` and \`web.py\`, which H146, H449, H364 and H671 also cite and were read against — the pairing store is not their subject); each was re-read against the diff on its cited paths before its hashes moved. Six keep their text and take fresh stamps — H146, H298, H363, H364, H449, H679: the in-turn re-resolution runs through \`_profiled\`, which still applies the job toolset on both sides of the profile, and the result-spill, cache, reasoning and job-pin mechanism those rows cite is untouched. Three are rewritten — H387: the ERROR line now comes from \`_announce_soul_verdict\` behind the \`_read_soul\` builder, for boot and boundary alike; H671 and H673: \`publish()\` re-reads the personas after the clock CAS, and the staged-route budget limit above is now on H673's own row. The 16 other needs_review rows on main (H060, H061, H068, H071, H104, H108, H130, H135, H139, H398, H477, H510, H523, H683 from #1188's edits to \`orchestrator.py\`, \`web.py\` and \`telegram.py\`; H288 and H684 from #1187's \`heartbeat.py\` and \`docs/ARCHITECTURE.md\`) are main's own drift, not this branch's, and are left untouched here; #1187's five-line comment in \`orchestrator.py\` re-drifted the nine rows above once more, and they were re-read against it and re-stamped. Fixed image estimates remain incomplete. For Gemini streams, usage-only final frames, absent terminal-local counts, unknown terminal semantics and ambiguous multi-candidate streams deliberately remain unreported. Synthesis/compression/background model calls are deliberately outside conversational usage attribution. Cache discounts/write premiums and undocumented vendor-specific usage mappings are not modeled by the new totals-only adapters. No live provider or billing proof. Responses accounting is limited to supported API-key GPT-4.1 and exact xAI Grok4.5/4.6 dialects, not Codex subscription usage or general OpenAI reasoning-model replay. Cache counts do not establish live discounts, prices or physical context occupancy. Actual specialist planning applies to the existing opt-in shared-compression path; disabled/unmanaged callers retain their existing behavior. Unknown capacity remains a conservative planning estimate, not verified provider metadata. Counter availability describes only the parsed response under its adapter's accounting contract, not physical retries, failed requests with no observation, auxiliary work or a complete turn bill. Any producers outside the explicitly flagged Gemini, Anthropic, Ollama, LM Studio, declared OpenAI-compatible and shared OpenAI/xAI Responses mappings retain legacy availability behavior. Bounds use the existing token estimator and selected effective/estimated window, not exact provider wire tokenization. Unmanaged calls, synthesis and later tool turns retain their separate behavior. Anthropic incomplete prompt partitions no longer create or replace anchors, but retained older anchors describe only their original covered prefix under existing freshness rules. They do not remeasure changed system, tool or persona material. Other raw provider mappings retain legacy prompt eligibility, including Gemini with ambiguous or unmapped tool-use prompt categories. Counter availability does not establish exact context occupancy. Gemini positive tool-use prompt counts remain outside the numeric mapping and estimated floors. Missing thoughts or unknown tool-use categories may make a valid accepted response incomplete for accounting; malformed core terminal counters still produce no stream event. The mapped positive prompt anchor is independent of accounting availability, not proof of exact full occupancy. Shared Responses accounting is deliberately conservative for unknown or positive cache-write details, including ordinary xAI payloads that omit that field. Inclusive prompt totals stay known; no absent-field zero, separate write pricing or universal input-plus-output invoice equation is asserted. The marker covers received observations, not every chargeable request or vendor-specific fee. Declining an initial incomplete Anthropic prompt leaves the existing estimate fallback, not a new complete measurement. The prompt marker is separate from physical-window occupancy, per-vendor internal tool-use context and the final managed dispatch guard; it does not change compaction algorithms or imply an over-window dispatch was demonstrated. Independent #1233 remaining limits: A model with no num_ctx parameter and no operator configuration remains unresolved (server environment/running context is not probed). Fixed image estimates remain incomplete. Gemini usage-only final frames, absent terminal-local counts, unknown terminal semantics and ambiguous multi-candidate streams deliberately remain unreported. Synthesis/compression/background model calls are deliberately outside conversational usage attribution. Cache discounts/write premiums and undocumented vendor-specific usage mappings are not modeled by the new totals-only adapters. No live provider or billing proof. Responses accounting is limited to supported API-key GPT-4.1 and exact xAI Grok4.5/4.6 dialects, not Codex subscription usage or general OpenAI reasoning-model replay. Cache counts do not establish live discounts, prices or physical context occupancy. Actual specialist planning applies to the existing opt-in shared-compression path; disabled/unmanaged callers retain their existing behavior. | <a id="h674"></a>H674 | Compression cannot stall the user: bounded holds, inactivity deadlines and derived thresholds | update | Echivalent | Reevaluat | Current e074fbc6 reread: H391 preflight whole-pass timeout is separate from the existing short summary hold and stream inactivity deadline. New durable micro publication preserves late-summary/source/clock ownership, and the reviewed stalled-retry cache fix retains a valid original prior without allowing an unsuccessful candidate to replace it. Strict-local summary routing, existing hold/idle notices and prior late-seeding semantics remain intact. A compaction summary no longer holds the owner's turn past a short bound, and a silent summarizer is cut. Hermes keeps two clocks: how long the summary may make the user wait, and how long the summarizer may go quiet. Nerva awaited the strict-local summarizer inline with neither. Its only limit was the httpx read timeout (120 s for Ollama), a total-duration wait on a non-streaming call, and nothing told the owner. (1) Bounded hold. ContextCompressor takes a gate (agents/core/context_compressor.py:327, used at :605). The orchestrator builds it per turn (_summary_gate, agents/core/orchestrator.py:4836, passed at :4514) around SummaryHold (agents/core/compaction_hold.py:149). SummaryHold.wait (:159) waits at most memory.compression_max_turn_hold_seconds for the LLM summary (settings_db.py:350; default 10 s, 0 = never wait, clamped 0..120 by hold_seconds, compaction_hold.py:64). One summary per session is written at a time: a turn that finds one still in flight neither waits on it again nor starts a second. Past the hold the turn goes on without the summary, and compress marks the result summary_deferred (context_compressor.py:650). compact (:422) then sends the turns verbatim, their old images dropped, when they still fit the window under the owner's memory.compression_max_tokens; otherwise it sends the deterministic digest. The summary keeps being written. When it lands it seeds this session's iterative-merge prior (_ctx_summary_cache), but only if no newer turn has replaced the prior this turn started from, and never through the compaction-clock CAS: publish commits only what the prompt was built from, and never writes the digest over the pending summary (orchestrator.py:5232). A turn cancelled while it waits (Stop, a client gone) still leaves its summary for the next turn. A summary that fails later seeds nothing and is logged by name. aclose stops what is still being written within the task budget (orchestrator.py:5982; SummaryHold.aclose, compaction_hold.py:198). (2) The owner is told. record_turn_notice (agents/core/turn_notices.py:35; a per-turn sink collected like turn_approvals, one notice per code) carries DEFERRED_NOTICE (compaction_hold.py:39) out as notices on /chat (ChatResponse.notices, agents/web.py:1193, TurnNotice :1118) and on every /chat/stream end event, the failed one included (:1490, :1497). The HUD shows each notice as a system line under the reply (frontend/src/turn-notices.ts, app.tsx:469). The hub log says the summary was deferred and, later, that it landed. (3) Inactivity deadline. The summarizer now streams (stream_summary, compaction_hold.py:89, called at agents/core/llm/auxiliary_text.py:186). It is cut after memory.compression_summary_idle_seconds with nothing received (settings_db.py:351; default 60 s, up to 600, no "off": idle_seconds, compaction_hold.py:72). Any chunk counts as life: a visible token, and a reasoning chunk that shows no text, through the new on_activity callback on the Ollama and LM Studio streams (agents/core/llm/base.py:797, :1022). A slow stream that keeps talking is never cut. A cut stream is cancelled and given CLOSE_GRACE (1 s) to close its HTTP response. A backend with no stream is awaited whole. A degraded reply ("⚠️ …", "\[backend error …\]") or an empty one is now a failure, and so the digest is used. Before, the non-streaming generate could hand an error text over as the summary. Tests: tests/test_h674_compaction_hold.py (52) covers both settings, the idle deadline (silent, slow-but-talking, token-only, thinking, degraded, no stream), the hold (in time, at the bound, single flight, zero, cancelled wait, late failure, failure within the hold, aclose), the compressor's deferral (digest, verbatim when it fits, owner's budget, covered with a prior), and the orchestrator: the turn going on at the hold, the late summary seeding the next turn, a newer prior never overwritten, no clock commit for the deferred summary, the idle setting reaching the summarizer, aclose. It also covers the notice on /chat and every stream end event, the collector unbound after /chat, and on_activity on both local streams. frontend src/test/turn-notices.test.ts covers the HUD. 72 mutants: 70 caught after nine survivors got cases. Two were equivalent. m23 (busy ignoring done()) is equivalent because the done callback always pops the flight first. The other was a redundant typeof check in the HUD helper, which was removed. The phase-2, H20.3 and compaction-policy suites pass unchanged. The AUD-7 and H677 end-event and reply pins gain the notices key. Stop revokes both registries, cancels every reserved fast-task set (five since the pending-input lane landed) and waits on their combined set for at most LANE_DRAIN_BUDGET before ordinary lane drain. | <a id="h683"></a>H683 | Chat replies stream, can be edited or deleted, and acknowledge receipt at ingest | update | Parțial | Reevaluat | (1) No edit or delete in the base contract: ChannelAdapter (agents/core/channels/base.py:14) still declares only abstract start/stop/send plus receive, and no adapter implements a delete operation for a sent reply (the only deleteMessage in agents/ is Telegram's TTL cleanup of ephemeral system notices at telegram.py:505, not a channel-contract method), so a sealed streamed preview cannot be removed and there is no base method that fails loudly for a channel that cannot edit; the fallback to a whole reply is silent. (2) Slack and Discord do not stream: both descriptors declare supports_edit=True (agents/core/channels/slack.py:105, agents/core/channels/discord.py:51) but neither adapter implements begin_stream or an edit call (Slack's send posts via chat_postMessage only, slack.py:609), and _begin_channel_draft refuses both (and ntfy) because a streamed draft would publish tokens before the channel.reply approval; streaming there needs an approval contract that covers output not yet generated. (3) No acknowledgement at ingest: Telegram sends a typing chat action only while reading an inbound attachment (telegram.py:1646) and a record_voice action before a spoken reply, so an ordinary text message gets no receipt signal until the first streamed token or the whole reply; Slack and Discord send none (the Slack Socket Mode envelope ack is a transport ack to Slack, not a signal the sender sees). [d1](../agents/core/channels/slack.py) [d2](../agents/core/channels/discord.py) [d3](../tests/test_workspace_channel_replies.py) |

CLI unhealthy or malformed responses exit nonzero; API is an admin-guarded GET. Inspection does not execute/read script bytes or secrets, mutate jobs, repair, restart or control the gateway. Direct-attempt recovery lives exclusively on registration/execution paths, never doctor. DB total_changes/state and diagnostic exclusion regressions cover this boundary. The exact frozen clause requires configured-path availability, not unsupported model workspace context or wider job options. Native scripts root and approved script-only workdir are the accepted mapping. Broader options and production-host observation remain independently open. | <a id="h687"></a>H687 | A recurring instruction runs once immediately, then on its cadence | update | Echivalent | Reevaluat | Built on this branch and reworked after two reviews. A recurring instruction now runs once when it is created, then on its cadence, with Hermes' split kept: - Hermes' /loop is an interval. LoopManager.set() starts it with next_due_at=now (hermes_cli/loops.py:466), and the reply says the first wakeup fires now. - A Hermes cron job waits for its first computed run. Nerva applies the /loop behaviour to its cron-style jobs where the schedule is an interval. Before this change, a new Nerva job always waited for its first slot, and every confirmation named only the schedule. Every creation surface goes through JobRunner.arm (agents/core/autonomy/jobs.py:1599): - POST /api/jobs (agents/core/routers/jobs.py:142); - the /remind slash command (agents/core/commands.py:322); - \`nerva jobs create\`, which posts to that route and prints the hub's confirmation (tests/test_nerva_cli.py:1571); - the HUD arm and JobCreateDialog notes (armNote, frontend/src/panels/jobs.tsx:38, used at frontend/src/panels/jobs.tsx:157 and frontend/src/panels/jobs.tsx:163). JobRunner.create is a thin wrapper around it (agents/core/autonomy/jobs.py:1597). first_run_policy (agents/core/autonomy/jobs.py:582) decides what runs before its first slot. Only an agent-instruction job does (ask, brief or task, or a script or monitor source), and only on an interval cadence. is_interval_cron (agents/core/autonomy/jobs.py:556) reads what the cron fires on, not how it is written: every hour with one minute or the minutes of a \`\*/N\`, or one minute in the hours of a \`\*/N\`, with no weekday, day or month restriction. So '0 0-23/2' and '0 0,12' count as '0 \*/2' and '0 \*/12', while two times of day ('0 9,21') and '\*/5 \*/2' (only in even hours) are calendar schedules. These wait for their first slot: - a calendar schedule (a 07:00 morning brief armed in the evening, a weekday job armed on Saturday); - a reminder; - a repeat-limited job, whose early run would spend one of its few attempts (critic note 15); - anything during quiet hours, whose output would be held and delivered after the next fresh run's; - anything whose first slot is near (first_run_margin, agents/core/autonomy/jobs.py:577): nearer than two minutes or than a quarter of the cadence (agents/core/autonomy/jobs.py:524-525), read from the real cron in the app's schedule timezone, the zone the job's trigger is registered with (slot_timing, agents/core/autonomy/jobs.py:1634; tests/test_job_first_run.py:520 sets the host scheduler to another zone to prove that one is not read). "every 12 hours" armed 45 minutes before its noon slot waits for it instead of running twice within the hour. first_run_decision (agents/core/autonomy/jobs.py:619) applies it at creation. A paused or disabled job never fires, and the create call's \`first_run\` (StrictBool, agents/core/routers/jobs.py:34; \`--first-run/--no-first-run\`, tests/test_job_first_run.py:363) overrides the policy either way. It is a creation-time choice, never a stored option: validate_options refuses it, so PATCH cannot store it and no rollback trips on it. The first run is a dispatch request drained by _fire_once (agents/core/autonomy/jobs.py:1747) under the shared job gate (agents/core/autonomy/jobs.py:1624; ORIGINS and the column at agents/core/autonomy/jobs_dispatch.py:12 and agents/core/autonomy/jobs_dispatch.py:40). Its origin is 'first_run' when the policy chose it and 'first_run_asked' when the create call asked for it. - The request is durable, so the drain checks a policy first run against first_run_policy again when it comes to run (first_run_due, agents/core/autonomy/jobs.py:1650; agents/core/autonomy/jobs_dispatch.py:214). By then the job may have been edited into a calendar schedule, a reminder or a repeat-limited job, quiet hours may have begun, or a scheduler that was down may have left its first slot near. The request is then cancelled and names the reason. An asked first run is not second-guessed. - The drain runs both with force=False (agents/core/autonomy/jobs_dispatch.py:223), so _fire_once applies the pause check (agents/core/autonomy/jobs.py:1761), the emergency stop (agents/core/autonomy/jobs.py:1767), option and action validation, the repeat reservation (now start_direct_run, agents/core/autonomy/jobs.py:1783; for scripts, agents/core/autonomy/jobs_scripts.py:144-146) and the quiet-hours hold on delivery (agents/core/autonomy/jobs.py:2108; for scripts, agents/core/autonomy/jobs_scripts.py:491-493). - Only the owner's own ▶ now runs a paused job. When ▶ now folds into a queued first run, it makes that request manual (agents/core/autonomy/jobs_dispatch.py:86). - Pausing cancels a not-yet-claimed first run of either origin (cancel_queued, agents/core/autonomy/jobs_dispatch.py:107, called at agents/core/autonomy/jobs.py:1719). - An edit that changes what runs (action or options) queues the first run again for the edited job, keeping its origin, instead of letting the claim's identity check drop it (agents/core/autonomy/jobs.py:1698; _requeue_first_run, agents/core/autonomy/jobs.py:1702). A rename or a new schedule leaves it queued. Either way a policy first run meets the policy again at the drain. If the queue refuses the new request, the edit is still saved and says why in the log. If the enqueue is refused at creation (the queue is at capacity, or the database is locked), the answer is still 201 with first_run null and 'first run not queued (…)', because the job is armed and a retry would duplicate it. POST /api/jobs returns the receipt as first_run, or null, plus one confirmation built by arm_confirmation (agents/core/autonomy/jobs.py:643): - 'first run now, then \<schedule\> (\<cron\>)', or 'first run queued, then …' with a note that nothing fires while the scheduler is not running (agents/core/autonomy/jobs.py:658); - '\<schedule\> (\<cron\>), on its cadence', with the quiet-hours or near-slot reason when that was the cause. /remind, the CLI and the HUD print it. Tests: - tests/test_job_first_run.py, 74 cases (41 before the second review). 28 of them fail on ccdd7161, with its fixture pointed at that commit's slot helper: - an interval ask job is queued and drained into one run before any slot (tests/test_job_first_run.py:109); - a calendar schedule waits (tests/test_job_first_run.py:123); - the emergency stop (tests/test_job_first_run.py:133); - pause cancels the first run, and one that slips past the pause is still skipped (tests/test_job_first_run.py:143, tests/test_job_first_run.py:155), an asked one too (tests/test_job_first_run.py:451); - ▶ now keeps its force (tests/test_job_first_run.py:164); - edits: one to the action runs the edited job (tests/test_job_first_run.py:176), one the policy would not fire drops it (tests/test_job_first_run.py:387), an asked one survives (tests/test_job_first_run.py:439), a rename leaves it alone (tests/test_job_first_run.py:473), and a refused re-queue still saves (tests/test_job_first_run.py:483); - at the drain: quiet hours that began (tests/test_job_first_run.py:402), a slot now near (tests/test_job_first_run.py:416), and an asked first run that runs anyway (tests/test_job_first_run.py:429); - first_run is a creation choice, never stored (tests/test_job_first_run.py:210); - a refused enqueue and a locked database (tests/test_job_first_run.py:229, tests/test_job_first_run.py:499); - quiet hours, the near slot, a long cadence near its slot and no scheduler (tests/test_job_first_run.py:242, tests/test_job_first_run.py:251, tests/test_job_first_run.py:462, tests/test_job_first_run.py:261); - an interval script job submits its first run (tests/test_job_first_run.py:273); - the interval table, the decision table and the slot timing on the real cron (tests/test_job_first_run.py:306, tests/test_job_first_run.py:339, tests/test_job_first_run.py:520); - both CLI flags (tests/test_job_first_run.py:353, tests/test_job_first_run.py:363). - tests/test_nerva_cli.py:1571 and tests/test_slash_commands.py:373. - frontend/src/test/jobs-first-run.test.ts (armNote). - tests/test_jobs_routes.py: a new reminder still sends nothing until /run, and the script job's /run is again a fresh manual request. Every guard added in the second review was mutated out one at a time, and a test failed each time. 656 job, dispatch, command, CLI and schedule tests pass. One-shot run_at jobs (H450) never take a first run, even when one is asked for: first_run_policy and first_run_decision answer "one-shot" (agents/core/autonomy/jobs.py:602, :607). The H450 row says they must stay out of the first run. A known pre-existing gap outside this row: parse_schedule drops a window or day qualifier after an interval ("every 30 minutes between 9 and 17" becomes '\*/30 \* \* \* \*'), so such a job runs all day and counts as an interval. Image-recovery collateral review (2026-10-02): changes to shared CLI/image-turn or HUD local-panel disclosure are outside this row's claimed symbols. | <a id="h688"></a>H688 | Config keys whose NAME contains a dot can be addressed | skip | Echivalent | Reevaluat | Final review at HEAD 57ed6db, branch codex/hermes-progress-20261010. The row is now equivalent to Hermes config-literal-dots for the CLI, which is the only place Nerva addresses a setting by a dotted name. The earlier assessment left three gaps: a json value could only be replaced whole, there was no unset, and no test pinned a dotted key name. All three are closed on this branch. What the code does now: - Name grammar. agents/core/settings_path.py:57-105 parses a setting name into segments. A backslash-escaped dot (\`\\.\`) or a double-quoted segment counts as one key and is never split (settings_path.py:66-99). - Greedy matching. Runs of plain segments are matched greedily against the keys that already exist at that level, longest first (settings_path.py:118-138). When more than one reading exists, the name is refused as ambiguous and the error spells out the quoted form of each reading (settings_path.py:133-137). - Category and key. resolve_setting takes the first segment as the category and matches the key greedily, so a declared key may itself contain dots (settings_path.py:141-156). - Reading, writing and removing inside a value. get_in, set_in and unset_in walk a json value with the same greedy step (settings_path.py:159-257). A list index must be ASCII digits (settings_path.py:36 and :171). - Phantom-sibling refusal. set_in refuses to create a plain key \`ui\` beside an existing dotted key \`ui.theme\`, which Hermes calls _phantom_sibling (settings_path.py:193-202, called at :225). Quoting or escaping the segment says the new key is wanted on purpose. - CLI wiring. agents/cli/nerva.py:1187-1206 resolves names for config get, set and unset; the unset verb is declared at agents/cli/nerva.py:261-264. \`config get\` also matches stored rows that nothing declares (nerva.py:1195-1199, passed stored=True at :1261). \`set\` and \`unset\` accept declared settings only (nerva.py:1280-1284). - Writes below a key. A path below a key goes through set_in or unset_in (nerva.py:1293-1305). The whole new value then passes the same validation, retention, model-selection guards and route-only refusals as any other write (nerva.py:1286-1317, the retention approval, selection guards and store write in _write_setting, agents/cli/nerva.py:1361-1422, which \`config edit\` shares). - Unset of a whole setting puts back its declared value (nerva.py:1302-1303). - An appearance write moves the device-sync revision (_stamped, nerva.py:1353-1358). - Docs. docs/INSTALL.md:134-135 shows the path, escape and quote spellings and \`config unset\`. Tests in tests/test_h688_config_paths.py: - greedy, escaped and quoted resolution of a dotted declared key (:50) - get, set and unset of a dotted key inside a value, behaving the same across all three (:68) - phantom-intermediate refusal (:82) - ambiguous and missing paths failing loudly (:94) - CLI round trip inside a json setting, including the phantom refusal and unset (:136) - whole-setting unset (:168) - a declared key whose name contains a dot, addressed plainly, escaped and quoted (:188) - an undeclared stored row is readable but not writable (:230) - non-ASCII digits are refused as list indexes (:261) - the appearance revision moves on a CLI write (:278) Review history: the r1 implementation went through review. That review raised three findings: \`config get\` had lost undeclared rows, non-ASCII digits were accepted as list indexes, and the docs example wrote a key nothing reads. r2 (commit bf34ed1) fixed all three with regression tests that failed before the fix. The row then passed two adversarial skeptics and was cherry-picked onto HEAD. Honest limits: - The dotted-key-name CLI test declares its key through a monkeypatched spec, because no shipped Nerva setting currently has a dot in its key name. - Path addressing exists only in the CLI. The HUD and HTTP settings routes still write whole values per category. Hermes's equivalent is also CLI-only. Test runs: the row's four test files were run twice with env -u TMPDIR, a fresh JARVIS_HOME, -o addopts="" and -p no:cacheprovider. The files were tests/test_h688_config_paths.py, tests/test_nerva_cli.py, tests/test_o26_p2_env_config.py and tests/test_orchestrator_bindings.py. Run 1 gave 227 passed in 39.36s and run 2 gave 227 passed in 42.88s. Nothing failed and nothing was flaky. | <a id="h694"></a>H694 | One canonical kill switch that every scope honors | keep | Echivalent | Reevaluat | Every hub on an install now obeys one kill switch, and no other code path bypasses it. This closes the gap where a hub running under $JARVIS_PROFILE ignored the default hub's ESTOP. \*\*The switch.\*\* \`paths.install_root()\` (agents/core/paths.py:177-191) returns the install's unprofiled root and ignores $JARVIS_PROFILE. \`profiles_root()\` (agents/core/paths.py:195-198) names the \`\<install root\>-profiles\` directory. \`data_root()\` builds each profile's root under it (agents/core/paths.py:201-207). The sentinel is \`install_root()/ESTOP\` (agents/core/estop.py:55-57), so \`engage()\` (agents/core/estop.py:120) writes the same file from any scope. \`check_paused()\` (agents/core/estop.py:181) is the gate used by the heartbeat (agents/core/heartbeat.py:489), the autonomy tick (agents/core/autonomy_coordinator.py:576) and the jobs runner (agents/core/autonomy/jobs.py:1755). It still fails safe: an OSError reports engaged (agents/core/estop.py:97-117). \*\*Legacy sentinels are one switch, not a hidden second one.\*\* - \`_legacy_sentinels()\` (agents/core/estop.py:60) lists \`\<install root\>-profiles/\*/ESTOP\`. - \`_fold_legacy()\` (agents/core/estop.py:75-94) moves the first one onto the canonical sentinel with \`os.replace\`, which keeps its body, and deletes the rest. A sentinel it cannot move stays where it is and still counts as engaged. - \`is_engaged()\` (agents/core/estop.py:97) and \`get_state()\` (agents/core/estop.py:155) both see legacy sentinels. - \`disengage()\` (agents/core/estop.py:137-152) removes the canonical sentinel and every legacy one. \*\*Forget and backup leave the shared switch alone.\*\* - ESTOP is on \`data_purge.KEEP_FILES\` (agents/core/data_purge.py:86). - \`create_backup\` leaves the root's ESTOP out of the archive (agents/core/backup.py:568-572; import at agents/core/backup.py:92). \*\*Tests\*\* (tests/test_estop.py): - The \`estop_home\` fixture patches only \`install_root\` (:26). - Profile tests: :131, :142, :147 and :159. - A legacy sentinel is folded into the canonical one (:183), is visible from the default hub and lifted by a resume there (:200), and a resume lifts several legacy sentinels at once (:217). - A forget keeps ESTOP (:230), and a backup never carries it (:247). - An unpatched integration test (:272) runs a real profiled \`HeartbeatScheduler\` and the ops estop state/resume routes. \*\*Red first and review fixes.\*\* With the new tests on the old code, 5 failed and 13 passed. The adversarial review led to three fixes: forget and backup keep ESTOP, legacy sentinels fold into the one switch, and the integration test was added. Both skeptics passed. \*\*Test results at HEAD e256d5d:\*\* - tests/test_estop.py: 18 passed. - Together with test_backup, test_data_purge, test_h689_install_identity, test_h689_shared_identity, test_h689b_profile_env and test_job_dispatch: 183 passed, 1 warning. The pre-restore rollback point is made by the same create_backup (agents/core/backup.py:1563-1565). The in-place restore extracts the archive over the root (agents/core/backup.py:1574, agents/core/backup.py:890-893) and afterwards removes only process marks and SQLite sidecars, never the ESTOP sentinel, so an engaged pause survives a restore. The ESTOP filter citation moved from line 411 to line 508 and the import from line 62 to line 87; the autonomy tick's check_paused moved to agents/core/autonomy_coordinator.py:576. tests/test_estop.py passes (18 tests, including the backup case at :247).
